They say that the most devoted of people to the Sunnah, Imam Ahmad, resorted to delegation in three places: the Black Stone, "The Black Stone is the right hand of God on earth" [narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq (8919) as a saying of Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, with the wording: "The corner, meaning the stone, is the right hand of God on earth, with which He shakes hands with His creation as a man shakes hands with his brother..."]; and "Indeed, I find the breath of God (*nafas Allah*) from the direction of Yemen" [narrated by al-Tabarani in *Musnad al-Shamiyyin* (1083) from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, with the wording: "And I find the breath of the Most Merciful from the direction of Yemen..."; and by Ahmad (10978) from him as well, with the wording: "And I find the breath of your Lord from the direction of Yemen..."]; and "The heart is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful" [narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2140) from the hadith of Anas, may God be pleased with him, with the wording: "Indeed the hearts are between two fingers of God's fingers; He turns them however He wills"]. They say he delegated. Is this statement correct?
* **Shaykh:** It is not correct at all. "The Black Stone is the right hand of God on earth" is never authentically attributed to the Messenger ﷺ, never. As we established in the book *al-Qawa'id al-Muthla* (The Best Principles), all the examples you mentioned are there, and the refutation of them is there too.
* **Student:** (...).
* **Shaykh:** The best method. But if they have authority, meaning that if you debate them openly you would be in danger, then leave that debate. However, you may speak in private gatherings, or in gatherings where they are not present, presenting the doctrine and explaining its falsehood. Even if the only benefit of this presentation were to make the common people doubt these people, it would be sufficient. Shaking belief and creating doubt about it is extremely important. Do you understand? For example, if you see people upon falsehood and you explain the truth, then even if the only benefit is that they doubt the matter, even among their leaders, and doubt their own statements, you have achieved something, since you have brought the truth and clarified it. This is why I heard about some propagators of Christianity, may God curse them and damn them until the Day of Resurrection, that he said to his people: "O our people, you will never convert a Muslim to Christianity; that is impossible, because our present Christianity, everyone knows, is a fable and has no basis. But it is enough for you to make the Muslim doubt his religion."
Look at the cunning ones: it is enough for you to make the Muslim doubt his religion. Let him merely doubt, and if he doubts, does he become a disbeliever or not? Yes. If a person doubts what must be believed, he is a disbeliever. What must be believed must be held with certainty. So observe their methods. We, praise be to God, have methods stronger than theirs. But the point is that when a person sees this world, he may fear. The bravery of Khalid ibn al-Walid and Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib seems to exist only in a few people.
This has begun before we knew it. Whoever catches up one rak'ah of the prayer [is considered to have caught the prayer].
* **Student:** Shaykh, may God forgive you, the Ash'aris' preachers make people love their school of thought by presenting their scholars, such as Ibn Hajar, al-Nawawi, Izz ibn 'Abd al-Salam, and so on.
* **Shaykh:** This is easy. When they say Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi: as for Ibn Hajar, may God have mercy on him, my view is that he was not on the path of al-Ash'ari. The man was inconsistent. Sometimes he speaks words that are one hundred percent the words of the People of the Sunnah, and sometimes he transmits the statements of the Ash'aris. Sometimes he quotes Shaykh al-Islam approvingly. As for al-Nawawi, may God have mercy on him, he was upon the Ash'ari school in everything I have read of his books. But if they confront us with so-and-so and so-and-so, we say: Do you know the truth by men, or men by the truth? If they say, "We know the truth by men," we say: We have Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn al-Qayyim, Imam Ahmad, and other great scholars. These stand against those. Then we have something above all of them: the Companions, may God be pleased with them. Bring us one single piece of evidence supporting the Ash'ari school. He says: ﴿istawa﴾ means *istawla* (to seize dominion). None of them said that *istawa* means *istawla*. All of them said *istawa* means *'alā* (to be high above). From where do we know this? We know it because they recited the Qur'an and understood its meaning, and no statement has come from any of them about diverting the wording from its apparent meaning. Do you understand? Praise be to God, the truth is clear.
So if someone said to us: The Companions unanimously agreed that the meaning of God's saying, ﴿He istawa upon the Throne﴾, is that He rose above it, they unanimously agreed. Could anyone dispute this and say, "They did not agree"? That is impossible, because we know that the Companions recited the Qur'an and interpreted its meaning according to the Arabic language, and in all of its usages in the Arabic language, when *istawa* is followed by *'alā* (on), the meaning intended is height.
God, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Shura 11], to its end.

* From the benefits of this verse: God, exalted is He, is the One who created the heavens and the earth originally, without any prior model.
* And from its benefits: the perfection of God's power, blessed and exalted, because no one but God can have power over these great heavens. Moreover, He created them in six days, which are detailed in Surah Fussilat.
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the heavens are plural. How many are they? Seven, and the earth is seven as well, but from other verses than this one.
* And from its benefits: the wisdom and mercy of God, mighty and majestic, in that He made for us mates from among ourselves. This is wisdom, since they are from ourselves, and mercy, since He made for us spouses with whom we enjoy ourselves on one hand, and through whom we grow and increase on the other.
* And also from the benefits of this noble verse: God's mercy toward us, in that He made for us mates from the livestock, because this is undoubtedly for our benefit.
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: that God, glorified and exalted, multiplies, spreads, and increases the children of Adam and the livestock He created for them through mating, by His saying: ﴿He multiplies you therein﴾ [al-Shura 11].
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the refutation of the polytheists who set up another god with God, since He says: ﴿There is nothing like Him﴾. He, glorified and exalted, has no like, neither in creation, nor in attributes, nor in anything else.
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the refutation of the People of Likening (*ahl al-tamthil*) in His saying: ﴿There is nothing like Him﴾.
* And from its benefits: the affirmation of two of God's names, *al-Samī'* (the All-Hearing) and *al-Baṣīr* (the All-Seeing).
* And from the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of hearing and sight as attributes of God, mighty and majestic, because *al-Samī'* derives from hearing (*al-sam'*), and *al-Baṣīr* derives from sight (*al-baṣar*).

Here is a principle we point out: every name of God necessarily includes two things. The first: the affirmation that it is one of God's names. The second: the affirmation of the attribute it indicates. So whoever says, "God is All-Hearing but without hearing," has not believed in the name, because you must believe in the attribute it indicates, otherwise you have not believed in it. Also, the affirmation that this attribute transitively extends to other things, if it is transitive. For example, *al-Samī'*: we believe God has it among His names, and that hearing is among His attributes, and we believe in an additional matter, that He hears everything. This is why the scholars said: if the name is intransitive, belief in it is not complete except through two things: the first, affirming it is one of God's names; the second, affirming the attribute it indicates. If it is transitive, then belief in it requires three matters: the first, affirming that it is a name of God; the second, affirming the attribute it indicates; and the third, affirming that this attribute extends to what it relates to, meaning that hearing relates to everything heard, and sight to everything seen.

Also, they say that names contain three kinds of signification: the signification of correspondence (*dalālat al-muṭābaqah*), the signification of inclusion (*dalālat al-tadammun*), and the signification of implication (*dalālat al-iltizām*); or, if you prefer, *dalālat al-luzūm*. So a name's signification of the essence alone is a signification of inclusion, its signification of the attribute alone is a signification of inclusion, and its signification of both together is a signification of correspondence. And the name's signification of a necessary meaning that follows from it is a signification of implication. These are important principles. How many are the significations?

* **Student:** Three.
* **Shaykh:** Three: correspondence, inclusion, and implication. So the name's signification of the essence alone?
* **Student:** Inclusion.
* **Shaykh:** And of the attribute alone?
* **Student:** Inclusion.
* **Shaykh:** And of both?
* **Students:** Correspondence.
* **Shaykh:** Correspondence. And of a necessary matter? Implication.

Let us give an example: *al-Khāliq* (the Creator). Among God's names is *al-Khāliq*. Its signification of the essence alone is inclusion, its signification of the attribute of creating alone is also inclusion, and its signification of both together is correspondence.

So we have understood that the signification of a word for its whole meaning is correspondence, for part of its meaning is inclusion, and for an external necessary matter that follows from it is implication. For example, the example we have now still stands: *al-Khāliq* signifies the attribute of creating, and the Creator Himself, and it also signifies something necessary to creating: power. For whoever is not powerful cannot create, and whoever is not knowing cannot create. So the signification of *al-Khāliq* on knowledge and power is a signification of implication.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the refutation of the People of Negation (*ahl al-ta'til*) in His saying: ﴿and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾.

We have mentioned *al-Samī'*. From the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of *al-Samī'* as a name of God, of *al-Baṣīr* as a name of God, the affirmation of sight as an attribute of God, and the affirmation of hearing as an attribute of God.

If someone asks: which is broader, the attribute or the name? The answer: the attribute is broader, because God is described by what He is not named by. But everything He is named by includes an attribute. Do you understand? Understand the principle first, then the example will come. Which is broader, the attributes or the names? The attributes. The reason is that every name includes an attribute, and so names and attributes are coextensive in this sense. But there are attributes by which God cannot be named. So the attribute is broader. Do we not say, "God expressed such-and-such," and "God spoke about such-and-such"? Yet we do not name God as "speaker" (*mutahaddith*), nor as "expresser" (*mu'abbir*). Why? Because the description is broader than the name. This is also an important benefit, contrary to what they say, that names do not include attributes.

* **Student:** Yes.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 42, verse 12:

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Shura 12]. ﴿To Him﴾ means: to Allah alone. We say "alone" because placing the predicate first (taqdim al-khabar) indicates restriction (hasr). Indeed, the rule is broader than this: placing what should be postponed indicates restriction. So if you say, "Zaydan akramtu" (Zayd I honored), it means you did not honor anyone else, because you have placed the object first. Thus we say, "lahu" (to Him), meaning: not to other than Him.

﴿The keys of the heavens and the earth﴾. The commentator said: (i.e., the keys of their treasuries). So he took maqalid to mean keys (mafatih). However, from the standpoint of the Arabic language, this does not fit the derivation, because maqalid is derived from qilada (a necklace/collar). The meaning is that the reins of all affairs in the heavens and the earth are in the hand of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, just as you say "qiladat al-ba'ir" (the camel's halter), because you lead it by it.

So the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that the commentator, may Allah have mercy on him, interpreted it in a way that contradicts the apparent sense. But some people say that maqalid is a foreign word that has been Arabicized, and that miqlad means key. But this is undoubtedly a weak view, because, O our brothers, one must not resort to Arabicization except out of necessity. That is, one cannot simply say, "This word originally is Persian, originally Roman, originally such-and-such, and was Arabicized." It is not permissible to turn to this except in cases of necessity, because Allah the Exalted made the Qur'an in Arabic. So if we say of a word that has been Arabicized and whose origin is non-Arabic, this contradicts the apparent sense of the Qur'an. But if we are compelled to this, in that we find no root for the word in the language, then we say it is Arabicized. Maqalid has a root: it is derived from the necklace by which the camel is led. So the meaning of maqalid is: the reins of affairs in the heavens and the earth belong to Him alone.

As for the author, may Allah have mercy on him, he said: (the keys of their treasuries, of rain, plants and other things).

﴿He extends provision to whom He wills﴾ [al-Shura 12]. ﴿Extends﴾ means widens, and ﴿restricts﴾ means narrows. Extension and restriction are a test and a trial, because among people there is one whom only poverty suits, and among people there is one whom only abundance suits. In the sacred hadith: "Among My servants is one whom, if I made him rich, wealth would corrupt him, and among My servants is one whom, if I made him poor, poverty would corrupt him."[[Al-Bayhaqi narrated in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat (231) from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, from Jibril (peace be upon him), from his Lord, Blessed and Exalted, and he related the hadith, in which it says: "Among My believing servants is one for whom only wealth is suitable; if I made him poor, it would corrupt him. And among My believing servants is one whose faith is not made right except by poverty; if I extended provision to him, that would corrupt him..."]]

﴿Indeed He is Knowing of all things﴾. The commentator says: (﴿He extends provision﴾ - and provision here means giving - widens it, ﴿to whom He wills﴾ as a test, ﴿and restricts it﴾ narrows it for whom He wills as a trial), as a test whether he will be grateful or not grateful, as a trial whether he will be patient or not patient.

﴿Indeed He is Knowing of all things﴾: He knows everything. So He knows that extension is better for this one, and restriction is better for that one.

* In this verse there are benefits, among them: that the reins of affairs belong to Allah alone in the heavens and the earth. He is the one who manages affairs and alternates the days among people, and turns circumstances over. How many a man becomes a disbeliever in the morning and a believer by evening, and how many a person becomes a believer in the morning and a disbeliever by evening, as the Prophet ﷺ informed about the trials at the end of time: that a person will become a disbeliever in the evening and a believer in the morning, or a believer in the morning and a disbeliever in the evening.[[Muslim narrated (118/186) from Abu Hurayah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Hasten to good deeds before trials like pieces of the dark night, when a man will be a believer in the morning and a disbeliever in the evening, or a believer in the evening and a disbeliever in the morning, selling his religion for a trifle of worldly goods."]]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whose hand is the extending and restricting of provision in? It is in the hand of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Does it follow from this that we should not take the means? No; for that would be a weakness in reliance (tawakkul) if one does not take the means. Take the means and rely on the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that we should not seek provision except from Allah, because He is the one who extends or restricts provision.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of Allah's will, from His saying: ﴿to whom He wills﴾.

If someone asks: is this will (mashi'a) free of wisdom or connected with wisdom?

The answer: the second, undoubtedly. That is, Allah's giving or withholding is not merely that He wished; rather, it must be for a wisdom. Fix this rule in your mind: every matter that Allah has linked to His will is necessarily connected with wisdom. He cannot do anything in vain, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play﴾ [al-Dukhan 38], and the Exalted said: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun 115]. So whenever something passes you that is linked to the will, know that it follows the wisdom of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. And recite the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way. And you will not will except that Allah wills﴾ [al-Insan 29-30], followed by: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Insan 30], meaning: His will is connected with knowledge and wisdom.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of the comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge, from His saying: ﴿Indeed He is Knowing of all things﴾. Of all things, existent or non-existent?

* Students: Both.

* The Shaykh: Both. Of all things, necessary existence, possible existence, or impossible existence?

* Students: All things.

* The Shaykh: All things? Even the impossible?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: He knows even the impossible; He knows it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya' 22]. Is it possible that there be gods in them other than Allah? It is not possible. Yet the Mighty and Majestic knows that if that were so, the heavens and the earth would be corrupted. Therefore we say: the knowledge of Allah the Exalted relates to everything: to the necessary, such as His knowledge of Himself; to the impossible, such as His knowledge of the corruption of the heavens and the earth were there gods other than Allah in them; to the possible, such as His knowledge of creatures. So the knowledge of Allah relates to everything, whether necessary, impossible, or possible.

Here is a warning about an error common among people: if a thing is small, they say, "This is basit" (simple/plain). This is wrong, because basf in the language means widening and multiplying. So do not say "hadha basit"; say "hadha yasir" (this is slight) or "hadha qalil" (this is little). If it is in terms of quality, say yasir; if it is in terms of number, say qalil.

We ask Allah the Exalted to take charge of us and you with His mercy, and to grant us and you success in what He loves and is pleased with.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion that which He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We have revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus, saying: Establish the religion and do not be divided therein.﴾ [Ash-Shura 13] and so on to the end.

﴿He has prescribed for you﴾: the address is to this Ummah, and all praise is due to Allah. The meaning of ﴿He has prescribed for you﴾ is that He legislated for you and established for you a sharia (a divine law), which is ﴿that which He enjoined upon Noah﴾. The commentator (al-Sharih) said: "[Noah] is the first of the prophets of the sharia," and Ibn 'Uthaymin, may Allah have mercy on him, was lax in this. The correct statement is that he is the first of the messengers of the sharia, because the authentic hadith says: "The people on the Day of Resurrection will come to Noah to intercede for them, and they will say to him: 'You are the first messenger Allah sent.'"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4476) and Muslim (193 / 322), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik. The wording of al-Bukhari, from Anas radiyallahu 'anhu, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The believers will gather on the Day of Resurrection and say: 'If only we could seek intercession with our Lord.' So they will come to Adam and say: 'You are the father of mankind. Allah created you with His own hand, commanded His angels to prostrate to you, and taught you the names of all things. Intercede for us with your Lord, so that He may relieve us from this place.' He will say: 'I am not in that position,' and he will mention his sin and be ashamed. 'Go to Noah, for he was the first messenger Allah sent to the people of the earth.' They will come to him and he will say: 'I am not in that position,' and he will mention his request of his Lord about which he had no knowledge, and be ashamed. He will say: 'Go to the Friend of the Most Merciful...'"]]

Because the messenger is more specific than the prophet, and one should not move from the more specific to the more general, the correct statement is: he is the first of the messengers of the sharia. As for the first of the prophets of the sharia, he is Adam, peace be upon him: a prophet who was spoken to by Allah, but not a messenger. The wisdom behind his not being a messenger is that people had not yet differed. Allah sent the messengers to judge between people concerning what they differed about, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Mankind was one community; then Allah sent prophets as bearers of good news and warners, and sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between the people concerning that over which they differed﴾ [Al-Baqarah 213]. But in the era of Adam there was no disagreement: the number was small, and there were no temptations or things that would cause people to differ. Therefore Adam worshipped Allah by the sharia that He had legislated for them.

His descendants followed him. When they multiplied, spread out and differed, the need, indeed the necessity, for messengers arose. So the better statement is: he is the first of the messengers of the sharia. Why? Because the first of the prophets of the sharia is Adam.

﴿and that which We have revealed to you﴾ [Ash-Shura 13]: meaning, He prescribed for you that which We revealed to you. ﴿and that which We have revealed to you﴾ is conjoined to ﴿that which﴾ in His saying ﴿that which He enjoined upon Noah﴾. The wasiyyah (enjoinment) is a binding covenant concerning a matter that is of concern, and it is called a wasiyyah. ﴿and that which We have revealed to you﴾ is the Qur'an. ﴿and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus﴾ [Ash-Shura 13]. Allahu Akbar! Allah mentioned the first of the prophets who are messengers and the last of them, then mentioned what lies between them, so that He, glorified and exalted, might gather the two ends and the middle. Who is the first of these noble messengers? Noah. And the last of them is Muhammad, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and upon them. These five are the messengers of firm resolve (ulu al-azm), as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So be patient as the messengers of firm resolve were patient﴾ [Al-Ahqaf 35]. They are mentioned in the Qur'an in two places. This is the first.

The second is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus﴾ [Al-Ahzab 7]. This verse is in Surat al-Ahzab.

﴿and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus, saying: Establish the religion﴾ [Ash-Shura 13]. The ﴿that﴾ here is explanatory, meaning "namely" (i.e.); therefore it governs nothing, since it is merely for explanation and clarification. ﴿Establish the religion and do not be divided therein﴾ [Ash-Shura 13]. ﴿Establish the religion﴾ means: bring it upright, not deviating.

What is the upright religion? It is the religion that Allah, mighty and majestic, legislated. So it is obligatory upon us to establish the religion as Allah, mighty and majestic, established it: we neither exceed in it nor fall short of it. For this reason, people in the religion of Allah were in three categories: a category that exaggerated, a category that fell short, and a category that moderated. What are we commanded in? Moderation: ﴿that you establish the religion﴾, neither exceeding it nor falling short of it. Therefore peoples perished, some of them through falling short and some through exceeding. Which is more dangerous? Exceeding, which is exaggeration (ghuluw). The Prophet ﷺ said: "Only exaggeration destroyed those before you."[[Recorded by al-Nasa'i (3057) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas radiyallahu 'anhuma.]] Because the exaggerator believes that this is the religion, he hardly ever abandons it, whereas the one who falls short admits that he is falling short, so perhaps one day he will take account of himself and complete it. Thus exaggeration is more dangerous. For this reason you find that the worst of the innovations of the innovators is exaggeration. The Rafidah, for example, exaggerated regarding the Family of the House and transgressed the limit; and those who deified the Messenger, peace be upon him, whom they believe to be greater than the God, exaggerated regarding the Messenger and perished; and the extremists in religion who want people to be upright in religion and not to commit even a major sin, exaggerating, like the Kharijites. In sum, if you reflect on innovations, you will find that exaggeration in them is the most harmful to a person, because the exaggerator believes that what he is upon is religion, while the one who falls short knows that he is falling short, and perhaps he will become upright afterwards.

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein.﴾ The word "religion" (din) is used with two meanings:
The first meaning: recompense (jaza').
The second meaning: action ('amal). That is, it is used for action and for recompense. Among its use for action is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾ [Al-Kafirun 6], meaning: for you is your action and for me is my action, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they deny you, say: For me is my action and for you is your action﴾ [Yunus 41]. Among its use for recompense is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Religion is? Then what will make you know what the Day of Religion is?﴾ [Al-Infitar 17, 18]. And what we recite in every prayer: ﴿Master of the Day of Religion﴾ [Al-Fatihah 4]. Which of the two meanings is intended? Recompense. Here, in ﴿that you establish the religion﴾, what is meant? Action. ﴿that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein﴾ means: do not be divided in your religion, becoming factions. So Allah, mighty and majestic, forbade division in the religion, and this entails the obligation of unity upon it, because a prohibition of a thing is a command to its opposite when that thing has no other opposite. Then it is obligatory upon the Muslims to unite in the religion of Allah and not to be divided in it.

As for matters over which scholars differ in opinions, the goal of them all is one for whoever has a sound intention, because each of the disputants only seeks to reach the truth, but they differ in the path. And when the goal is one, namely reaching the truth, it is not permissible to make this difference a cause of division in direction. This is absolutely not permitted; rather unity and togetherness are obligatory even with a difference of opinions. For this reason the noble, outstanding Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, differed in many important matters, yet their hearts were united. But when the difference reached the point of dividing hearts, there occurred what occurred of strife between 'Ali, Mu'awiyah, 'A'ishah, al-Zubayr and the like.

In our present time there is no doubt that people differ: some tend toward a political direction, some toward a Sufi direction, and some are moderate; many differences. So it is obligatory upon us to defuse this difference, and to be one community, so that we do not divide and thereby fail, because Allah says: ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength departs﴾ [Al-Anfal 46]. That is, let there be no worth for you. ﴿And be patient; indeed Allah is with the patient﴾ [Al-Anfal 46].

Therefore we now find, with great regret, that what is called the Islamic awakening has been afflicted by this calamity: the religious people themselves slander one another, mislead one another, declare one another innovators, and perhaps declare one another disbelievers. That awakening was lost, and those who were meant to be a party against the enemies of Allah and a force against the enemies of Allah became a force against themselves and factions against themselves. This is what the enemy would spend his most precious resources to achieve, and it has been achieved for him for free. So it is obligatory upon us to remove these differences, leave them aside, and abandon what many people fill their gatherings with: insulting so-and-so, disparaging so-and-so, or exaggerating about so-and-so, because this wastes time, breeds hatred, and benefits nothing but harms. What business do we have with so-and-so? If he is dead, he has faced his reckoning; if he is alive, we hope he becomes upright. As for making our greatest concern this talk which brings the community nothing but evil. For this reason Allah, mighty and majestic, forbids division in several verses, as in this verse: ﴿that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein.﴾

If you and your companion differ over one of the opinions which is open to ijtihad (independent reasoning), then it is obligatory that you believe your companion will not oppose you. Why? Because he has taken the path you take: he exercised ijtihad and said, "This is the correct view," and you exercised ijtihad and said, "This is the correct view." So what is the aim of each of you? Reaching the truth. Your ijtihad cannot be a proof against him, nor his ijtihad a proof against you. Then in reality we are in agreement, even if he opposes me: I believe he agrees with me, because we all intend the truth and do not want to oppose the truth. But unfortunately, now some people take this difference which is a matter of ijtihad and make it a ladder to division and slander.

Some years ago at Mina, two African groups were present, each cursing and declaring the other a disbeliever. They came to the leader of the da'wah of which I am one of the members, coming to him very, very hostile, at Mina, in the days of Hajj, in a sacred month, in a sacred land. He, may Allah reward him well, came to me with them, and said: "What is the matter?" They said: "These are disbelievers; these have turned away from the Sunnah of the Messenger ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me.'"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5063) and Muslim (1401/5), from the hadith of Anas radiyallahu 'anhu.]]

We disavow them. A long, strange discussion. And what was the difference? One of the two groups says: when he stands to pray, he places the right hand over the left, and the other group says: when he stands to pray, he lets his hands hang. The matter is not a difference in creed; the matter is a difference over one of the Sunnahs of prayer, which is a matter of ijtihad. Each one says to the other that he is a disbeliever, because he turned away from the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."

Look at the calamity! Now the youth's disagreement has become about another matter: about individuals. They make a person the target. "What do you say about so-and-so?" If he says, "By Allah, so-and-so is good, beloved, and among the best servants of Allah," his heart expands, as if he had been given Paradise. And if it is said, "By Allah, this man has a deviation in his path, a person with such-and-such and such-and-such," he is constricted, his heart tightens, and he abandons his companion. This is a mistake, O brothers.

People, men: if they err, ask Allah to pardon their error; for they are Muslims, whatever they are, and they do not leave Islam. And if they are right, take their correct view and praise them for it, and do not take their error. But to make them a measure of loyalty and disavowal is a grave mistake. Therefore I call upon our brothers from the Saudis and others to abandon this path and keep away from it, and to believe that we are brothers, and that each of us will be recompensed for his deeds, and not to make this a cause of division, because Allah has forbidden us, and we know with certainty that Allah forbids us only from what is harmful to us. So here He says: ﴿that you establish the religion﴾, meaning not exaggerating in it nor falling short, ﴿and do not be divided therein﴾, be united upon it.

﴿Hard upon the polytheists is that to which you call them﴾ [Ash-Shura 13]. ﴿Hard﴾ means: great and grievous for them.
﴿upon the polytheists﴾ means: those who associate partners with Allah.
﴿that to which you call them﴾: what is it? Tawhid (monotheism). For what is hardest for the polytheist is tawhid; the greatest thing for him is tawhid; that is, the greatest thing that burdens him is tawhid. For this reason they said of the Messenger ﷺ: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing!﴾ [Sad 5]. ﴿And the chiefs among them went forth, saying: Walk on, and be steadfast for your gods; indeed this is a thing that is intended﴾ [Sad 6]. Look how they forced themselves to be steadfast in polytheism, may Allah protect us, and they said of tawhid: ﴿Indeed this is a strange thing!﴾, meaning very wondrous. What, in truth, is the strange thing? Their associating others with Allah, mighty and majestic, whom they themselves acknowledge as their Creator, with no creator besides Him. From here we derive that tawhid is grievous for the polytheists.

I say to you: if tawhid is grievous for them, they must necessarily take every means to prevent this tawhid from standing and spreading, is that not so? Everything great to you, you must resist. So they are now at war against tawhid and its people. For this reason you now hear of the schemes of the Christians, regarding their religion in which they are in error and which opposes reason and the senses: you find them broadcasting powerful radio programmes without interference, broadcast at times suitable for calling to the religion they follow. I do not say: to the religion of the Messiah, for the Messiah is innocent of them, but to the religion they are upon.

You find some of the people of innovation find it very hard that someone calls to the Sunnah; they fight against whoever calls to the Sunnah, and they defame his reputation, because it is great upon them. So here He says: ﴿Hard upon the polytheists is that to which you call them. Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns penitently﴾ [Ash-Shura 13].

He says: ﴿Allah chooses for Himself﴾: ﴿chooses﴾ means selects and elects. His saying ﴿to Himself﴾: the author (may Allah have mercy on him) referred the pronoun back to tawhid, but there is a stronger possibility than what he said, which is that the pronoun refers to Allah, mighty and majestic: that is, Allah chooses unto Himself whom He wills, and guides unto Himself whoever turns penitently. This is better than what the author adopted. Allah, exalted is He, chooses unto Himself whom He wills, and rejects others; the first He guides to His straight path, and the others He misguides, because they are the ones who took the cause: ﴿Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills﴾. We ask Allah to make us and you among those whom He chose for Himself.

It has been mentioned to us recently that everything Allah attached to His will is accompanied by wisdom: He wills nothing, whether bringing into existence, annihilating, or changing, except for a wisdom.

﴿and guides to Himself whoever turns penitently﴾: that is, whoever turns toward His obedience. The commentator says: "turns toward His obedience." So He guides him to Himself. It has been established from the Prophet ﷺ, in what he related from his Lord, that Allah, blessed and exalted, said: "My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him." That is, the obligatory acts are more beloved to Allah than the voluntary acts: "And My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him; and when I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks."[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (6502) with his chain from Abu Hurayrah, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah said: Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him; and when I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks."]]

Likewise, the Blessed and Exalted said in the Hadith Qudsi: "Whoever draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; and whoever draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7405) and Muslim (2675/2) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), and its wording is: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs. And if he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; and if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running.'"]]. "And whoever turns in repentance to Allah, Allah guides him to Himself, helps him, and makes him steadfast."

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the religion's legislation belongs to Allah alone. For this reason Allah condemned those who legislate for their peoples a religion that Allah did not permit, as He said: ﴿They have prescribed for them in religion what Allah did not permit﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:21].

* Among its benefits: the basic rule regarding acts of worship is prohibition, unless there is evidence. Therefore, if you see a person performing an act by which he draws near to Allah, do not object to it unless you establish evidence. This differs from non-worship matters, where the basic rule is permissibility (ḥill). Therefore, if you see a person doing something that is not an act of worship and you object to it, the burden of proof is on you.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the religions of the prophets are one, from Noah to Muhammad (ﷺ), because of His saying: ﴿He has prescribed for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We have revealed to you﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:13].

What, then, is the unity of the religions? The unity of the religions is what His saying the Exalted indicates: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut"﴾ [An-Nahl 16:36]. This is the general principle in all the messages: ﴿Worship Allah and avoid the taghut﴾.

As for the laws (sharāʾiʿ) and the methods (manāhij), each nation has what suits it, because of the saying of the Exalted: ﴿For each of you We have made a law (shir'ah) and a method (minhaj)﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 5:48]. For this reason we find that Allah made some restrictions upon certain peoples of the Children of Israel in one law and eased them in another law. ʿĪsā ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) said: ﴿And to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you﴾ [Ali 'Imran 3:50].

So the basic principle is the unity of the messages, and this basic principle is what is referred to in: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut"﴾ [An-Nahl 16:36].

As for the laws and methods, Allah the Mighty and Majestic legislates for each nation what suits it, even within one nation: He legislates for it what suits it at the beginning of its affairs and at the end of its affairs, like what was abrogated (mansukh) in this Islamic law.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the prophethood of Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, because of His saying: ﴿That which He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:13].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the care of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, for the laws, in that He made it a commandment (waṣiyyah), and a commandment is a pledge concerning something one cares about.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that this noble Quran is a revelation that Allah, Exalted, revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ), because of His saying: ﴿And that which We have revealed to you﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Quran comprises the entire law, because of His saying: ﴿And that which We have revealed to you﴾.

If someone says: "Is there in the law something that is not found in the Quran in detail?"

The answer: an indication to it is sufficient. That is, if we investigated whether the Quran contains evidence for the number of the prayers, the number of their units (rakʿahs), and their manner, the answer would be: No, it is not found there. But the fact that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commands us to obey the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to follow him is sufficient, because the Sunnah of the Messenger (peace be upon him) has been commanded to us along with everything it contains. Thus the whole law is found in the Quran, either by allusion and indication or by explicit statement.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the message of the Prophet (ﷺ), since He said: ﴿And that which We have revealed to you﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that all nations are commanded to establish the religion and not to be divided in it, because of His saying: ﴿That establish the religion and do not become divided therein﴾.

* Among its benefits: that division in the religion of Allah contradicts what Allah revealed to His Messenger (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family), and what He enjoined upon Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that what the Prophet (ﷺ) called to of monotheism was great and difficult for the polytheists, because of His saying: ﴿Difficult for the polytheists is that to which you call them﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:13].

* A consequence of this benefit: whenever monotheism is burdensome to the polytheists, they will certainly strive with all their efforts to nullify this monotheism, because every person, by the requirement of his nature, must strive to remove what is burdensome to him.

* A benefit that follows from this: beware of the plots of the polytheists.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to call both Muslims and non-Muslims to the religion of Allah, because of His saying: ﴿Difficult for the polytheists is that to which you call them﴾. This has been put into practice, and its evidence is in the situation of the Prophet (ﷺ): he would go out to other lands to call people to monotheism, as he went out to Ta'if. During the season of Hajj he would present himself to the tribes (peace be upon him). He would come to each tribe and call them, saying: "Is there anyone who will give me shelter (yuwini) until I convey the message of my Lord, for the Quraysh have prevented me from conveying the speech of my Lord?"[[Ahmad (14456) narrated from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained in Makkah for ten years, following the people in their dwellings at ʿUkāẓ and Majannah, and in the seasons at Mina, saying: "Who will shelter me? Who will support me until I convey the message of my Lord, and for him is Paradise?"]].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah may bestow upon some of His servants selection (ijtibā') and guidance, because of His saying: ﴿Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:13].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the will of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, concerning the action of the servant, because of His saying: ﴿He chooses for Himself whom He wills﴾. Thus it contains a refutation of whom? Of the Qadariyyah (those who deny divine decree), who say that a human being is independent in his deeds and that Allah's will has no role in his actions.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of guidance for everyone who turns in repentance (munīb). This guidance is other than turning in repentance. Turning in repentance is a prior guidance, but whenever a person turns to his Lord, his guidance increases.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, protects the one who turns in repentance from innovations (bid'ah) and violations, because of His saying: ﴿He guides to Himself﴾. This is undoubtedly opposed to innovations, since innovations contain no guidance to Allah; rather they are misguidance.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the encouragement to turn in repentance to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, since it is a cause of guidance.

* Among its benefits: a refutation of the Jabriyyah (those who deny human choice), because of His saying: ﴿Whoever turns in repentance﴾, where He attributed the action to the servant. The Jabriyyah do not attribute actions to the servant; they say that the servant acts without will or choice.

So in the verse there is a refutation of the Qadariyyah and a refutation of the Jabriyyah, and they are two innovating and extremist sects. So what is the middle position? The middle position is the one that says: a person is not compelled in his action, and he performs the act by his own choice, and he does not feel that anyone has forced him. Yet we know that this act which occurred from him occurs by the will of Allah and the decree of Allah, and a person cannot be independent in anything in the universe apart from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. If a person passes by a verse in which the prophets are mentioned, whether during the prayer or outside the prayer, is it prescribed for him to send blessings upon them?

* Shaykh: No, except for the Messenger (ﷺ).

* Student: Even outside the prayer?

* Shaykh: What do you mean, "even outside the prayer"? Yes, even outside the prayer, because we do not know that the Messenger (peace be upon him), when he passed by the messengers, greeted them.

* Student: I mean our Prophet (ﷺ), when he is mentioned during a recitation in the prayer?

* Shaykh: If he is mentioned to you, then send blessings upon him in whatever state you are in, except if you are in the toilet, then no (...).

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿He has prescribed for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:13]. We have previously mentioned that these noble messengers have a special title, which is what?

* Student: Ulu al-'Azm (the messengers of firm resolve) among the messengers.

* Shaykh: They are Ulu al-'Azm among the messengers. They are mentioned in the Quran in more than one place. In how many places?

* Student: In two places.

* Shaykh: In two places. The first is in Surat al-Ahzab. Recite it.

* Student: ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, the son of Mary﴾ [Al-Ahzab 33:7].

* Shaykh: And the second place is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿That establish the religion﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:13]. Its meaning is explanatory, but what is the meaning of ﴿That establish the religion﴾?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Do it upright, without crookedness in it. Crookedness in the religion occurs through two extremes?

* Student: First: innovation and innovations.

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: Exaggeration (ghuluww) in the religion, and the second: falling short in it and deficiency.

* Shaykh: Exaggeration and falling short. Which of them is more dangerous for a person?

* Student: Exaggeration, Shaykh.

* Shaykh: Exaggeration. Why?

* Student: Because exaggeration is an excess.

* Shaykh: Yes, this too is considered a deficiency in the religion.

* Student: That he believes, and is certain of what he is upon.

* Shaykh: He believes that he is upon the truth and that this is the religion, so he hardly abandons it. But the one who falls short knows that he is falling short, and tries to correct what he has neglected.

Then Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And they did not divide﴾, meaning: the people of the religions, regarding the religion, by some of them affirming monotheism and some of them disbelieving. ﴿Except after knowledge had come to them﴾, of monotheism, ﴿out of rivalry﴾ on the part of the disbelievers ﴿among themselves﴾).

﴿And they did not divide﴾. The author says: (meaning, the people of the religions). This is a good explanation. Allah, blessed and exalted, mentioned in Surah al-Bayyinah His saying: ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not divide except after clear evidence had come to them﴾ [al-Bayyinah 4]. So do we say that this general verse, ﴿And they did not divide﴾, is specified by the verse of al-Bayyinah, so that the intended meaning is: "And those who were given the Scripture did not divide"? Or do we say that it is general, and ﴿those who were given the Scripture did not divide﴾ refers to some individuals? And when some individuals are mentioned with a ruling that matches the ruling of the general statement, does it not count as a specification?

The second answer: This is a principle of usul al-fiqh (the principles of jurisprudence): when some individuals of a general term are mentioned with a ruling that agrees with the general ruling, this is not specification. Example: you say, "Honour the students." Then you say, "Honour Muhammad, and he is among them." Does this require that you not honour anyone else? Answer me.

* Students: No.

* The Shaykh: No. So mentioning him with a ruling that agrees with the general ruling does not require restricting it to him. But if the ruling contradicts it, then this is specification. If you say, "Honour the students," and then you say, "Do not honour Muhammad," then his ruling departs from the general ruling.

﴿And they did not divide except after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves﴾ [ash-Shura 14]. The author's words (by some of them affirming monotheism and some of them disbelieving) are suitable in light of His saying: ﴿Hard on the polytheists is that to which you call them﴾ [ash-Shura 13]. Otherwise, disagreement is broader than being disagreement over monotheism and disbelief.

﴿Except after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves﴾. So their division was with knowledge, and the proof had been established against them.

His saying ﴿out of rivalry among themselves﴾ is an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi); that is, their division was for the sake of rivalry and transgression.

(﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾ [ash-Shura 14], by delaying the recompense ﴿to a specified term, the matter would have been decided between them﴾), and so on to its end.

﴿Except after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾ [ash-Shura 14]. The word that preceded from Allah is the delay of the recompense until they meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿To a specified term﴾, meaning a defined appointed time, which is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿The matter would have been decided between them﴾ by punishing the disbelievers in this world. ﴿The matter would have been decided between them﴾, meaning it would have been settled and judged between them: the disbelievers would have been destroyed and the monotheists spared.

(﴿And indeed those who were given the Scripture after them﴾, and they are the Jews and the Christians), the commentator says: (﴿are in doubt concerning it﴾, concerning Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿in disquieting doubt﴾, causing unease).

The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾. The word is that He, Mighty and Majestic, decreed the delay of the punishment from them as a trial and a test. Allah the Exalted pointed to this trial and test in His saying: ﴿Had Allah willed, He could have avenged Himself upon them, but [He ordained fighting] to test some of you by means of others﴾ [Muhammad 4]. Had Allah taken vengeance upon them and destroyed them, there would be no place left for jihad, and the believers would have no trial or test. Therefore He said: ﴿But to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the way of Allah, He will never waste their deeds﴾ [Muhammad 4].

His saying ﴿to a specified term﴾ means appointed and fixed, and that is the Day of Standing. The Day of Standing is fixed in Allah's knowledge; it does not come early or late, just as a person's death is fixed by Allah; it does not come early or late.

﴿And indeed those who were given the Scripture after them are in doubt concerning it, in disquieting doubt﴾. And "those who were given the Scripture": that is, were given it. Was it given freely or in exchange? Freely, meaning without effort, just as the heir inherits the property of the deceased without effort, freely.

﴿Were given the Scripture after them﴾. Is the intended meaning of "the Scripture" here the Torah and the Gospel, or is the intended meaning the Qur'an, so that the meaning is: "And indeed those who were given the Scripture," which is the Qur'an, "after them," meaning after those who divided among the People of the Book and others, "are in doubt concerning it," meaning concerning this Book, "in disquieting doubt"?

What I am saying is better than what the author, may Allah have mercy on him, adopted. The author implies that the intended meaning of "the Scripture" is the Torah and the Gospel, because he said: (they are the Jews and the Christians). The Jews have the Torah and the Christians have the Gospel. But the apparent meaning is that the intended "Scripture" is this Qur'an: ﴿are in doubt concerning it﴾, meaning concerning this Book, ﴿in disquieting doubt﴾, meaning causing unease. Ribah (disquieting doubt) is stronger than shakk (doubt), because it is uneasy suspicion and anxiety. The one who merely doubts may be cold of heart and have no anxiety, but the one in ribah is more intense. Usually ribah occurs when the evidences conflict, each of which requires that one turn to it, so the person becomes suspicious, hesitant, and anxious. Mere doubt, however, is only doubt. It does not lead to ribah unless it becomes great and strong and the evidences conflict; then the person remains in intense suspicion.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: their division occurred after the proof had been established against them, based on His saying: ﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾ [Al 'Imran 19].

* Among its benefits: whoever opposes the religion after knowledge has come is a transgressor and an aggressor, based on His saying: ﴿out of rivalry among themselves﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, based on His saying: ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾ [ash-Shura 14]. There is no doubt that Allah, the Exalted, is described as speaking, because speech is a perfection, and its opposite is muteness, which is a deficiency. If we negated speech, this would necessitate muteness, and that is a deficiency from which Allah is far removed.

If someone says: What is the speech of Allah?

We say: The speech of Allah is what is heard by the ears. Gabriel hears it, and others hear it from among those whom Allah speaks to. This is the truth. The Jahmiyyah agreed with us on this, saying that the speech of Allah is what is heard by the ears. But we differ from them in that they say it is created, while we say it is not created.

The Ash'ariyyah and the Kullabiyyah and their like say: the speech of Allah is the meaning subsisting in His self, not what is heard. What is heard is an expression or a narration of the speech of Allah, and the speech of Allah is what subsists in His self. For this reason they hold that the speech of Allah is not connected to His will, so they do not say that Allah speaks whenever He wills, because it is a meaning subsisting in the self, like the subsistence of hearing and sight. There is no doubt that this is a false view, further from the truth than the view of the Jahmiyyah, because the Jahmiyyah explicitly state that the speech of Allah is what is heard and not an inner meaning, but they say it is created. Those people, when they say that the speech of Allah is the meaning subsisting in His self and that He created sounds that express what is in His self, did they oppose the Jahmiyyah? They did not oppose them; they agreed that this codex in our hands is created. But the Jahmiyyah became bolder than the Ash'ariyyah: the Jahmiyyah said, "This is the speech of Allah," while the others said, "It is an expression of the speech of Allah."

In any case, we say: when Allah attributes speech to Himself and says: ﴿And Allah spoke to Moses with direct speech﴾ [an-Nisa 164], and emphasizes it with His saying ﴿direct speech﴾, the evidences establish that He speaks to whomever He wills among His creation. What, then, makes us distort it? Which is more deserving of perfection: a god who speaks whenever He wills and with whatever He wills, or a god who does not speak? The first. Indeed, the second does not deserve to be a god. For this reason Abraham said: ﴿O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear or see and does not avail you at all?﴾ [Maryam 42]. So from His saying ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded﴾ [ash-Shura 14] we derive the affirmation of speech for Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in delaying punishment from the disobedient. Among the wisdoms in this is that Allah gives them respite, perhaps they will repent; therefore He said: ﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for what they earn, He would not leave upon it [the earth] any creature, but He defers them to a specified term﴾ [Fatir 45].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the world has a limit, based on His saying ﴿specified﴾, meaning defined and fixed, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And We do not delay it except for a limited term﴾ [Hud 104], meaning the punishment.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: those who were given the Scripture after them are in doubt concerning it, disquieting doubt. That means the Jews who encountered this Qur'an and inherited it after the earlier Jews, and likewise the Christians, are in disquieting doubt concerning it.

* Derived from this benefit: such people are not benefited by admonitions or signs, and the saying of Allah the Exalted supports this: ﴿But signs and warnings do not avail a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus 101].

* Student: Sometimes a person is asked by some common people or by upright people who have no knowledge: "What is your opinion of so-and-so and so-and-so?" referring to specific people. So what is the position of the student of knowledge regarding this?

* The Shaykh: If he says, "What is your opinion of so-and-so and so-and-so?", we now know that there are leaders who are a bell (a means of calling) for the people. If he asks me this, I would say: "What is it to you about so-and-so? Leave him alone. If he is dead, he has met his Lord; and if he is alive, we ask Allah only to make him upright." But if he specifies, saying, "What do you say about the opinion of so-and-so?", then I must speak, and I say: "This is right or wrong, according to what I have."

* Student: Is the disagreement among the parties (al-ahzab) a disagreement in thought, or in creed, as between the Shi'ah and the Sufis?

* The Shaykh: No. The disagreement of the Shi'ah with Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah is a wide divergence. The Shi'ah's disagreement with Ahl al-Sunnah is not like the disagreement of the Shafi'is with the Malikis, for example. No, it is a great disagreement, a disagreement over the foundations of creed. For example, among the foundations of creed for the Shi'ah is that they have leaders whom they call Imams, and they claim that some of these Imams know the unseen and govern the universe, and that some of their Imams reach a station that no drawn-near angel or sent prophet reaches, meaning the station of lordship. This is something we cannot agree with under any circumstances.

Among them are those who revile the Companions in general, except for a small few. Among them are those who curse Abu Bakr and 'Umar and say that they both died in hypocrisy. And what is strange is that I saw in the book of Ibn Hazm, may Allah have mercy on him, al-Milal wa'l-Nihal, a Shi'ah sect that declares 'Ali a disbeliever and declares Abu Bakr a disbeliever, both of them. As for Abu Bakr, they say he is a disbeliever because he wronged by seizing the caliphate. As for 'Ali, they say he was lax in his obligation. Why did he not prevent Abu Bakr? So the one is a transgressor and the other negligent, and both are disbelievers. Who remains? Nobody remains. They say: The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: why did he not designate him from the beginning and end the dispute? A strange thing!

But the disagreement between the Malikis, the Shafi'is, the Hanbalis, the Hanafis and those like them is not a disagreement. In reality there is no disagreement, except with a fanatic, of whom we say, "This is the truth," and he says, "No."

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Who?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: I say: it is not possible to agree with these people, but agreement with the Malikis, the Shafi'is and the Hanbalis is possible.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 42, verse 15 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So for that, call (people)﴾ [al-Shura 15]. "For that" refers to establishing the religion and not splitting into factions within it.

As for His saying ﴿call﴾, the fa' is extra, added to beautify the wording; the original would be "fa-li-dhalika ud'u" (for that, call). For this reason we say that this sentence contains restriction (hasr), the fronting of what should be delayed. What is fronted? The prepositional phrase (al-jar wa-al-majrur, the preposition with its object). That is why I told you that the fa' in His saying ﴿fa-d'u﴾ is extra for the sake of beautifying the wording. Had it not been from the speech of Allah, we would have said "fa-li-dhalika ud'u" (for that, call), and this is the secret behind our saying that this sentence conveys restriction.

﴿So for that, call﴾. The author, may Allah have mercy on him, said: (﴿For that﴾ refers to the tawhid, the oneness of Allah). It would have been better had he said: "﴿For that﴾, i.e., for establishing the religion and not splitting into factions within it." ﴿So for that, call﴾ is addressed to the Messenger ﷺ; for this reason the author said: (O Muhammad, the people). Mentioning "the people" indicates that the object of ﴿call﴾ is omitted, and the implied meaning is (the people).

(﴿And be upright﴾ in it ﴿as you have been commanded, and do not follow their desires﴾ [al-Shura 15] in abandoning it.) ﴿Be upright as you have been commanded﴾: this is not specific to the Messenger ﷺ, because of Allah's saying in Surah Hud: ﴿So be upright as you have been commanded, and those who turned in repentance with you﴾ [Hud 112].

His saying ﴿be upright as you have been commanded﴾ means in the manner you were commanded, without addition or deficiency. ﴿And do not follow their desires﴾: what are the desires that he was forbidden to follow? Whatever opposes what he was commanded; for this reason the author-commentator said: (in abandoning it).

﴿And say: I believe in what Allah has sent down of Scripture﴾ [al-Shura 15]. ﴿Say﴾ openly to them and to others: ﴿I believe in what Allah has sent down of Scripture﴾. ﴿I believe﴾ means: I affirm. Faith (iman) is affirmation that entails acceptance and submission, not mere affirmation. For this reason we say that Abu Talib was not a believer, even though he affirmed the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ. He said in his famous Lamiyya:

They certainly know that our son is not a liar among us,
nor is he one who is concerned with false speech.

And he said:

Indeed I know that the religion of Muhammad
is the best religion of mankind in religion.
Were it not for blame, or fear of disgrace,
you would see me gladly declaring it clearly.

But he—and we seek refuge in Allah—had already been decreed wretchedness by Allah. The last thing he said was that he was upon the religion of 'Abd al-Muttalib, and he declared in that state that, had it not been that his people would blame him and say, when he despaired of life, "He has believed out of fear," he would have believed—so he said, and we seek refuge in Allah, while in the throes of death.

So His saying ﴿I believe in what Allah has sent down of Scripture﴾: we say that faith is affirmation that entails acceptance and submission. Abu Talib affirmed, but he did not accept and did not submit, so he became a disbeliever.

﴿I believe in what Allah has sent down of Scripture﴾, i.e., in what Allah has sent down of all the books. Likewise it is obligatory upon us too to believe in what Allah has sent down of Scripture. But is it obligatory upon us to follow what Allah has sent down of Scripture?

The answer: No. We follow what has come in our Sharia, even if it opposes what is in the earlier laws; but we believe that the books sent down to Musa, 'Isa, Dawud and other prophets are true. Following, however, is for the Sharia of Muhammad ﷺ and his family.

﴿And I have been commanded to act justly between you﴾. What comes after ﴿li-a'dila﴾ according to you?
* Student: (...) ﴿And I have been commanded to act justly﴾; the author said: (so that I act justly between you).
* The Shaykh: The author, may Allah have mercy on him, informed us that the lam in His saying ﴿li-a'dila﴾ has the meaning of the ba' (bi); i.e., I have been commanded that I act justly ﴿between you﴾. This is what the author, may Allah have mercy on him, estimated, and there is no doubt that this is an easy estimation: to say the lam means the ba' and move on. But using the lam in the sense of the ba' may not be permissible in the Arabic language, and Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger ﷺ with a matter beyond that, i.e., ﴿And I have been commanded﴾ with the Sharia or with justice ﴿so that I act justly between you﴾. The thing commanded is then omitted, and what is present is the cause: "I have been commanded with such-and-such so that I may act justly between you." This is more eloquent than saying the lam means the ba', and that I have been commanded to act justly between you. No; we say: I have been commanded with the Sharia and with belief in every book, ﴿so that I act justly between you﴾ in judgment.

﴿Allah is our Lord and your Lord﴾. This sentence is true, without doubt. But someone may say: what is the benefit of it? Is it not like someone saying: the sky is above us and the earth is below us? Since these people acknowledge that Allah is their Lord, what is the benefit?

The benefit is to bind them to be like what we were upon in religion, because the Lord is one: ﴿Allah is our Lord and your Lord﴾ by your own acknowledgment. If that is so, then it is obligatory upon you to submit to the commands of your Lord, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds﴾: meaning that your deeds do not harm us and our deeds do not harm you. So do not attach yourselves to us, and we do not attach ourselves to you; each has his own deeds, and each will be recompensed for his deeds.

﴿There is no argument between us and you﴾. How can there be no argument between us and you when we have the argument against them? The intended meaning: there is no argument, the commentator said: (dispute, so that I act justly ﴿between us and you﴾) and so on.

The correct view: do not estimate "so that I act justly," because there is no need for it. Rather the meaning is: there is no argument established in the manner of dispute between us and you, because we have despaired of you and argument will not benefit you. ﴿Allah will gather us together﴾. He said: (This was before being commanded to fight).

After being commanded to fight, did their deeds become ours and ours theirs? Does the argument become void when fighting was legislated? No. For this reason we say to the author, may Allah pardon you: first, establish for us that this verse predates the command to fight. If he says: this verse is Meccan, and fighting was only commanded in Medina, we say: establish for us that when he was commanded to fight, this disavowal was annulled. He cannot establish that. Allah, glorified and exalted, speaks here about the state of the polytheists while the Prophet ﷺ was among them in Mecca, and fighting has no place in this at all, so that we could say this falls under abrogation.

(﴿Allah will gather us together﴾ on the Return, for the decision of judgment ﴿and to Him is the destination﴾, the return.) The sentence ﴿to Him is the destination﴾ contains restriction, its method being the fronting of what should be delayed. And Allah knows best.

* Student: Shall we say that abrogation covers earlier nations, or is it specific to one nation (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, it applies to us and to others. Listen to Allah's saying: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them good things which had been made lawful for them﴾ [al-Nisa 160]. This is abrogation: these good things had been lawful, then they were abrogated and made unlawful. The Sharia is one, while the two laws differ, as 'Isa said to the Children of Israel: ﴿And to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you﴾ [Al 'Imran 50].
* Student: The author's statement "this was before fighting"; perhaps he means the dispute between the Muslims and the disbelievers?
* The Shaykh: No. Many scholars, including the author, when they encounter verses like these, say: this was before the command to fight, meaning it is abrogated. Like His saying: ﴿For you is your religion and for me is my religion﴾ [al-Kafirun 6]; they said: this was before the command to fight. There is no need for that: the disavowal exists even after the command to fight.
* Student: The laws of those before us?
* The Shaykh: This is a matter of disagreement. Some scholars say the laws of those before us are laws for us; others say: no, the laws of those before us are laws for them, and for us there is a law, because of His saying: ﴿For each of you We have appointed a law and a path﴾ [al-Ma'ida 48]. The issue has long ramifications and deep investigations in the principles of jurisprudence. What appears to me is that the law of those before us which Allah revealed to us is a law for us, because Allah did not reveal to us in vain but so that we might take heed. Then if it is abrogated in our Sharia, it is abrogated. This is why you find scholars deriving many rulings from the stories of the prophets. Our Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, has benefits derived from the story of Yusuf; a treatise.
* Student: Is there any benefit or wisdom in the Prophet ﷺ being specified with revelation, and the rest of the prophets with a charge (wasiyya)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, the wisdom is establishing that this Qur'an is revealed.
* Student: On some radio stations there is a recitation from the Torah; is it permissible for laypeople and students of knowledge to listen to it?
* The Shaykh: Establish this for me, may Allah bless you; I am asking you for the authenticity of the transmission.
* Student: I heard it from the radio myself.
* The Shaykh: Saudi Arabia?
* Student: No, in Lebanon, Shaykh.
* Another student: Through another radio station not run by the state; a person hears it...
* The Shaykh: Who forbids the airwaves?! No, it is absolutely not permissible. It is narrated that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab showed the Prophet ﷺ a page from the Torah, and he became angry and said: «Are you in doubt, O son of al-Khattab? I have brought it to you white and pure. Had my brother Musa been alive, he would have had no choice but to follow me»[[Ahmad (15156) narrated with his chain from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the Prophet ﷺ with a book he had obtained from some of the People of the Book and read it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he became angry and said: «Are you bewildered by it, O son of al-Khattab? By Him in whose hand my soul is, I have brought it to you white and pure. Do not ask them about anything, lest they inform you of truth and you deny it, or of falsehood and you affirm it. By Him in whose hand my soul is, if Musa were alive, he would have had no choice but to follow me.»]]. Not at all, and it is not permissible. But the problem is: who forbids the airwaves? I am hesitant: should we warn laypeople against listening to these broadcasts? Because, regrettably, this station's voice comes through loud and perfectly clear. Should we warn people? There is a problem: if you warn people, you open the door for listening to it; they say, "What is it that he warns against?" And if you leave them, most people do not hear it, praise be to Allah.

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿So for that, call, and be upright as you have been commanded﴾ [al-Shura 15].

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation to call to the tawhid of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by His saying ﴿So for that, call﴾; and fronting the object indicates its importance.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: a person must be upright as he has been commanded, so that he does not introduce into the religion of Allah what is not part of it, by His saying ﴿and be upright as you have been commanded﴾.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: it is permissible to address a command to someone who already possesses the quality, in order to keep him steadfast in it, by His saying ﴿and be upright as you have been commanded﴾; because the Prophet ﷺ was upright as he had been commanded from the time he was sent, indeed from the time he was commissioned, but what is meant is steadfastness in this matter.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: the Prophet ﷺ is a servant who is commanded, to whom commands are directed, and he has no share in the affair, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You have no share in the matter﴾ [Al 'Imran 128]; and here He said: ﴿as you have been commanded﴾.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: a refutation of those people who claim that the Prophet ﷺ has a power of disposition over the universe and its management. A fortiori, it is also a refutation of those who say that someone other than the Messenger ﷺ has power of disposition over the universe, such as the Rafidah and some Sufis who claim that some of their imams dispose of the universe, and those Sufis who claim that some of their "poles" (aqtab) dispose of the universe. These people are without doubt astray and polytheists with respect to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: the prohibition of following desires, by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿and do not follow their desires﴾.
If someone asks: is following desire praiseworthy or blameworthy?
We say: whatever agrees with the Sharia is praiseworthy; for this reason it is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: «None of you believes until his desire is subordinate to what I have brought»[[Ibn Battah narrated it in al-Ibana (279) from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]. Whatever opposes the Sharia is blameworthy.
* From the benefits of this verse: Allah, blessed and exalted, strengthens His Prophet ﷺ, because commands and prohibitions such as these support him, firm him up and strengthen him.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation to believe in every book Allah has sent down, by His saying ﴿And say: I believe in what Allah has sent down of Scripture﴾ [al-Shura 15]. But how is belief in earlier books to be? Belief in earlier books is by believing that they were truly sent down from Allah, Mighty and Majestic; as for following them, it has been abrogated by this Sharia brought by Muhammad ﷺ and his family.
If someone asks: Do we believe that the books now in the hands of Christians and Jews are the books sent down to their prophets?
The answer: No, because Allah the Exalted mentioned that they altered them and concealed much of them; therefore we have no confidence in what they have of books that they claim are the books of Allah.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of justice, by His saying ﴿and I have been commanded to act justly between you﴾, in every dealing; indeed even in dealing with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, justice is obligatory. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and excellence and giving to relatives﴾ [al-Nahl 90]. When the Prophet ﷺ sent 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha to the Jews in Khaybar for the purpose of dividing the produce, he gathered them and said: "I have come to you from the most beloved of people to me, and you are more hateful to me than your counterparts of monkeys and pigs; yet my love for him and my hatred for you does not prevent me from acting justly among you." They said: "By this the heavens and earth stand."
The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, have mentioned: if a Muslim and a disbeliever are in a dispute before a judge, it is obligatory upon him to be just between them in seating, in looking, and in speech; that is, he should not speak to the disbeliever harshly or glance at him with contempt, but should treat him as he treats the Muslim, because justice is obligatory, and it is not permissible in the place of judgment to distinguish between so-and-so and so-and-so. For this reason He said: ﴿and I have been commanded to act justly between you﴾.
* From the benefits of this noble verse: the announcement of what binds the opponent, by His saying ﴿Allah is our Lord and your Lord﴾; meaning, since He is our Lord and your Lord, it is obligatory that we all submit to His commands.
If someone asks: is Allah the Lord of disbelievers?
