The third: 'izzat al-imtina', meaning that evil is impossible for Him, the Mighty, and imperfection is impossible for Him. The wrongdoers try to describe Him with deficiency, but it is impossible for Him. From it is their saying: "This is ground 'azaz." "Ard 'azaz" means what, exactly?

* Student: Inaccessible.

* The Shaykh: Hard and solid, the hard solid one that tools do not affect. They say it is 'azaz; in our colloquial language we say 'aza, dropping the second zay: "ard 'aza," meaning solid. So al-'Aziz, one of Allah's names, has three meanings. The first?

* Student: Overpowering and dominance.

* The Shaykh: It is dominance.

* Student: Magnitude and dominance.

* The Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: Magnitude, dominance, and inaccessibility.

* The Shaykh: May Allah bless you. All of these are established for Allah the Exalted. Ibn al-Qayyim said:

"He is al-'Aziz, so His threshold cannot be approached; how can the threshold of the possessor of authority be approached? He is al-'Aziz, the Dominant, the Overpowering, whom nothing overcomes; these are two attributes. He is al-'Aziz with a strength that is His attribute; so might then has three meanings."

Al-'Izz has three meanings: Allah the Exalted is the Strong and the Overpowering. When might is combined with strength and dominance, authority is complete, because some people are strong but not dominant. Have you considered: if there were a man extremely strong, with the strength of a horse, but he was a coward, does he overcome or is he overcome?

* Students: He is overcome.

* The Shaykh: He is overcome, because he is a coward. When strength and might combine, authority is complete. ﴿And He is the Strong, the Mighty﴾ and so on; Allah willing, it will come tomorrow.

We have previously established that "alla" (ألا) is an opening particle, and that it conveys?

* Student: Alertness.

* The Shaykh: Threat!

* Student: Alertness.

* The Shaykh: Alertness, it conveys alertness. Its example? An example of the opening alla that conveys emphasis and alertness?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: ﴿Unquestionably, the allies of Allah will have no fear, nor will they grieve﴾ [Yunus 62]. And in the verses before us: ﴿Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in extreme error﴾.

Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿Allah provides for whom He wills﴾ [Al 'Imran 37]. What is the meaning of "yarzuq" (provides)?

* Student: Gives.

* The Shaykh: Gives. And His saying "whom He wills" affirms will. But is Allah's will mere will, or is it will joined with something else?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: With wisdom, yes; for He does not will anything except that wisdom requires it, whether bringing it into existence or annihilating it.

What is the evidence that Allah's will is joined with wisdom?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills; indeed Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [Al-Insan 30]. Meaning: He does not will except what wisdom requires, whether bringing it into existence or annihilating it. And Allah is the One who grants success. We ask Allah the Exalted to encompass us and you with His mercy, and to grant us and you success in what He loves and is pleased with.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 42, verse 20:

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his tilth﴾ [ash-Shura 20].

It is not hidden from any of us, in terms of i'rab (grammatical analysis), that ﴿مَنْ﴾ (man, "whoever") here is conditional (shartiyyah). The evidence is His saying ﴿نَزِدْ لَهُ فِي حَرْثِهِ﴾ (nazid lahu fi harthihi, "We will increase him in his tilth"), where the response is in the jussive mood. In this construction the conditional verb is in the past tense and the response is in the present tense: past in ﴿مَنْ كَانَ﴾ (man kana, "whoever was"), and the response is ﴿نَزِدْ لَهُ فِي حَرْثِهِ﴾. The reverse also occurs, where the conditional verb is in the present tense and the response is in the past tense, as in: man yashkur Allah zadahu Allah (whoever thanks Allah, Allah increases him).

(﴿مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ﴾ means whoever desires, by his deed, ﴿حَرْثَ الْآخِرَةِ﴾ (harth al-akhirah, "the tilth of the Hereafter"), meaning its gain, which is the reward. ﴿نَزِدْ لَهُ فِي حَرْثِهِ﴾ means We will multiply it for him: a good deed becomes ten, or more.)

﴿حَرْثَ الْآخِرَةِ﴾: the original meaning of harth is what is tilled for growth and increase. From it comes the farmer's tilling of the land so that he sows it, gains, and his wealth increases.

His saying ﴿حَرْثَ الْآخِرَةِ﴾ (harth al-akhirah): he says (i.e., the author says): "That is, its gain, which is the reward."

﴿نَزِدْ لَهُ فِي حَرْثِهِ﴾: the author, may Allah have mercy on him, explained the increase of the tilth as an increase of reward: a good deed is multiplied tenfold, to seven hundredfold, to many multiples. We add another matter, namely that We give him from both this world and the Hereafter. The evidence is His saying: ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him from it, but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ [ash-Shura 20].

So ﴿نَزِدْ لَهُ فِي حَرْثِهِ﴾ has two aspects:

The first: Allah the Exalted gives him the reward of this world and the Hereafter.

The second: He multiplies the reward: a good deed becomes ten times its like, up to seven hundredfold, up to many multiples.

He said: ﴿وَمَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الدُّنْيَا﴾ (whoever desires the tilth of this world), meaning its gain and enjoyment of it. This person, generally, turns away from the Hereafter, because he wants nothing but this world. For this reason you find him intensely preoccupied with worldly affairs. Even if his car gets a spot of mud from walking on mud, he goes to clean and wipe it, yet his heart is full of filth, and he does not care to clean and purify it, because he desires nothing but this world. You find him, for example, in his palaces, concerned only with repairing and cleaning the walls, while the building of his religion does not concern him at all. About this person Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿We give him from it﴾, ﴿from it﴾, and We do not give him everything he wants: ﴿We give him from it﴾.

The phrase ﴿نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا﴾ (nu'tihi minha, "We give him from it") is absolute, but it is qualified by what is in surah al-Isra': ﴿Whoever desires the hasty (life), We hasten for him therein what We will, for whomever We desire﴾ [al-Isra' 18]. That is, not what he himself wills. Allah the Mighty and Majestic has made clear that what is hastened is subject to His will, and that the one for whom it is hastened, who is the human being, is subject to His desire. Hence He says: ﴿We hasten for him therein what We will, for whomever We desire﴾ [al-Isra' 18]. Pay attention: do not think there is repetition in the verse. ﴿مَا نَشَاءُ﴾ (ma nasha', "what We will") refers to what is hastened, and ﴿لِمَنْ نُرِيدُ﴾ (liman nurid, "for whomever We desire") refers to the one to whom it is hastened. Not everyone who wishes to be given something is given it, and not everyone who desires something obtains what he desires, because the matter is in the hand of Allah, glorified and exalted. For this reason He says here: ﴿We give him from it﴾.

If someone says: the phrase ﴿نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا﴾ is the response of the conditional, and it implies that Allah will give him from it.

We say: this absolute statement is qualified by the verse of surah al-Isra': ﴿Whoever desires the hasty (life)﴾, which is this world, ﴿We hasten for him therein what We will, for whomever We desire; then We have made for him Hell, he will burn in it, blamed and rejected﴾ [al-Isra' 18].

(﴿نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا﴾ means without multiplication, only what has been apportioned to him. ﴿وَمَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ نَصِيبٍ﴾ means and he has no share in the Hereafter.) We ask Allah for well-being.

* In this verse there is an exhortation for a person to desire the Hereafter by his deeds.

If someone asks: how can one desire the Hereafter through worldly actions? Let us suppose eating and drinking: a person goes to the market to buy bread and a condiment. How does he desire the Hereafter?

We say: he can desire the Hereafter through it in the following ways:

First, he desires to comply with Allah's command, by His saying: ﴿Eat and drink﴾ [al-A'raf 31].

Second, he desires to preserve his strength and health, and this is something required, because Allah says: ﴿Do not kill yourselves﴾ [an-Nisa' 29].

And we were commanded to eat of the good things and to thank Him. By this he desires to strengthen himself for obedience to Allah, because whenever the body is stronger, worship is more complete. So by his eating and drinking he desires to strengthen himself for obedience to Allah.

Fourth: he desires by this to enjoy the generosity of Allah. How is that? Because the generous person loves that his generosity be accepted. Is that not so? That is, if a generous, bountiful man gave you a gift, would he rejoice if you accepted it and be saddened if you returned it, or the opposite?

* The students: The first.

* The Shaykh: The first. He is pleased if you accept it and saddened if you refuse it.

Indeed our Lord, may He be exalted, is the most generous of the generous. He loves that His servants take pleasure in His bounties and enjoy them. So this is desiring the tilth of the Hereafter through worldly action. As for purely Hereafter acts, such as prayer, fasting, and pilgrimage, and what is similar to them, their ruling is clear.

So now I repeat the question once more: how can a person desire the tilth of the Hereafter through what belongs to the affairs of this world?

The answer is that this is possible. We give an example with eating and drinking, and four intentions become clear to us, for each of which a person is rewarded, although a careful reflector would find more than this.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a warning against desiring this world alone, by His saying: ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him from it, but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾.

* Among the benefits: whoever desires the tilth of this world is not given everything he desires, by His saying: ﴿We give him from it﴾. Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter is given all he desires and more.

* Among them: an indication that actions are by intentions, by His saying: ﴿desires﴾. In this there is an indication of the goodness of intention, and that a person should make his intention good, indeed it is obligatory upon him to do so.

* Among them: a refutation of the Jabriyyah (determinists). From where is this derived? From His saying ﴿desires﴾, because the Jabriyyah say that a human being has no will. Glory be to Allah! He has no will?! No, he has no will! He cooks food to eat it, and they say this is without will. He prepares household utensils to use them, and they say this is not by his will, it is not by his choice. What do you say about this opinion? This is an opinion contrary to human nature, contrary to the least natural disposition. Even a child knows the difference between being compelled and acting by choice.

A thief was brought before the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and he ordered that his hand be cut off. The conditions for the amputation were met, and the man said: "Wait, O Commander of the Faithful! By Allah, I only stole this by the decree of Allah." What did he mean? That the prescribed punishment be lifted, since it was by Allah's will, meaning I had no choice in it. The Commander of the Faithful said to him: "And we will not cut off your hand except by the will of Allah." So he was struck dumb, because he could not say anything. Yet the Commander of the Faithful's cutting off his hand was by Allah's universal and legislated will, while the thief's theft was by Allah's universal will only, since he was not permitted to steal. So in the verse there is a refutation of whom? Of the Jabriyyah.

Is there in the verse any evidence for the Qadariyyah, who deny Allah's will regarding what the servant does?

The answer: No. There is no refutation of their view in it, but there is no affirmation of their view in it either, because is a person's will one of his attributes or not? It is one of his attributes; it is he who wills.

Is the servant created or not created? Created. So if he is created, his attributes are also necessarily created. Your will is created by Allah, inasmuch as you yourself are created, and the attribute of a created thing is created.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the perfection of the authority of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, by His saying: ﴿We give him from it﴾, ﴿We will increase him in his tilth﴾.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of Allah's generosity, and that He, the Mighty and Majestic, is more generous than His servant: the servant does a little and is rewarded much.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the Hereafter. Its affirmation is established by the Qur'an, the Sunnah, the consensus of the Muslims (ijma', scholarly agreement), and sound reasoning, that is, the intellect.

As for the Book and the Sunnah, they are full of affirmation of the Last Day.

As for consensus, it is established: none of the Muslims denies the Hereafter, and whoever denies it has disbelieved.

As for sound reasoning, it is based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, He who ordained the Qur'an upon you will surely return you to a place of return﴾ [al-Qasas 85], and His saying: ﴿Did you think that We created you in vain and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun 115]. Consider, O brothers: suppose Allah the Mighty and Majestic created this creation, sent the messengers, revealed the books, and enjoined jihad, and this man kills that man for the sake of Allah's religion, takes his women captive, and seizes his property, plunders his wealth, and then the matter ends with us becoming dust and never being raised. What would this action be? Vanity, from which Allah is far removed. Were it not for our belief in the Last Day, the strong among us would devour the weak, because he would not expect any reckoning. But reason requires and makes obligatory belief in the Last Day.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever desires the world by his deed has no share in the Hereafter.

But is the negation of share here a complete negation, or is it that he has no share in the Hereafter through this deed by which he desired the world? The second or the first?

* The students: The second.

* The Shaykh: The second, without doubt, unless this deed and intention are of the kind that takes one outside the religion, in which case he has no share at all.

Suppose a person studies in order to obtain an ijazah, that is, a certificate. Would he be among those who desire the tilth of this world or of the Hereafter?

It depends on what is in his heart. If he wanted the certificate in order to rise to a worldly position, then he desired this world. If he wanted by it to rise to a position through which he could benefit the Muslims by teaching or by administering, then he desired the Hereafter without doubt. For this reason, in this matter, the difference between this world and the Hereafter is no more than a hair's breadth, or less. Do you want, through the certificate, to say: "I am ranked fifth, or tenth, or hundredth, or two hundredth, or thousandth, or two thousandth"? Or do you want by it to occupy a place through which you benefit people? The first is a loser, and the second is a winner. Unfortunately, we have now reached the point where a person is valued only by the card he carries. Knowledge has become a paper you bring out from (...), a doctorate certificate number (A). If you hand it over, that is it: "What do you want? Where shall we employ you? What place do you want?"

But if a man of knowledge like Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah came and said: "Employ me in a primary school," what would they say to him? Answer, O people, with reality.

* The students: (...).

* The Shaykh: "You have no certificate, we will not employ you." O man, employ him, try him! They say: "There is no such position." So now the measure of people's knowledge is this card. If people have descended to this level, I will go along with them, and my intention is known to Allah. My aim is to occupy a place in the Ummah: to be a teacher, a judge, or a head of something through which I can guide people. And Allah is the Granter of success.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Or do they have partners who have prescribed for them﴾ [Ash-Shura 21]. The commentator (al-mufassir) said: (﴿Am﴾ means *bal*, "rather"). By this he indicates that *am* here is *munqati'ah* (disjunctive, i.e., a separate interrogative construction, "am" meaning "rather"). The disjunctive *am* is the one that comes with the meaning of *bal* ("rather") together with the interrogative hamzah. The meaning is: "Rather, do they have partners?"

﴿Or do they have partners who have prescribed for them﴾. The author said: (﴿for them﴾ refers to the disbelievers of Makkah). The correct view is that it is more general than that, meaning that all polytheists have partners whom they have set up alongside Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who prescribe for them from the religion what Allah has not permitted.

He said: (They are their devils. ﴿Prescribed﴾, i.e., the partners, ﴿for them﴾, i.e., for the disbelievers). Here he said "for the disbelievers," and previously he said "the disbelievers of Makkah," so the definite article in his words is for prior mention (*al-'ahd al-dhikri*). (﴿From the religion﴾, the corrupt religion, ﴿what Allah has not permitted﴾, such as polytheism and denial of resurrection). This interrogation here carries the sense of rebuke against them for taking these as partners who prescribe for them from the religion what Allah has not permitted.

As for His saying ﴿what He has not permitted﴾, the permission meant here is the legal permission (*al-idhn al-shar'i*), because permission is of two kinds: decreed (*qadari*) and legislated (*shar'i*). What relates to command and prohibition is legislated, and what relates to creation and bringing into existence is decreed. So, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [Al-Baqarah 255], is the intended permission legislated or decreed?

* A student: Legislated.

* The Shaykh: It may be either. ﴿Except by His permission﴾ means that He permits it by decree, that someone may intercede, or permits it by law.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they cannot harm anyone by it except by Allah's permission﴾ [Al-Baqarah 102]. Which of the two permissions is it?

* The students: The decreed one.

* The Shaykh: The decreed one, because Allah, exalted is He, does not legislatively permit sorcerers to harm anyone.

And here: ﴿They have prescribed for them from the religion what Allah has not permitted﴾ [Ash-Shura 21], i.e., what He has not permitted legislatively. As for by decree, He has permitted it, because it occurred, and everything that occurs is permitted by decree, since nothing can occur in the dominion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He has not permitted by decree.

Among that, i.e., among their legislating what Allah has not permitted, is making lawful what Allah has forbidden or making unlawful what Allah has made lawful. For this reason, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, made those who make lawful what is forbidden and make forbidden what is lawful into lords, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ [At-Tawbah 31]. ʿAdiyy ibn Hatim said to the Messenger (ﷺ): "We do not worship them." He said: "Do they not make lawful what Allah has forbidden, and you make it lawful, and make unlawful what Allah has made lawful, and you make it unlawful?" He said: "Yes." He said: "That is their worship."[[Al-Tirmidhi (3095) and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (17/92, no. 218), with the wording of the latter, from the hadith of ʿAdiyy ibn Hatim, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a gold cross around my neck. He said: "ʿAdiyy, throw this idol from your neck," so I threw it away. I came to him and he was reciting Surat Bara'ah, and he recited this verse: ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ until he finished it. I said: "We do not worship them." He said: "Do they not make unlawful what Allah has made lawful, and you make it unlawful, and make lawful what Allah has forbidden, and you make it lawful?" I said: "Yes." He said: "That is their worship."]] That is, their obedience.

(﴿And had it not been for a decisive word﴾, i.e., the prior decree that the recompense is on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾, and between the believers, by punishing them in this world, ﴿and indeed the wrongdoers﴾, the disbelievers, ﴿will have a painful punishment﴾ [Ash-Shura 21], i.e., painful).

﴿Had it not been for the decisive word, the matter would have been decided between them.﴾ The grammarians say that *lawla* (lawla) is a particle of prevention due to existence. What was prevented in this verse?

* The students: The judgment.

* The Shaykh: The judgment between them. What exists is the decisive word.

Know that *lawla* is a particle of prevention due to existence, *lamma* is a particle of existence due to existence, and *law* is a particle of prevention due to prevention. These three particles divide the three meanings among them.

*Law* is a particle of prevention due to prevention. You say: "Had you visited me, I would have honored you." Here the honoring was prevented because the visit was prevented.

And you say: "When I saw you, I honored you." Here the honoring existed because the seeing existed.

And you say: "Had it not been for Zayd, I would have done such and such." This is a particle of prevention due to existence.

﴿Had it not been for the decisive word﴾, which is Allah's prior word by which He, Mighty and Majestic, decreed that everything has a determined term. Had it not been for this word, by which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, decreed that everything has a determined term, Allah would have decided between them and the believers by hastening the punishment upon them.

* In this verse there are benefits, among them: whoever obeys leaders and elders in forbidding something Allah has made lawful, or making lawful something Allah has forbidden, or making obligatory something Allah has not made obligatory, has indeed taken them as partners.

From this benefit it follows that those who follow the callers to innovations have taken them as partners.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: matters that are legislated must have permission from Allah. That is, whatever a person does as an act of worship must have permission from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because Allah, exalted is He, denounced those who took partners who prescribed for them from the religion what Allah has not permitted. This is the meaning of our saying: The basic principle regarding acts of worship is prohibition and prevention, unless evidence is established for their legislation. Accordingly, if we see a person worshipping in a way we did not know, we have the right to denounce him until he brings evidence, isn't that so? Because religion is received from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: what is other than religious matters is subject to customary matters, or customary circumstances, because of His saying: ﴿They have prescribed for them from the religion﴾. Based on this, if they legislate laws and systems that have no connection with religion, then that is permissible, and conforming to these systems is not considered polytheism. How much more so when these systems are supported by general principles, namely, securing benefits and averting harms!

* Among the benefits of this verse: a refutation of those ignorant people who deny every system that governments enact, regardless of whether it is a religious or a worldly matter, and regardless of whether it conforms to the Shariah or not. For some people say, for example: "I do not abide by traffic regulations, because there is no evidence for them." Perhaps they also say: "These are innovations."

It is said to him:

First: Worldly matters are originally permissible, and whoever does them outside the customary practice is not to be called an innovator; rather, one examines whether they are lawful or unlawful.

Second: The texts indicate the obligation to obey those in authority, as in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those of authority among you﴾ [An-Nisa' 59], and the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning the ruler: "Listen and obey, even if he takes your wealth and strikes your back."[[Muslim (1847/52) from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman with the wording: "Hear and obey the ruler, even if your back is beaten and your wealth is taken, so hear and obey."]]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in hastening or delaying the punishment, because of His saying: ﴿And had it not been for the decisive word﴾.

* Among its benefits: what Allah has decreed from eternity, meaning in the past, does not change, because of His saying: ﴿And had it not been for the decisive word, the matter would have been decided between them﴾.

If someone says: What do you say about His saying: ﴿Allah erases what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 39]? Does it contradict what we have established as benefits of this verse?

The answer: No, it does not contradict, because Allah said: ﴿Allah erases what He wills and establishes﴾, then He said: ﴿and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, meaning its origin. What is in the Mother of the Book does not change, and what is not in it does change. Does not Allah, exalted is He, say: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds﴾ [Hud 114]? So bad deeds, after being recorded, are followed by good deeds which erase them. A person sins, the sin is recorded, then he seeks forgiveness and the sin is erased. As for what is in the origin of the Book, it does not change. Accordingly, this does not contradict this verse, namely His saying: ﴿And had it not been for the decisive word, the matter would have been decided between them﴾.

If someone says: What do you say about the authentic hadith: "Whoever wishes to have his provision expanded and his life extended, let him keep the ties of kinship"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5986) and Muslim (2557/21), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]]? This indicates that keeping ties of kinship is a cause for abundant provision and a cause for long life, while you say that life is written and provision is written.

The answer: Provision is written upon this cause, and the term is written upon this cause. So Allah has written the term of this person to be delayed for keeping ties of kinship, and has expanded the provision of this person for keeping ties of kinship, and this is known to Allah. But the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned this to encourage keeping ties of kinship, because a person does not know what has been written for him in the future, and thus there is no contradiction.

As for those scholars who said that the meaning of His saying: "his life is extended" (yunsa'a lahu fi athrihi) is that Allah blesses him in his lifespan, this is not correct, because it contradicts the apparent meaning of the hadith. The apparent meaning of the hadith is that he is delayed, but it is written with Allah that he keeps ties and that his life is until such and such. But does a person know that it is written with Allah in this way? He does not know. So the Prophet (ﷺ) wanted to urge people to keep ties of kinship by such a promise.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of causes, because of His saying: ﴿And had it not been for the decisive word, the matter would have been decided between them﴾. So the word is a cause for delaying the punishment. The affirmation of causes is something that none denies except the one who rejects the truth.

Know that people have divided regarding causes into three categories:

One category denied causes entirely and said: There is no effect of the cause on the caused.

Another category affirmed causes in an excessive manner and claimed that they are—i.e., the causes—necessarily effective and binding.

The third category affirmed causes, but made that subject to the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

So how many categories are there?

* A student: Three.

* The Shaykh: Three. Count them.

* A student: The first category denied causes.

* The Shaykh: Yes, they denied the effect of causes.

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: He went to excess in affirming them and made them necessarily effective in themselves. And the third?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: They said: But they are under the will of Allah. This view is the one that is required: we do not deny causes. How could we deny them while we see them with our own eyes? They say: What happens through a cause is not caused by it, but occurs in its presence. For example, if you throw a stone at a glass bottle and it breaks, they say: What broke it was not the stone, but the will of Allah at the moment of contact with the stone. So it occurred at the cause, not by the cause. When you put a piece of paper in fire and it burns, they say: The fire did not burn it; the will of Allah burned it at the moment of contact with the fire. This is incomprehensible talk, at which the foolish laugh before the wise. How can we say, while we see that a stone falling on a bottle breaks it, that it did not break it? If a person leaned on the bottle, anyone who was present would say to him: Do not lean on it, or it will break.

As for the second view, the excessive affirmation of causes, those who say that causes necessarily act or necessarily have effect, these too are misguided. Here is the great fire which was cool and safe for Abraham. If the cause were necessarily effective in itself, it would have burned Abraham in every case. But Allah said: ﴿O fire, be cool and safe upon Abraham﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 69], so it became cool and became safe. The scholars said: Had Allah said "be cool" without saying "and safe," it would have destroyed Abraham with cold. But Allah joined the coolness with safety. So the verse before us includes the affirmation of causes, because of His saying: ﴿And had it not been for the decisive word, it would have been decided﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the severe warning to the wrongdoers, because of His saying: ﴿For them is a painful punishment﴾.

* Among its linguistic benefits: *alim* (painful) may come with the meaning of *mu'lim* (causing pain). That is, *fa'il* with the meaning of *mufil*. This is rare in the Arabic language. Most often *alim* in Arabic means *alim* (in pain/hurting), i.e., with the meaning of the active participle; this is the most common usage. But *fa'il* may come with the meaning of *mufil*, as in this verse, and as in the saying of the poet:

Is it from Rayhanah, the summoner who hears, that sleeplessness keeps me awake, while my companions are in deep sleep?
Is it from Rayhanah, the summoner who hears ∗∗∗ …………………
(*al-Sami'* means *al-Musmi'*, the one who makes to hear). He says it about his beloved: the summoner who makes to hear.

……………………… ∗∗∗ keeps me awake, while my companions are in deep sleep.

I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"?﴾ [Ash-Shura 24].

﴿Am﴾ here, the exegete said: (Bal, "rather"). That is, "am" has the meaning of "bal." They call it disjunctive (munqati'ah), because "am" may be connective (muttasilah) or disjunctive (munqati'ah). When it means "bal," it is disjunctive, since it resembles a turning away from what preceded it. When it means "aw" ("or"), it is connective, as when I say: "Do you want a book or a watch?" What is this?
* The students: Connective.
* The shaykh: Connective, because it means "aw," and neither of its two parts can do without the other.
But when you say: ﴿Or do they say, "He has forged it"?﴾ [Yunus 38], you do not find a counterpart in it, so it is disjunctive, meaning "bal."
﴿They say﴾: that is, the disbelievers among the idolaters of Quraysh and others. ﴿"He has invented a lie against Allah"﴾: that is, he fabricated a lie against Allah, by his saying that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah. They said: the Qur'an is not the speech of Allah, Muhammad is a liar, but he is a sorcerer, a soothsayer, a madman, and similar words with which they slandered the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If Allah willed, He would seal up your heart, and Allah would erase falsehood and establish the truth by His words﴾ [Ash-Shura 24].
﴿If Allah willed, He would seal up your heart﴾: the object of "willed" is omitted and is determined by the context; that is: if Allah willed that you fabricate a lie against Him, which is impossible, ﴿He would seal up your heart﴾. The author said: (He would bind it), and the correct meaning is that sealing here means stamping: that is, if you had fabricated a lie against Allah, Allah would have stamped upon your heart. ﴿And Allah would erase falsehood﴾: the falsehood you had fabricated, supposing that you had fabricated it. ﴿And establish the truth by His words﴾: (He would confirm it), that is, He would establish it, ﴿by His words﴾ revealed to His Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾ [Ash-Shura 24].
The meaning of the verse in summary: even supposing you had fabricated a lie against Allah, Allah would not leave you alone; He must make the truth clear. He would seal your heart, that is, stamp upon it; then Allah would erase falsehood and establish the truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts.

This is similar to the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke [or desired], Satan threw into his wish. But Allah abolishes what Satan throws in; then Allah makes His verses precise. And Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ [Al-Hajj 52]. That is: when he recited, Satan cast into his recitation. ﴿Then Allah abrogates what Satan casts, then Allah establishes His verses, and Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ [Al-Hajj 52].

As for His saying: ﴿If Allah willed﴾, does this conditional necessarily entail its occurrence? No. A condition sometimes comes with the greatest impossibilities. Have you not considered the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say, "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers"﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 81]? Is it possible for Allah to have a son? It is not possible, yet the conditional was used.
And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it has certainly been revealed to you and to those before you: If you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be lost﴾ [Az-Zumar 65]. Does this entail the permissibility of the Prophet ﷺ associating partners with Allah? It does not entail that.
And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, then ask those who recite the Scripture before you. The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [Yunus 94]. Is it possible that he be in doubt? No.
So ﴿If Allah willed﴾ means: if Allah willed that you fabricate a lie against Him. This conditional does not entail the permissibility of the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, fabricating a lie against Allah. It is well known that Allah has testified to His Prophet ﷺ regarding his prophethood, saying: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness﴾ [An-Nisa 166].

He said: ﴿And establish the truth by His words; indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾. That is, "of the companion of the breasts." And what is "the companion of the breasts"? It is the hearts, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ [Al-Hajj 46].

Among the benefits of this noble verse: the attempt by the polytheists to confuse people so that they deny the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"?﴾, so that the common people think he fabricated a lie against Allah and turn away from what he brought.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: showing the severity of the disbelievers' opposition to what the Prophet ﷺ brought, from their saying: ﴿He has invented a lie against Allah﴾.
* Among its benefits: that such speech is a disparagement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, a disparagement of the Qur'an, and a disparagement of the Prophet ﷺ.
As for its being a disparagement of Allah: it is not wise for Allah, the Exalted, to support one who fabricates a lie against Him; rather, wisdom requires that He punish him and not support him. Allah, glorified and exalted, has supported His Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, with signs that demonstrate his truthfulness.
It is a disparagement of the Qur'an, because on their claim it is speech fabricated by the Messenger, peace be upon him. They said: ﴿It is only a human who teaches him﴾, so Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [An-Nahl 103].
It is a disparagement of the Messenger, peace be upon him, that the most truthful of creation be placed in the position of one who fabricates against whom? Against Allah. And fabricating against Allah is more grievous than fabricating against others. For this reason the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾ [Al-An'am 21].

* Among the benefits of the verse: affirming the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. From where is this derived?
* A student: (...).
* The shaykh: From His saying: ﴿If Allah willed, He would seal up﴾.
Is the will of Allah unaccompanied by wisdom, or does He will nothing except for a wisdom?
The second, due to the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills; indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [Al-Insan 30]. He made clear that He, Mighty and Majestic, has complete will, and followed that with His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾, to make clear that the will of Allah, glorified and exalted, is not a mere will without purpose, but is for a wisdom.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the Prophet ﷺ is a creature of Allah whom He does with as He wills. From where is this derived?
* A student: ﴿If Allah willed, He would seal up your heart﴾.
* The shaykh: ﴿If Allah willed, He would seal up your heart﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the heart is the locus of perception, intellect, and action, due to His saying: ﴿He would seal up your heart﴾, which indicates that the whole management of action revolves around the heart.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that sealing upon the heart is a punishment, whether it is a sealing upon knowledge or a sealing upon intention and will, for it is undoubtedly a punishment. For this reason, among the supplications of the Prophet ﷺ was: "O Turner of the hearts, make our hearts firm upon Your obedience"[[Recorded by al-Kharaʼiti in I'tilal al-qulub from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, with the wording "O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your obedience"; and al-Tirmidhi (2140) and Ibn Majah (3834) recorded it in similar wording from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]], and "O Director of the hearts, direct our hearts to Your obedience"[[Recorded by Muslim (2654/17), and al-Nasa'i in al-Kubra (7692) with this wording, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As.]]. Therefore a person must not rely on the certainty that is in his heart, for it may vanish; rather he must always ask Allah for steadfastness. This is taken from His saying: ﴿If Allah willed, He would seal up your heart﴾.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the excellence of the Qur'an's arguments, in that it argues from a clear matter against what these people claimed: that if Allah had willed that the Messenger, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, fabricate a lie against Him, He would have sealed his heart and made him forget what he had, then Allah would have erased the falsehood he had fabricated, then He would have established the truth by His words.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, the Exalted, does not sanction falsehood: ﴿Allah would erase falsehood﴾, so it is impossible for Allah, the Exalted, to sanction falsehood.
From this benefit there branches a great benefit: when something was done in the time of the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, and we do not know that the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, was aware of it, do we judge it permissible because Allah was aware of it and remained silent about it, or do we not judge it so until we know that the Prophet ﷺ knew of it?
The first, because Allah does not sanction falsehood, and revelation was still descending. For this reason some scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, err when evidence is drawn from what occurred in the time of the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family; they say: the Prophet ﷺ did not know. We say: Grant that he did not know; Allah did know.
An example of this: some scholars said: it is not valid for the imam to be performing a voluntary prayer while the follower is performing an obligatory prayer; that is, it is not valid to pray the dawn prayer behind one who is praying a supererogatory prayer. This is the position of our school. It was said to them: this view is rejected, because Mu'adh ibn Jabal used to pray the 'Isha' prayer with the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, then he would go to his people and lead them in that same prayer during the time of the Prophet ﷺ[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (701) and Muslim (465/178), from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah that Mu'adh ibn Jabal used to pray with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the late 'Isha', then return to his people and lead them in that prayer.]]. They said: there is no proof in this, because we do not know that the Prophet ﷺ was aware of it. What is the answer?
The answer: if he was not aware of it, Allah was aware of it; and had it been false in Allah's sight, He would have made it clear, as He made clear the state of those who plot at night what He does not approve of in speech and conceal it from people. He said: ﴿They hide from people, but they cannot hide from Allah, and He is with them when they plot by night what He does not approve of in speech﴾ [An-Nisa 108]. Thus we repel the doubt of those who said: perhaps the Prophet ﷺ did not know of it. With what? With the fact that Allah knew it, and had it been false, He would not have approved it.
Moreover, we say: it is far-fetched that the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, did not know of it, while Mu'adh had been complained about to the Messenger ﷺ for prolonging the prayer. But we want to descend to the level of the opponent and say: grant that the Messenger did not know of it; Allah did know of it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, blessed and exalted, can never grant an unbeliever absolute empowerment. From where do we take this? Who knows?
* A student: ﴿And Allah would erase falsehood﴾.
* The shaykh: No.
* A student: The saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: If Allah had willed, He would have sealed their hearts.
* The shaykh: Is this verse from your own pocket?!
* A student: From His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah would erase falsehood and establish the truth﴾.
* The shaykh: No.
* A student: ﴿If Allah willed, He would seal up your heart﴾.
* The shaykh: Yes indeed, ﴿If Allah willed, He would seal up your heart﴾, so He does not empower you over falsehood.
Our phrase "absolute empowerment" excludes the case in which Allah, the Exalted, empowers the unbeliever in a manner that is not stable, as occurred at the Battle of Uhud, when the polytheists defeated the Muslims, but that was not a stable defeat. Rather, it is from the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that He empowers the disbelievers so that they become emboldened to fight the Muslims, and then the Muslims subdue them.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that when Allah, glorified and exalted, erases falsehood, He puts the truth in its place: ﴿And Allah would erase falsehood and establish the truth﴾.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: affirming words for Allah: ﴿by His words﴾.
Allah, glorified and exalted, speaks with real speech, with letters and audible sounds, and with dialogue between Him and whomever He wills of His creation. This is the doctrine of the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-salih), and upon it the great trial (al-mihnah) befell the leaders of the Muslims at the hands of unjust rulers and evil scholars, when the Jahmiyyah and the Mu'tazilah innovated the view that Allah does not speak but rather creates speech; they said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not speak, but creates speech, and His speech is created.
It is said: if we said that the speech of Allah is created, the Sharia would be nullified, because command, prohibition, information, questioning, and narratives would all be equal, being created and none distinguished from another. In terms of sound, it would be like the roar of thunder, and in terms of writing, like wall engravings, since they are created; and then there would be no command, no prohibition, no information, no questioning, and nothing at all.
A group tried to be subtle but did not succeed, and said: the speech of Allah is uncreated, but His speech is the meaning subsisting in His essence, and what is heard from Him is an expression of the speech of Allah, and it is created. Look how this group went astray until they became more astray than those who said that speech is created.
What is the meaning of their words? They say: the speech of Allah is the meaning subsisting in His essence, just as if you, within yourself, determined to speak a statement and then said it. They say: Allah, the Exalted, concealed speech within Himself and then created sounds that indicate it. So what is in the Mushaf is not the speech of Allah, is it not? It is not the speech of Allah, but it is created, which Allah created to express what is in the essence of Allah.
The Mu'tazilah say: what is in the codices is the speech of Allah and is created; the Ash'arites say: it is not the speech of Allah, and it is created. Which of them is closer to the truth? The Mu'tazilah are closer.
These people claim to be the rational ones, meaning the Ash'arites, and that they sought to combine the transmitted and the rational, but they corrupted both the transmitted and the rational.
So we say: Allah speaks with audible speech and with successive letters, and Allah does what He wills: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin 82].
* Among its benefits: the comprehensiveness of the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the depth of His knowledge; that it is a profound knowledge reaching the most hidden thing. From where? ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾.
* Among its benefits is the important practical benefit, that when a person knows that Allah, the Exalted, knows what is in his heart, he will refrain from every evil intention and proceed to every good intention.
* Among them: that the servant must correct what is in his heart, because everything depends on it. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered (9) and what is in the breasts is obtained?﴾ [Al-'Adiyat 9-10].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 42, verse 24 (part 2 of 2):

Know, my brother, that judgment in this world is based on the outward, while judgment in the Hereafter is based on the inward. So which will you do: improve your outward appearance so that you are judged in this world according to what this outward appearance requires, or improve your inward so that you are judged in your favour on the Day of Resurrection according to what this inward requires? Which of the two? The second. For this reason, do not be deceived by abundant bowing and prostration, weeping of the eye, and the like. Rather, look to what is in the heart. Although these deeds I have mentioned are a sign of the heart's righteousness, nevertheless firmly establish faith in the heart. You must reform the heart before anything else. Plant in your heart the love of Allah and His Messenger. Plant in your heart the love of the Sharia, even if it is burdensome to you, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Fighting has been enjoined upon you while it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you know not.﴾ [Al-Baqarah 216]. Plant in your heart the love of the believers. Do not hate any believer, even if he has wronged you. If a believer wrongs you, then hate his wrongdoing, but as for him personally, do not hate him. Plant in your heart loyalty (wilayah) to every Muslim and enmity to every disbeliever... and so on. The important thing is that you attend to the righteousness of your heart, for it is upon it that the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection revolves. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, He is Able to return him. (8) On the Day when secrets are examined﴾ [At-Tariq 8, 9], i.e., the hidden things are tested. O Allah, reform our outward and our inward, O Lord of the worlds.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the matter revolves around the hearts, and that they are in the chests. The hearts are in the chests, and by them is the intellect. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have they not travelled in the earth so that they would have hearts by which to understand?﴾ [Al-Hajj 46], and ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ [Al-Hajj 46]. Based on this, we must believe that the intellect is in the heart, because the verse is explicit or clear on this point.

As for the saying of some that the intellect is in the brain, it is weak, being opposed to the word of the Knowing Creator, the Mighty and Majestic. Yet the brain, there is no doubt, when it is impaired, the person's conduct becomes disordered, and the origin of the intellect is in the heart without doubt. The Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The intellect is in the heart, and it has a connection to the brain."

We are also related from our shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, 'Abd al-Rahman, that one of the Mu'tazilites was sentenced to death at a time when people disagreed over whether the intellect is in the brain or in the heart. He said to them: "When you kill me, sever my head. Then, if the intellect is in my heart, I will move my hand, or he said: my finger; and if it is in the brain, it will depart with the brain." They did so, and when they killed him, he moved the limb he had mentioned to them in the manner he had described. This is a sensory proof, if the story is authentic, a sensory proof that the intellect is in the heart, because he moved his limb, either his finger or his hand, in the manner he had mentioned to them. This indicates that after his head had been severed, he recalled in his heart what he had promised them and performed it as he had promised. If this story is authenticated, it is a sensory proof; and if it is not authenticated, then we have a textual (sam'i) proof. And what is the textual proof, O people? What is the sam'i proof? The textual proof, according to the scholars, is that which is established by the Book and the Sunnah.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 42, verse 25 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds, and He knows what you do﴾ [al-Shura 25].

He said: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance﴾. Allah, mighty and majestic, accepts the repentance of those who repent, and indeed He loves the repentance of those who repent, as Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 222]. So what is repentance (tawbah)?

Repentance is the return from disobedience of Allah to obedience of Allah, and it occurs in two forms: a comprehensive (kulliyyah) form and a specific (juz'iyyah) form.

The comprehensive form is that a person repents from every sin. Among this is the repentance of the disbeliever, which is comprehensive, whereby Allah, exalted be He, erases by it all that has passed of his sins, as the Most High said: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they cease, they will be forgiven what has already passed﴾ [al-Anfal 38]. The Muslim says: "O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness for all sins and I repent to You." This is the comprehensive form.

The specific form is that one repents from a particular sin, such as a person who has repented from consuming usury (riba) but who persists, may Allah protect us, in drinking wine. This is a specific, partial repentance, which is not all-encompassing, and the discussion of it will come soon, Allah willing.

Repentance has five conditions:
First: sincerity to Allah.
Second: regret over what one has done.
Third: giving up the sin.
Fourth: resolve not to return to it.
Fifth: that the repentance occurs before the doors are closed.

Five conditions: the first is sincerity, the second is regret, the third is giving up, the fourth is resolving not to return, and the fifth is that the repentance be within the time of possibility.

Sincerity means that what moves one to repent is the fear of Allah, mighty and majestic, and hope of drawing near to Him, so that one does not intend by it worldly gain, nor status, nor anything of Allah's creation; he desires only to attain the pleasure of Allah, mighty and majestic, and the abode of His honour. Sincerity, as you know, may Allah bless you, is a condition in every act.

The second: regret for the past sin, such that a person feels sorrow and grief over how this sin came from him. Regret is an emotion in the soul that arises from a person's own action and from other than his action, but our discussion concerns the regret in repentance that arises from his own action; meaning that he feels grief and remorse that the sin occurred from him, and his state is not like the state of one who has not sinned.

The third: giving up the sin. If it is a disobedience involving something forbidden, then he must avoid it; and if it is a neglect of an obligation, then he must perform it. On this basis, if someone claims he has repented from backbiting (ghibah) but he does not leave any opportunity for backbiting without backbiting, do we say he is repentant?

* Students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Why?
* Students: Because he has not given it up.
* The Shaykh: Because he has not given it up. Likewise, one who denies another person's property and refuses to return it, and says: "I am repentant," then he must return the property to its owner, otherwise his repentance is not accepted. And one who has backbitten a person, that is, mentioned him in his absence with what he dislikes, must give it up and seek the forgiveness of the one he backbit; he goes to him and says: "Forgive me, absolve me, for I have said about you a statement from which I have repented." This is necessary.

If he says: "If I go to him to seek his pardon, I fear he will think the matter greater than what I said, and enmity will result."

The answer: Even if that is so, you have cleared your duty. That enmity or the like results from it is not up to you. Yes, if it is supposed that your companion did not know of your backbiting against him, then here it suffices that you regret and give up backbiting him in the future, and that you mention him, in the gathering where you backbit him, with his good qualities.

The fourth?

* Students: The resolve.
* The Shaykh: The resolve not to return, by the heart settling that he will not return to this disobedience. If he has repented but is hesitant as to whether, should this disobedience become available to him, he would do it or not, then the repentance is not valid; he must resolve not to return.

If he returns, meaning he resolved not to return and then returned afterwards, does the repentance become void?

The answer: It is not void; the first repentance is valid, but he must renew repentance for the second sin. This is why the phrase is "resolve not to return," and not "on condition that he does not return." Is there a difference between them?

* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Be certain of the first.
* The student: There is a difference between them.
* The Shaykh: What is the difference?
* The student: The first, "resolve not to return," is not conditional (...) if he returns, his first repentance remains. But if we say "on condition that he does not return," if he returns, the repentance is void.
* The Shaykh: So this is the difference: if we say "resolve not to return," and he resolved not to return and then returned, the first repentance is valid, but he must renew repentance for the second sin. But if we say "on condition that he does not return," this implies that if he returned the repentance would be void, and that is not the case.

The fifth condition, and how great it is! That the repentance be within the time of possibility. If the time has passed, it does not benefit. The passing of the time is general and particular: the general is the rising of the sun from its west, and the particular is the arrival of death.

As for the first, its evidence is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, a soul will not benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or earned good through its faith﴾ [al-An'am 158]. The Prophet ﷺ explained some of the signs as the sun rising from its west. The Prophet (ﷺ) also said: "The migration will not cease until repentance ceases, and repentance will not cease until the sun rises from its west." [Narrated by Abu Dawud (2479) from the hadith of Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan.]

As for the particular, it is the arrival of the appointed term, for when death arrives repentance is not accepted, due to the saying of Allah, the Most High: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now," nor for those who die while they are disbelievers﴾ [al-Nisa 18]. The evidence is His saying: ﴿until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now."﴾ This condition entails that repentance must be immediate, without delay. The reason is that one does not know when death will come to him; he may die suddenly on his bed, or on his chair, or while prostrating or bowing. At that point it becomes clear that repentance is obligatory immediately. So hasten, O servant, rectify yourself, if the matter is between you and Allah or between you and the creation, for you do not know when death will come.

The summary: the conditions for accepting repentance that we enumerate are five:
First: sincerity to Allah, mighty and majestic.
Second: regret for the sin.
Third: giving up immediately.
Fourth: resolve not to return.
Fifth: that repentance be within the time of possibility.

We ask Allah for ourselves and for you repentance.

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾. The author said: (from among them), so he turned the meaning of ʿan ("from") to the meaning of min ("from among"), and this is based on what preceded, that particles of meaning alternate; that is, some of them take the place of others. But keeping the word on its apparent meaning is better, and ﴿accepts repentance from His servants﴾ is taken as implying the meaning "pardons them," so that ﴿accepts repentance from His servants﴾ means: He accepts it and pardons them, and we keep ʿan on its basic usage, and His saying ﴿and pardons misdeeds﴾ serves as an emphasis of what came before.

﴿accepts repentance from His servants﴾ (﴿and pardons misdeeds﴾ those from which one has repented). Pardon (ʿafw) is derived from the saying "the trace was effaced (ʿafa al-athar)" when the winds erased it, and it means overlooking punishment for sins.

﴿Sayyiʾat﴾ (misdeeds) is the plural of sayyiʾah, and it is everything that displeases a person in what he does or in what befalls him. What is meant by misdeeds here, meaning my explanation of them according to the wording, is opposition to the Sharia; everything that opposes the Sharia is a misdeed, whether by abandoning an obligation or committing a forbidden act.

﴿and He knows what you do﴾: some read it as "what they do" with the ya' and some with the ta'. As for the reading ﴿what they do﴾, it agrees with the preceding pronouns, meaning what the servants do. As for the reading with ta', it is a case of iltifat (shift) from third person absence to second person address. The style of iltifat is a rhetorical style, and its purpose is to alert the addressee to what will be presented to him; for when speech is in one uniform pattern, a person becomes accustomed to it and may become heedless, but when it varies, a person pauses and asks why the matter became so. The iltifat in the reading ﴿and He knows what you do﴾ is a shift from what to what? From absence to address.

Iltifat is a well-known art in rhetoric, and among its benefits is alerting the addressee. Consider the saying of Allah, the Most High: ﴿And Allah had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We sent up from among them twelve leaders﴾ [al-Ma'idah 12]. The context requires that He say "and He sent up from among them," but He said "and We sent up from among them," shifting from absence to first person speech in order to alert the addressee.

He said: ﴿and He knows what you do﴾. His knowledge of what we do includes knowledge of apparent things and hidden things. A person may commit an apparent sin that people know and that the Lord of the people, mighty and majestic, knows; and it may be hidden, unknown to people but known to Allah, blessed and exalted.

* A student: If the explanation of repentance (regret) is reported from some of the Companions and Successors, is it by way of mentioning the most important conditions, or by way of mentioning the greatest of them?
* The Shaykh: It is either by way of limiting the mention to some of the conditions, or they were addressing someone whom they knew had not regretted; he had come with a broad disposition, unconcerned and unbothered, so they focused on this condition without others.
* A student: Why was the author's explanation of His saying (...)?
* The Shaykh: It is an error; for he claimed that ﴿yakhtim﴾ means "bind upon your heart," and binding is a meaning that does not fit the context, and "yakhtim" does not come with the meaning of binding, but rather with the meaning of sealing, as Allah said: ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts﴾ [al-Baqarah 7], and He said: ﴿their hearts are sealed﴾ [al-Tawbah 87].
* A student: May we say: "Allah, the Exalted, expressed it with such-and-such a verse"?
* The Shaykh: Yes, it is permissible, because ʿibarah ("expression") means speech, and describing the actions of Allah is broad; regarding the actions of Allah, mighty and majestic, it is broad, and it is not of the category of names. Whatever may properly be attributed to Allah, express it.
* A student: What is the difference between "the expression (ʿibarah) of Allah's speech" and "the narration (hikayah) of Allah's speech"?
* The Shaykh: There is no clear difference, but the Ash'ariyyah say ʿibarah, and the Kullabiyyah say it is hikayah. ʿIbarah means that Allah created this sound to express what is in His self, while hikayah resembles what is known as an echo: if a person is among mountains and speaks, you find that all the mountains have a sound, relaying the sound. In any case, all false expressions are misdeeds, and Allah knows best.

* * *

Good. And here there is ﴿am﴾; is it connected (muttasilah) or disconnected (munqati'ah)?

* A student: (...) meaning "but" and the hamzah.
* The Shaykh: Yes. What is the difference between connected and disconnected?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: What is it?
* The student: (...) meaning "or."
* The Shaykh: Correct, meaning "or." Another point: the connected form must include two opposing things mentioned, whereas the disconnected form is that which means "but," and it does not require the combining of two similar things.

His saying, the Most High: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, we ask about the conditions of repentance in summary.

* A student: Repentance?
* The Shaykh: Yes, ten, five.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, one by one: sincerity to Allah, Most High; and second, regret..
* The student: Third: giving up the sin, and resolve not to (...), and that it be within the time of possibility.
* The Shaykh: Well done, five conditions.

What do you say about the repentance of a man who stole money from a person, then the one robbed disappeared and did not know of it, and he despaired of his return?

* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: He regretted, repented to Allah, and feared the punishment of Allah.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: He does not know where he is now; he does not know who.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: But he does not know about him; one condition was lost without his choice.
* A student: We say: his repentance is valid, but (...) with this money that he stole, not with the intention of reward and merit.
* The Shaykh: Yes, meaning his repentance is not complete unless he removes this stolen property from his ownership and gives it in charity, correct?

Good. If the one robbed was a disbeliever, how does he give it in charity on his behalf, when it is not accepted; charity does not benefit him?

* A student: The intention of charity is not for the disbeliever, but the intention of disowning this money.
* The Shaykh: That does not contradict. On what foundation does this follow?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Known; this is a condition, whether the owner is a Muslim or a disbeliever. But this I did not mention to you; this is placed in the public treasury (bayt al-mal), because the public treasury is the house for every property whose owner is unknown.

* * *

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds﴾ [al-Shura 25].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah's mercy toward His servants, in that He urges them to repent; its indication is in His saying: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, for this is not merely a report that Allah accepts, but an exhortation from Allah, mighty and majestic, that we repent to Allah. O Allah, grant us success in repentance, O Lord of the worlds. A parallel to this is my saying: "Whoever visits me, I will give him a hundred dirhams." The meaning of this is urging people to visit, and every person will eagerly come to visit. ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ is undoubtedly an exhortation to people to repent to Allah, mighty and majestic.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the manifestation of the generosity of the Lord, mighty and majestic, in that He accepts repentance from His servants whatever the sin. Read the saying of Allah, the Most High: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful"﴾ [al-Zumar 53]. Is repentance from disbelief accepted or not accepted?
* The students: Accepted.
* The Shaykh: Accepted, and Islam demolishes what came before it, however great it is, even one who reviled Allah or His Messenger and then embraced Islam, his repentance is accepted, due to the generality of the evidences. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they cease﴾, meaning: from their disbelief, ﴿they will be forgiven what has already passed﴾ [al-Anfal 38]. What has already passed from whom?
* The students: (...).
* The Shaykh: And even if it was great?
* The students: (...).
* The Shaykh: And even if it was great; because of His saying: ﴿what has already passed﴾. ﴿What﴾ is a relative pronoun that conveys generality. Even if this disbeliever killed a thousand believing men and then embraced Islam, Allah accepts his repentance. Therefore, when disbelievers embrace Islam after having destroyed the property of Muslims in war, are they made to compensate the Muslims' property? They are not made to compensate the Muslims' property, because Islam demolishes what came before it.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: an indication of the gentleness of Allah, blessed and exalted, in that He said: ﴿from His servants﴾, meaning, as if He, and Allah knows best, when they were His servants, treated them with gentleness, pardon and acceptance of repentance.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that when Allah accepts the repentance of a servant, He pardons his misdeeds however great they are; because of His saying: ﴿and pardons misdeeds﴾.
* And among the benefits of the noble verse: affirming the comprehensiveness of the knowledge of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, of everything we do; because of His saying, the Most High: ﴿and He knows what you do﴾.

From this benefit there branches the warning against disobedience. What is the reasoning for this?

* A student: A warning against disobedience?
* The Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: ﴿And He knows what you do.﴾
* The Shaykh: ﴿And He knows what you do﴾. Meaning: beware of doing anything that would anger Him, for He is All-Aware of you.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 42, verse 26 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [ash-Shura 26]. He said: (He gives them what they ask for). (Yastajību, "He responds") means yujību (He answers). Although it may occur to a person that the meaning of yastajību is yuti' (He obeys), as when you say: "I called upon so-and-so and he responded to me," meaning he obeyed me, here yastajību means yujību (He answers). The evidence for this interpretation is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿So their Lord responded to them: "Never will I allow to be lost the work of any worker among you, whether male or female; you are of one another"﴾ [Al 'Imran 195]. Therefore istajāba means ajāba, and ﴿yastajību﴾ means yujību.

So what is the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of (alladhīna, "those who")? In ﴿And He responds to those who﴾, (alladhīna) is the direct object (maf'ul bih), not the subject; the subject is a concealed pronoun referring to Allah.

﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: they believe with their hearts and do righteous deeds with their limbs. Faith and righteous deeds are always mentioned together, because each one is necessarily linked to the other; whoever truly believes will certainly do righteous deeds.

The evidence for this principle is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52) and Muslim (1599 / 107), from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.]

If they believe in what? In everything that faith in it is obligatory. And you know that the pillars of faith, which the Prophet (ﷺ) described, are: "Faith in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree, its good and its evil." [Narrated by Muslim (8 / 1) from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab.]

﴿Did righteous deeds﴾: "righteous" (ṣāliḥāt) is an adjective of a deleted noun, and the estimated phrase is "the righteous deeds." What is the criterion of a righteous deed? The criterion of a righteous deed is that it be sincere for Allah and in accordance with the Law (shari'ah) of Allah. This applies to the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ). But does it occur in earlier nations? The answer is yes: while their laws were in force, faith and righteous deeds occurred among them. So the criterion of a righteous deed is that it be sincere for Allah and conform to the Law of Allah.

Our saying "sincere for Allah" is to exclude any deed in which shirk occurs; such a deed is not righteous, even if the shirk is slight, because of the saying of Allah in the sacred hadith: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in regard to partnership. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his partnership." [Narrated by Muslim (2985 / 46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]

And (in accordance with the Law) means that it must be free of innovation (bid'ah). If there is innovation in it, it is not righteous, even if its parts are a righteous deed, for if it is an innovation it is not a righteous deed. That is, if someone introduces dhikr from the Qur'an or the Sunnah but in a form that the Law did not prescribe, it is not a righteous deed. A deed is not righteous unless it conforms to the Law in six matters: the cause, the quantity, the manner, the type, the time, and the place.

(The cause): that the deed be legislated for a specific cause. If a person introduces it for another cause, it is not accepted and is not righteous.

An example: we see some people who, when perfume is presented to them, say: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad." This is not a righteous deed.

If someone says: How can you say it is not a righteous deed, when it is a blessing upon the Messenger?

We say: Because it is not the guidance of the Messenger (ﷺ) that whenever he applied perfume he sent blessings upon the Prophet, nor did he command his nation to do so. So you have now established a cause that is not legislated.

And among this is that some people, when they belch, say: "Praise be to Allah." (Tajashshu', "belching") what does it mean? It is the release of wind from above; belching is this. Some people say, "Praise be to Allah." We say: Who told you that it is legislated to praise Allah when belching? Then your deed is not righteous, because it does not conform to the Law. And we say: it would follow from your view that when you pass wind you should praise Allah, and there is no evidence for this.

﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds, and increases them of His bounty; and as for the disbelievers, there is a severe punishment﴾. (Yastajību) means yujību. What is the evidence that yastajību means yujību? The saying of Allah: ﴿So their Lord responded to them: "Never will I allow to be lost the work of any worker among you, whether male or female; you are of one another"﴾.

On this meaning, what is the i'rab of ﴿alladhīna﴾? It is a direct object, built on the yā' in the accusative position.

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And the disbelievers, for them is a severe punishment﴾. This is a resumed (independent) sentence. When He mentioned what befalls those who believe and do righteous deeds, He mentioned what befalls their opposites, because the Noble Qur'an is paired (mathānī), in which meanings are repeated in pairs: Paradise is mentioned and then the Fire, reward and then punishment, the believer and then the disbeliever, and so on.

﴿And the disbelievers, for them is a severe punishment﴾. The kāfir (disbeliever) is originally one who denies, derived from al-kufurrā, which is the sheath of the date-palm spathe; but it is applied to everyone who disbelieves in Allah, the Exalted, by denial or otherwise, whether by denial, such as denying the messengership or the Qur'an, or by arrogance toward the religion of Allah, such as abandoning prayer, the abandonment of which is disbelief.

His saying: ﴿for them is a severe punishment﴾ is a subject and predicate. The predicate of the first subject, which is (al-kāfirūn, "the disbelievers"), is this phrase. The expression came in this form to emphasize their punishment, may Allah protect us; otherwise it would have sufficed to say: "and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment," or something similar. But Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the disbelievers, for them is a severe punishment﴾. Shadīd means strong and forceful. If you want to know this, read what the Qur'an and Sunnah say about the punishment of the people of the Fire.

We say: ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds, and increases them of His bounty﴾; that is, He gives them from His bounty in addition to what they did, for a good deed is rewarded tenfold, up to seven hundred times, and to many more multiples.

His saying: ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾ means they did righteous deeds, and a deed is not righteous except by conformity to the Law: first by sincerity to Allah, and second by conformity to the Law. Conformity is not realized unless the deed matches the Law in six matters:

First: the cause.

Second: the kind (jins), that it be of the kind that the Law brought; if it departs from this, it is not a righteous deed.

Its example: if someone sacrificed a horse, which is generally more expensive than a sheep, the sacrifice is not accepted. Why? Because sacrificing it is not of the kind legislated; sacrifice is only from livestock animals: camels, cattle, and sheep, as Allah said: ﴿and mention the name of Allah on known days over what He has provided them of the livestock animals﴾ [al-Hajj 28].

Third: that it conform to the Law in its quantity, so it does not exceed what the Law brought. For this reason, if a person added a unit of prayer (rak'ah), it is not a righteous deed, even if the rak'ah in itself is legislated, because in this case it is not legislated.

If someone says: What do you say if a person adds to the night prayer beyond eleven rak'ahs? Is the addition a righteous deed? If you say yes, it troubles us, because we said that it must conform to the Law in its quantity, I mean the act of worship. And it is known that "the Prophet (ﷺ) did not exceed eleven rak'ahs in Ramadan or otherwise," [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1147), and Muslim (738 / 125), from the hadith of 'A'ishah], and he sometimes prayed thirteen rak'ahs?

The answer: The night prayer has no fixed limit from the Prophet (ﷺ) such that he said: "Do not exceed such-and-such." Rather, he himself prayed eleven rak'ahs, and to the one who asked him about the night prayer he said: "Two by two. If you fear the dawn, pray one rak'ah which will make odd what you have prayed" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (472), and Muslim (749 / 145), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar]. His saying "two by two," without a limit, indicates that the night prayer has no limit; pray as many rak'ahs as you wish.

Fourth: that it conform to the Law in its time. If it contradicts the Law in time, it is not accepted.

Its example: a man sacrificed and slaughtered his sacrifice before the Eid prayer; this sacrifice is not valid.
