For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ), when told by someone that he had slaughtered before praying, said to him: "Your sheep is merely a sheep of meat" [al-Bukhari (955), from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib].

Fifth: that it conform to the Law in its place; that is, if the Lawgiver has specified an act of worship for a particular place, then performing it in another place is not accepted. Standing at 'Arafah: if a person stood at Muzdalifah instead of 'Arafah, this is not valid, because he stood in a place other than the one specified. And if a person performed i'tikaf (seclusion) in his house, the i'tikaf is not valid, because i'tikaf is restricted to the mosques.

Sixth: that it conform to the Law in its form (hay'ah); that is, the manner. If a person performed wudu' and washed his hands before his face, the wudu' is not valid, because it contradicts the Law in its form, since Allah says: ﴿So wash your faces and your hands﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6]. And if a person prayed and prostrated before bowing, then stood and bowed, the prayer is not valid, because of non-conformity to the Law in its form.

These are six things; an act of worship cannot conform to the Law unless these six things are realized.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the virtue of faith and righteous deeds, and that they are a cause of Allah's response.
* Among the benefits: that Allah gives the believers who do righteous deeds more than they did, by His saying: ﴿and increases them of His bounty﴾. This increase Allah explained in other places of His Book, when He said: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like﴾ [al-An'am 160], and He said: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes, in each spike a hundred grains; and Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah 261]. It may also be said that there is another increase beyond number: He increases them in faith and righteous deeds, because whenever a person does a righteous deed his certainty increases; for this reason it is the view of Ahl as-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah that deeds are included in faith.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that whatever good a person attains is by the bounty of Allah. On this basis, a person must cut off self-admiration for himself, and must not say: "This is from me," or "I deserve it," or similar words by which he boasts over Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a warning against disbelief, by His saying: ﴿and the disbelievers, for them is a severe punishment﴾, because the purpose of this sentence is not merely to inform of the severity of punishment for the disbelievers, but to explain this and to warn against disbelief out of fear of the severe punishment.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that Allah warns people against sins and disbelief by mentioning punishment. The scholars derived from this that when Allah mentions a punishment for an action, this indicates its prohibition, and when He mentions a reward for an action, this indicates its legislation.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you. We said that His saying ﴿of His servants﴾ [ash-Shura 25], that acceptance here includes the meaning of pardon (...). Is there repetition in the verse?
* The Shaykh: No, there is repetition, but it is emphasis in meaning (tawkid ma'nawi).
* Student: Shaykh, we learned among the rules of tafsir that interpreting a meaning as establishing new information (ta'sis) is preferable to interpreting it as emphasis (tawkid)...
* The Shaykh: Provided there is no evidence; that is, if this and that conflict, we interpret it as ta'sis without doubt, but the meaning has not conflicted.
* Student: Five conditions of repentance were established, and we also mentioned among the conditions that if the sin is related to the right of a human being, the right must be returned or forgiveness sought. We did not mention that among the five conditions. Is it included in one of them?
* The Shaykh: What do you say? He says: we did not mention that if the right belongs to a human being, it is necessary to seek his forgiveness or return it.
* Student: It is included, O Shaykh, in abandoning (al-iqla').
* The Shaykh: Did you hear? No, it is included, there is no problem.
* Student: If a person belches and says "Praise be to Allah" because the disbelievers laugh while you belch?
* The Shaykh: Who laughs?
* Student: The disbelievers; it is shameful among them?
* The Shaykh: It is shameful even among some Muslims. For this reason the jurists said: it is disliked for a person to raise his face toward the sky, except if he belches during prayer, then he may raise it, so as not to harm those around him with the smell. People do not understand what you mentioned at all. The elderly man or the old shaykh, when he belches and says "Praise be to Allah," does it occur to him that it is because of those who laugh? No, never; this is a sick and diseased cause whose cure is not hoped for.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, this reason is not correct; it is not correct always. The correct view is, for example, that if a person finds tightness in himself and sees himself needing to belch, he praises Allah; this is not because of the belching itself, but because of the removal of harm. This is for a reason.
* Student: May Allah be good to you, Shaykh, (...)?
* The Shaykh: It is necessary, again, that we know that ta'wil is used to mean tafsir, and this includes implication (tadmin). This is what the Messenger (ﷺ) meant when he said to Ibn 'Abbas: "O Allah, grant him understanding of the religion and teach him ta'wil" [al-Bukhari (143) and Ahmad (2397), the wording is his, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas]; that is, tafsir.
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, this is not called ta'wil; this is called tahrif (distortion), and we may not call it ta'wil. Even if they call it ta'wil, they say "ta'wil" so that people will not be repelled by their practice. If they said, "the people of distortion," would anyone accept them, or not? No one would accept them. So they brought the term "ta'wil" as a softening. There are similar cases: the Christians at the end named themselves "Messianic" (masihiyyun) to lend their abrogated religion the appearance of legitimacy and to claim they are followers of the Messiah, and the Messiah, peace be upon him, was far removed from them, and if he came out he would fight them, and they lie about the Messiah in what they claim; but they named themselves "Christians" in order to give themselves legitimacy.
Similarly, the Rafidah reject the name "Rafidah" and become angry with you, so they named themselves "Shi'ah." And who is more deserving of being called Shi'ah? Ahl as-Sunnah, because they are the ones who love the People of the House with the sunnah-based, lawful love. As for these Rafidah, they love the family of the House with a love involving shirk; the People of the House disavow them without doubt. For this reason, when 'Abd Allah ibn Saba' and his group said to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, "You are truly God," he disavowed them and ordered trenches to be dug, which were dug and filled with firewood, and he threw them into the fire, burning them because of how severely they had affected him.
So should those who exaggerated about the People of the House, raising them above their station, be called Shi'ah of the People of the House? Never, by Allah. They are the greatest enemies of the People of the House, because they raised them above their station. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I do not like that you raise me above the station which Allah has given me" [Ahmad (12551), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik]; and the People of the House, like the Prophet (ﷺ), do not like to be raised above the station Allah has given them. Never. Have you understood now?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, if the evidence indicates it, it is ta'wil; if the evidence does not indicate it, it is tahrif. This is the criterion.
* Student: Whoever kills a person by a disbeliever outside of war, is he liable for compensation if the disbeliever becomes Muslim?

The shaykh said: Originally, the disbeliever is a combatant (harbi) so long as there is no treaty between us and him. So we may kill him, and he may kill us. That is, "he may" means that if he kills us, he is not liable. Otherwise, it would be forbidden for him to kill us, just as it is forbidden for me to disbelieve. For this reason, the stronger opinion is that disbelievers are addressed by the branches of the Sharia (furu' al-shari'ah, the detailed rulings) just as they are addressed by tawhid (monotheism). Indeed, I say that the disbeliever is sinful even in what is permissible. Now, the disbeliever eats and drinks, feels safe and dresses, and for every blessing he is punished in addition to the punishment for disbelief. Allah says: ﴿Let not the movement of those who disbelieve through the land deceive you. It is a little enjoyment; then their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ [Aal 'Imran 196-197]. When the people of the Fire are asked: ﴿"What has caused you to enter Saqar?" They will say: "We were not of those who prayed, and we did not feed the poor, and we used to engage in vain discourse with those who engaged in it, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment, until there came to us the certainty"﴾ [al-Muddaththir 42-47]. Therefore, they are sinful. The Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾ [al-Ma'idah 93], while others are blamed. And the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Say: "Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?" Say: "They are for those who believed in the worldly life, purely for them on the Day of Resurrection"﴾ [al-A'raf 32]. They are for those who believed, while for those who did not believe, these are neither theirs nor purely theirs on the Day of Resurrection. Pay attention, my brothers: the disbeliever is the enemy of Allah. Had this world been worth the wing of a mosquito in Allah's sight, He would not have given a disbeliever a single sip of water from it. So when they eat, drink, feel safe, are healthy, or receive any blessing, they are punished for it.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if Allah had extended provision for His servants, they would surely have rebelled throughout the earth﴾. "Basṭ" (extending) means "wus'" (widening), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah withholds and extends﴾ [al-Baqarah 245], and the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿He extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it﴾ [ash-Shura 12]; i.e., He constricts. So basṭ means tawsīr (widening); meaning, if Allah widened provision for the servants, they would rebel throughout the earth.

As for His saying ﴿for His servants﴾, the commentator (al-mufassir) said: "(all of them)", meaning: if all people were wealthy, provision would be extended to them, and they would rebel throughout the earth. He said: "(﴿they would rebel﴾ all of them ﴿throughout the earth﴾; i.e., they would transgress therein)" and exceed their limits. This is because all of them would be in ease and in abundant provision, with no restraint, no lesson, and no admonition. Moreover, if Allah extended provision to all the servants, the world would be corrupted; for were it not for this difference among the servants in provision, no one would serve another and affairs would not be set right. If people were all on one level of wealth, and you asked a person to work for you, he would not comply. Why? Because he is self-sufficient with what he has. But Allah, blessed and exalted, has favored some people over others and raised some of them above others in degrees, so that some may take others in service (sukhriyyan).

This is what the author (al-Mu'allif) held. However, it may be said: Allah's saying ﴿And if Allah had extended provision for His servants﴾ encompasses either all of them or individuals. When Allah extends provision to a person, he rebels and becomes self-sufficient; this is why you find that most of those who denied the prophets were the wealthy chieftains and the great ones, whereas the poor and weak were mostly those who followed the prophets. Thus the intended meaning of ﴿And if Allah had extended provision for His servants﴾ is the genus; i.e., if He extended it to even one of His servants, that one would rebel throughout the earth.

﴿But He sends down in measure what He wills﴾. He said: "(﴿sends down﴾ with takhfīf [the lightened form] and its opposite)." What is its opposite? Tashdīd (the doubled form): ﴿yunazzilu﴾ and ﴿yunzilu﴾; ﴿yunazzilu﴾ is from nazzala, and ﴿yunzilu﴾ is from anzala. The author's, may Allah have mercy on him, convention is that when he gives such an expression, both readings are of the seven canonical readings; likewise when he says "(and in a reading)", both readings are of the seven. But if he says "(and it was read)", the reading is shādh (irregular), because he used it in the passive, impersonal form. Pay attention to the terminology. The expression here, "(with takhfīf and its opposite)", is on the same footing; i.e., he equated the two readings, and on this basis both are canonical.

He said: "(of provisions)" is an explanation of what is sent down; the implied object is therefore "of provisions", and what shows that the implied object is "of provisions" is His saying ﴿And if Allah had extended provision﴾ and ﴿but He sends down in measure﴾; i.e., with a decree written from eternity that does not change or alter.

("﴿what He wills﴾, so He extends it to some of His servants and not to others, and rebellion arises from extension.") His saying ﴿in measure what He wills﴾: this willing, as already mentioned, is joined with wisdom. Whoever Allah's wisdom requires He make wealthy, He makes wealthy; whoever Allah's wisdom requires He make poor, He makes poor. In a sacred hadith: "Among My servants is one who, if I made him wealthy, wealth would corrupt him, and among My servants is one who, if I made him poor, poverty would corrupt him" [narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat (231) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik]. Allah, blessed and exalted, is All-Wise, and how many a person has returned to Allah because of calamities, such as poverty, the death of a close relative or friend, or the like: ﴿what He wills﴾.

The author, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said: ("so He extends it to some of His servants and not to others, and rebellion arises from extension"). That is, the distribution of provision (rebellion, al-baghy). This is given as a rationale for the answer ﴿And if Allah had extended provision for His servants, they would surely have rebelled﴾: that rebellion, transgression, arrogance toward worship and denial of the truth arise from extension.

﴿Indeed He is, of His servants, All-Aware, All-Seeing﴾. This sentence is a resumptive clause (isti'nafiyyah) explaining that His extending or withholding provision arises from knowledge and expertise. Khibrah (expertise) is more specific than 'ilm (knowledge), since it is knowledge of the inner realities of matters. However, we say: knowledge of inner realities implies, by necessary inference, knowledge of outward matters a fortiori.

Baṣīr is derived from seeing with the eye (al-ibsār) and from baṣīrah, which is knowledge, so baṣīr has two meanings: the first from seeing, which is sight with the eye, and the second from baṣīrah, which is knowledge. ﴿Indeed He is, of His servants, All-Aware, All-Seeing﴾, and this means He restricts whom He wills and extends to whom He wills.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the extending and restricting of provision is from Allah alone; by His saying ﴿And if Allah had extended provision for His servants, they would surely have rebelled throughout the earth﴾.

If someone says: Is this not objected to by the fact that we see a man work, toil and trade, and his wealth increases?

We reply: It is not an objection, because the origin of his work is from Allah the Mighty and Majestic; it is He who placed the intention in his heart and enabled him to work, so it is from the bounty of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. This is one answer.

Another answer: we find some people who toil, work and exert themselves yet are not granted success; whenever they try one thing, they suffer more loss. In that case the objection is entirely dispelled.

The objection? It is raised against us that a person may trade, work and earn, so that the extension of his provision results from his own work; how then do you say that the extension of provision is from Allah the Mighty and Majestic? This is the objection. What is the answer?

* A student: We say: the decree is itself a bounty of Allah the Mighty and Majestic upon the servant.

* The Shaykh: That is, Allah, blessed and exalted, placed in his heart the resolve to do this and facilitated this trade for him; it is from Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Had Allah willed, He would not have placed the resolve in his heart, and had Allah willed, He would have rendered him unable to work. This is one answer. Another answer?

* A student: The other answer is that we see in reality someone who toils and earns, and someone who toils and does not earn.

* The Shaykh: Yes, we see in reality someone who exerts effort and energy in trade, in taking and giving, yet he only increases in loss. Therefore the extension is entirely from Allah the Mighty and Majestic, neither from its origin nor from what branches from it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: caution against luxury and abundance of provision. The reason is that Allah the Exalted informed us that extending provision is a cause of rebellion, as in His saying: ﴿Nay, indeed man does transgress (6), when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-'Alaq 6-7]; and the Prophet ﷺ informed us: "What I fear most for you is what will be opened up for you of the splendour of this world" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1465) and Muslim (1052/122) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri]. So a person should beware of the provision extended to him, for perhaps his misery will be caused by it; we ask Allah for safety and well-being.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the wisdom of Allah, blessed and exalted, in what He sends down of provision; by His saying ﴿But He sends down in measure what He wills﴾.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of Allah's will, blessed and exalted, even in what befalls the servant.

* Among its benefits: an indication that the extending of provision to one person and restricting it for another is based on expertise and knowledge; by His saying ﴿Indeed He is, of His servants, All-Aware, All-Seeing﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 42, verse 28:

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain (al-ghayth)﴾. From where does He send it down? From the sky. ﴿Al-ghayth (the rain that brings relief)﴾, meaning that by which relief (al-ighathah) is obtained, and it is rescue from hardship. ﴿After they had despaired﴾, meaning after the servants had despaired. The commentator (al-mufassir) said: (﴿al-ghayth﴾ the rain, ﴿after they had despaired﴾, meaning they had lost hope of its descent), because it was delayed beyond its time. They said: "So this year there will be no rain." Then God sends down the rain, and the sending down of rain at a time of anxiety for it and despair of its descent has a stronger effect on souls and is clearer evidence of the mercy and bounty of Allah, blessed and exalted.

He said: (﴿And He spreads His mercy﴾, meaning He spreads out His rain). This is what the commentator said, but if what was meant were as he said, it would have said: (He sends down the rain after they had despaired and spreads it out). Rather, the correct reading is: He spreads His mercy; that is, the mercy that is produced by this rain: the growth of crops, the milk of udders, abundance of provision, and other things that arise from rain.

Some scholars said: ﴿He spreads His mercy﴾; that is, He makes the sky clear until the sun comes out. But this is open to question, except when the rains reach a level that their harm is feared; then the clearing of the clouds and the emergence of the sun is mercy. As for the mere emergence of the sun and the clearing of the clouds, it is not mercy but wisdom. We know that Allah, exalted, does this for a wisdom. ﴿And He spreads His mercy﴾, so the matter is more general than what the author mentioned.

(﴿And He is the Walī (protector)﴾, the one who does good to the believers, ﴿the Praiseworthy (al-Ḥamīd)﴾, the one praised by them.) As for his saying: (﴿al-Walī﴾, the one who does good to the believers), he explained wilāyah (guardianship) as ihsān (benevolence), but the correct view is that wilāyah is more general. So His saying ﴿And He is the Walī﴾ means: the one who manages the affairs of His servants. And His saying ﴿al-Ḥamīd﴾ means: the one praised for this guardianship, because it is a guardianship of mercy, wisdom and justice, so He is praised for it.

If Allah is the Walī, to whom does one turn when affairs become straitened? One turns to Allah, may He be exalted, because He is the Walī, just as the orphan returns to his guardian in managing his wealth.

As for His saying ﴿al-Ḥamīd﴾, it means: the one praised for His guardianship. The guardianship of Allah, blessed and exalted, is divided into two kinds from which it does not depart: either benevolence or justice. The third, which is impossible, is injustice. So the guardianship of Allah does not go beyond these two matters, namely benevolence and justice.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: that the sending down of rain is in the hand of Allah, may He be exalted, by His saying: ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain﴾.

* And from its benefits: that with the sending down of rain hardship is removed, because al-ghayth is the removal of hardship.

* And from the benefits of the noble verse: that it is the nature of man that he does not endure patiently, so despair and loss of hope in the mercy of Allah overcome him. What is obligatory upon a person is that he not despair of the mercy of Allah, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾ [az-Zumar 53], and He said of Ibrahim: ﴿And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except the astray?﴾ [al-Hijr 56]. So it is obligatory upon you, when harm touches you, not to despair; it is obligatory that you be patient and seek reward, and that a state should persist is impossible. But Allah, blessed and exalted, mentions things according to what actually happens, not according to what befits a person in constant patience and awaiting relief.

* And from the benefits of the noble verse: that the descent of rain is mercy, by His saying: ﴿And He spreads His mercy﴾ [ash-Shura 28]. This is according to the author's explanation that by mercy is meant rain, but we have mentioned that mercy is more general than that, and so it includes the sending down of rain, the growth of the earth, the fattening of livestock, and the abundance of activity and movement.

* And from the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the guardianship of Allah over all creation, by His saying: ﴿And He is the Walī﴾, without restriction.

Know that the guardianship of Allah, exalted, is of two kinds: special guardianship and general guardianship.

General guardianship is that which includes the guardianship of Allah, glorified and exalted, over all servants: believer and disbeliever, righteous and wicked, young and old, male and female. This is general, and among it is His saying, exalted: ﴿Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master (mawlāhumu al-Ḥaqq)﴾ [al-An'am 62]. This is among the general guardianships, because what is meant by them are the disbelievers.

Special guardianship is that which belongs to the believers only, and its evidence is the saying of Allah, exalted: ﴿Allah is the Walī of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light. And those who disbelieve, their protectors are the Ṭāghūt; they bring them out of light into darkness﴾ [al-Baqarah 257].

So what is the difference between the special and the general? The difference between them in terms of the locus is clear: general guardianship includes everyone, special guardianship is for the believers. The difference between them also in terms of effect or influence: special guardianship necessitates Allah's granting success to the servant in guidance and other things, whereas general guardianship does not necessitate that, for the disbelievers have Allah as their Walī in the general sense, yet He did not guide them, because wisdom requires that He not guide them.

* And from the benefits of the noble verse: that the guardianship of Allah, exalted, is praiseworthy in every state, by His saying: ﴿al-Walī al-Ḥamīd﴾. Compare this with His saying, exalted: ﴿He is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghanī), the Praiseworthy (al-Ḥamīd)﴾ [Fatir 15], and you will find complete harmony. So the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy, is praised for His self-sufficiency, such that by it He enriches whom He wills; and the Walī, the Praiseworthy, is praised for His guardianship, such that He specifies special guardianship for whom He wills and withholds it from whom He wills. In every state His guardianship is praiseworthy, and His self-sufficiency is praiseworthy, may He be exalted.

* Student: Are both correct?

* Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: And there is no preference for one of them, so that both are taken together?

* Shaykh: On condition that they do not contradict each other. Here they contradict.

* Student: What is the reason, Shaykh?

* Shaykh: The reason is that if we say ﴿yastajību﴾ refers back to Allah, exalted, then (alladhīna) takes the accusative position, meaning they are the ones being answered. And if we say that it refers back to Allah, then (alladhīna) becomes the direct object.

Also, the second view is weakened: that ﴿yastajību alladhīna āmanū﴾ means that those who are the ones who responded to their Lord. His saying ﴿and He increases them from His bounty﴾ weakens it, for the principle is that pronouns are one referent, and it is known that increase from bounty belongs specifically to Allah, exalted. So the claim that it bears the second meaning is weak, because it is outweighed.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you well, regarding His saying: ﴿And if Allah had expanded provision for His servants, they would have transgressed in the earth﴾, some have mentioned that a poor person whom Allah has made poor in His wisdom, it is not permissible for anyone to make him rich (...), meaning giving him something by which he becomes self-sufficient, only that he eats. Is your giving him what makes him self-sufficient a breach of manners with Allah, glorified and exalted?

* Shaykh: Who said this?!

* Student: They mentioned it in a book of the Sufis sanctifying individuals. Is this a fatwa from one of the scholars?

* Shaykh: No consideration is given to the statements of the Sufis. Were you a Sufi before?

* Student: Yes, I was a Sufi.

* Shaykh: Praise be to Allah who rescued you from them. This is a great blessing. This is not correct, because if it were so, Allah would not have given the poor a share of zakat. Did not Allah make a share of zakat for the poor? And command kindness to the poor? So the weakness of this view is clear.

* Student: What is the difference between yaʾs (despair) and qunūṭ (despair/loss of hope)?

* Shaykh: Qunūṭ is the intensification of yaʾs; that is, when yaʾs rises until no hope remains in the person, this is qunūṭ.

* Student: Is it conjoined to it (by 'atf)?

* Shaykh: No, (alladhīna) is the direct object.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Also, the preference for our view, that the one who answers is Allah, is His saying: ﴿and He increases them from His bounty﴾. If it were so, He would have said: "fa-yazīduhum" with the fa (so, then). "Those who believe and do righteous deeds are answered, so He increases them when they respond." But since the conjunction came that requires the equality of the conjoined and what it is conjoined to, what you said is not sound. Otherwise He would have said: "And He answers those who believe and do righteous deeds, so He increases them," meaning: because of their response He increases them from His bounty.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: And regarding the answering, Allah, exalted, said: ﴿So their Lord answered them﴾ [Al 'Imran 195], meaning: He responded to them.

This is from qunūṭ: when a person is struck by a distress and judges in himself that it cannot be removed, this is qunūṭ without doubt. But if he judges in himself that it cannot be removed by a created being, this is true, and there is no objection to it, because some illnesses, for example, are known to be impossible for creatures to remove. But they may be removed by the permission of Allah, exalted.

It is related to us that some reciters whom Allah has granted faith and piety recite over one afflicted with cancer, and he is cured by the permission of Allah, while cancer, according to sensory medicine, is regarded as one of the incurable diseases. So despair that this distress will be removed at the hand of a creature is true and there is no harm in it. But from the Creator it is not permissible, because Allah is over all things capable. The One who created you from a despised water is able to heal you from this illness, for example. The One who brought you out of your mother's womb with no clothing, until Allah provided you with clothes, is able to clothe you with wealth after poverty. So do not despair of the mercy of Allah ever. Await relief, but be patient; do not hasten matters, for Allah, exalted, has made for everything a sunnah and a way by which it comes in the end.

* * *

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they had despaired, and spreads His mercy, and He is the Walī, the Praiseworthy﴾. What is meant by al-ghayth?
* Student: That by which relief is obtained.

* Shaykh: And here?

* Student: The rain.

* Shaykh: And it is the rain. Is there a difference between al-ghayth and al-maṭar (rain)?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: What is it?

* Student: Al-ghayth is that by which hardship is removed.

* Shaykh: By which hardship is removed.

* Student: And rain may fall without hardship being removed by it.

* Shaykh: Good, and hardship is not removed by it. Is there evidence for this?

* Student: The saying of the Prophet: "Drought is not that you are not rained upon."

* Shaykh: The saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Drought is not that you are not rained upon; rather, drought is that you are rained upon, yet the earth produces nothing"[[Recorded by Muslim (2904/44) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]]. His saying: ﴿after they had despaired﴾. Is there in this an affirmation of despair and that it is permissible, or a statement of the reality?

* Student: A statement of the reality.

* Shaykh: A statement of the reality, because the legal ruling on despair is what?

* Student: It is not permissible.

* Shaykh: It is not permissible; rather, it is among the major sins. Good. Reporting a reality does not mean approving it. And the evidence for this?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: The saying of the Prophet: "There will certainly be among my ummah peoples who consider adultery, silk, and musical instruments lawful"[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (5590) from the hadith of Abu 'Amir or Abu Malik al-Ash'ari.]], and his saying: "You will certainly follow the ways of those before you"[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (7320) and al-Hakim (8610), the wording is his, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]], meaning the Jews and Christians, and his report that "a woman will travel from one place to another fearing none but Allah"[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (3595) from the hadith of 'Adi ibn Hatim.]]. This reporting of a reality does not imply its permissibility or approval.

The guardianship of Allah, blessed and exalted, is divided into general and special. The special is specific to whom? To the believers. What is the evidence? His saying, exalted: ﴿Allah is the Walī of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light﴾ [al-Baqarah 257]. The general guardianship is His saying: ﴿Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master﴾ [al-An'am 62], and it is general to all people.

﴿al-Ḥamīd﴾ is a form of (faʿīl) in the sense of (mafʿūl, passive): the praised. Is there in the Arabic language a form (faʿīl) in the sense of (mafʿūl)? (qatīl) in the sense of (maqtūl, killed). So, meaning that Allah is praised for His guardianship; (ḥamīd) means praised for His guardianship. Thus everything He carries out in His dominion is praiseworthy.

What did the Prophet ﷺ say when something displeasing befell him? He said: "All praise is due to Allah in every state." And when something pleasing befell him he said: "All praise is due to Allah, by whose blessing good deeds are completed"[[Recorded by Ibn Majah (3803) from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]]. As for what some ignorant people say: "Praise be to Allah, who is not praised for anything disliked except Him," this is an innovated expression that is not permissible, because it indicates a person's aversion to what Allah, exalted, does; furthermore, there is a contradiction between "disliked" and "praiseworthy." Moreover, a person is obligated to be content with everything Allah, exalted, decrees, because among faith is belief in divine decree, its good and its bad.

The point is that this is an innovated expression that is forbidden, and it is said to whoever says it: say what the Messenger, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, said: "All praise is due to Allah in every state."

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 42, verse 29:

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾. (Min) is for partitive meaning. Ayat is the plural of ayah, which is the specific sign that points to and distinguishes the thing it belongs to; the sign that identifies and defines a thing is called an ayah. (Among the signs of Allah) means: among His signs that indicate the perfection of His power, Mighty and Majestic, and the perfection of His dominion, is the creation of the heavens and the earth, for no one can create the likes of them. The discussion of "the heavens and the earth," why the first was put in the plural and the second in the singular, and similar matters, has already been covered.

(And the creation of ﴿what He has scattered﴾, that is, spread out and dispersed, ﴿in them﴾) meaning: in the heavens and the earth, (﴿of living creatures﴾, which is what crawls upon the earth). The words ﴿what He has scattered﴾ mean: what He created. (Baththa) means to disperse and spread out. ﴿In them﴾ means: in the heavens and the earth. ﴿Of living creatures﴾ means: of what crawls upon the earth, of humans and others. This too is among the signs of Allah. Among the signs of Allah in these creatures is that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, gave everything its nature and then guided it. You find animals, which are dumb and have no intellect, earning their sustenance and going out to seek it, and storing what is stored of food if it is of the kind that is stored. You find them yearning for their young, showing mercy to their offspring, and hungering so that their young may be satisfied. And other such things, which if you reflect upon them, you will marvel at these dumb creatures.

Allah gave birds a strong power of distant sight, as evidenced by the fact that they see grain while they are in the air of the sky, and no human sees this without doubt. But since birds do not walk on the earth, Allah made easy for them a piercing, strong sight, so that they see the grain while in the air of the sky, then descend, take it, and fly off, along with other wondrous signs.

Consider, for example, the tiny ant, how it finds its way to its burrow even when it comes from afar. Then it walks along a single line. We have witnessed with our own eyes it walking in a single line over a cloth on which there is no trace of dust; you find it reaching the end and then turning at an angle. How did it find its way to this? Only by the guidance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It has been said that whenever it walks, a substance comes out of it, which the other ant smells, so it follows its trail. This is among the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

You find the ant, which is larger than the tiny ant, eager to bring its provisions from afar and then store them in its burrow. When it wants to store the grain, it eats the heads of the grains so that they do not sprout, for if the grain remained with its heads, it would sprout and spoil for it. So you find it nibbling the top and bottom of the grain so that it does not sprout. Then, when the rain comes and the earth becomes moist and the dampness reaches its burrow, you find it moving this grain out into the sun and the air until it dries. Who taught it? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, without doubt. So it is among the signs of Allah.

How excellent it is to aid oneself in this by reading the book Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah by Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him. This Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah mentions wonders, including a story: that a man placed bait for one of the tiny ants, either meat or something else. The ant tried to carry it but was unable, so it returned to its burrow and sought help from its sisters, and they came to him in a rush. When they came to it, he removed it from the ground, so the ants went searching for it but found nothing, and they dispersed, leaving only the first one that had guided them to it. He placed the bait again, and when she was certain of it, she went back to her people and summoned them, and when they came, he removed it; they searched for it but did not find it, and they returned. Then he placed the bait a third time, and this ant was certain of it, then went back to her people to alarm them. When they came, he removed it; when they searched and did not find it, they devoured this ant completely, tearing her limb from limb. He said: I related this to Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, marveling at it, and he said: Yes, every creature is instinctively inclined to punish the wrongdoer and the liar, and this one lied to them and wronged them, so there was nothing left but that she be destroyed, for whoever strives in the earth to cause corruption must be executed, even a human being.

But I ask you: is there blood money for this killed ant, the man? Yes, he wronged her. We ask Allah to pardon him.

In any case, my purpose in this is that everything Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has guided for what He created, even the ant. I witnessed myself, in the basin of a palm tree, when the palm was watered, water entered from beneath the earth into the ant's burrow, so the ants began carrying their white eggs quickly until they removed them from the water. Who guided them to this? Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

The signs of Allah are many, and for this reason He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿and what He has scattered in them of living creatures﴾, and in another verse: ﴿and what He scatters of living creatures﴾ [al-Jathiyah 4]. So He used the past tense and used the present tense, which indicates continuity.

His statement: (﴿of living creatures﴾, which is what crawls upon the earth, of people and others, ﴿and He is, over their gathering﴾ for the assembly, ﴿when He wills﴾ to gather them, ﴿All-Powerful﴾). ﴿And He is, over their gathering﴾ means: over the gathering of these creatures. ﴿When He wills﴾ means: when He wills to gather them. The object is omitted, indicated by the context. ﴿All-Powerful﴾ means: nothing can overpower Him. The commentator, may Allah have mercy on him, says: (In the pronoun there is precedence of the rational). The pronoun, meaning in ﴿their gathering﴾, is the precedence of the rational, because the mim that indicates the plural is only used for rational beings, while for non-rational beings the pronoun of feminine plurality is used. But here the plural pronoun is used even though most of what crawls on the earth is non-rational. Yet the author, may Allah have mercy on him, says: (a precedence for the rational).

* In this noble verse: a clarification that the Creator of the heavens and the earth is Allah, as His saying: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, and no one shares with Him in that.

* And among its benefits: these creatures are among the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But, our brothers, it becomes clear that they are signs of Allah only through reflection and contemplation, for we have grown accustomed to these creatures: we are accustomed to the sunrise and sunset, and the rising and setting of the moon, so that does not stir our hearts because it is a familiar thing. But if we reflected upon these creatures, it would become clear to us that they are among the great signs of Allah.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that among the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is what is scattered in the heavens and the earth of living creatures, of humans and non-humans, for in each of them there is a sign indicating the perfection of His oneness, Mighty and Majestic, His mercy and His wisdom.

* And among the benefits: the apparent meaning of the verse is that there are living creatures in the heavens; as His saying: ﴿and what He has scattered in them of living creatures﴾. As for the earth, its creatures are known to us, most of them known to us, which we recognize and witness. As for the heavens, there are living creatures in them, but we do not know what they are.

If you say: (the angels), this presents a difficulty. If you say: other than the angels, we say: Allah is over all things Powerful. For Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made clear that the angels have wings, saying: ﴿the Originator of the angels, messengers with wings, two and three and four﴾ [Fatir 1], and one with wings can fly, and perhaps also walks.

In any case, we are only obligated to what we understand from the apparent meaning of the verse and we do not go beyond that. So we say: the apparent meaning of the noble verse is that the heavens contain living creatures as the earth does, and if a questioner asks us: what are these living creatures? We say: either the angels or others; Allah knows best.

Some scholars said: ﴿and what He has scattered in them of living creatures﴾ means: on the earth, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting together﴾ [al-Rahman 19] up to His saying: ﴿from them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾ [al-Rahman 22]. They claimed that this happens only in salt water. The correct view is that the verse of al-Rahman is on its apparent meaning: ﴿from them comes forth﴾, and that both the salt and the sweet seas produce pearls and coral, though more is found in one of them.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the perfection of Allah's power, Mighty and Majestic, in gathering these creatures for the Day of Reckoning; as His saying: ﴿And He is, over their gathering when He wills, All-Powerful﴾.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: a refutation of those deniers of resurrection who said: ﴿Bring us our fathers, if you are truthful﴾ [al-Jathiyah 25]. The deniers of resurrection say: if you are truthful, produce our fathers. It is said in reply: Allah, Exalted, has not willed that now, but He will will it later; and you have not been told that you are gathered today, rather it was said: ﴿Indeed, the first and the last are gathered to the appointed time of a known day﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 49-50]. As for challenging them with what the speaker did not commit to, this is wasted and purposeless.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the perfection of the power of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in gathering these creatures.

If it is said: Does the verse indicate that the power is restricted by will?

The answer: No, for what is restricted by will is not the power but the gathering. By this we know that some people who say: He is All-Powerful over what He wills have made a grave error and restricted what Allah has left unrestricted; for Allah said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things Powerful﴾ [al-Baqarah 20], over what He wills and what He does not will. These people say: He is All-Powerful over what He wills, placing the object first, and placing the object first implies restriction. So He is powerful over what He wills, and as for what He does not will, He is not powerful over it. This is a grave error. Allah is capable of all things, what He wills and what He does not will.

So should we forbid one whom we hear saying it? Yes, we forbid him from that and say: "O brother, say what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, He is over all things Powerful﴾ [Fussilat 39]; do not say: He is All-Powerful over what He wills." We ask Allah, Exalted, to gather us and you in His mercy, and to grant us and you success in what He loves and is pleased with.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned﴾ [ash-Shura 30].

His statement: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you﴾ — this "ma" is a conditional particle, I mean (ma), and its response is ﴿it is because of what your hands have earned﴾. His statement ﴿it is because of what your hands have earned﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, and the estimated reading is: "so it is because of what your hands have earned." The commentator says: (﴿And whatever affliction befalls you﴾ is addressed to the believers. ﴿Of affliction﴾ is an explanation of (ma). He said: (calamity and hardship. ﴿It is because of what your hands have earned﴾, i.e., what you have earned of sins; but He expressed it by the hands, because most actions are carried out by them. ﴿And He pardons much﴾ [ash-Shura 30] of it, so He does not requite for it, and He, the Exalted, is too generous to repeat the requital in the Hereafter. As for those who are not sinners, what befalls them in this world is to raise their ranks in the Hereafter.)

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you﴾. The commentator restricted this to the believers. The reason for the restriction is that He said: ﴿And He pardons much﴾, and disbelievers are not deserving of pardon. As for his words ﴿of affliction﴾, he said: (calamity and hardship), and it includes religious afflictions and worldly afflictions. Which of them is greater? Religious afflictions, for they are greater than worldly afflictions. So if it is assumed that someone is afflicted with a downfall, God forbid, it is worse than that his family and wealth are destroyed; for religious afflictions are far greater than worldly afflictions, since worldly afflictions pass away and are forgotten. As one of them said: "Either you endure with the endurance of the noble, or you console yourself with the consolation of animals; it must pass away." Religious afflictions, God forbid, are a loss in this world and the Hereafter.

If someone says: What is the evidence that turning away is an affliction? The evidence is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿So if they turn away, know that Allah only intends to afflict them for some of their sins﴾ [al-Ma'idah 49]. Reflect that sins became the cause of their turning away, and turning away is a great affliction. The point is that His saying ﴿of affliction﴾ includes worldly afflictions, such as the loss of wealth, the death of loved ones, fear, poverty and the like; and religious afflictions, such as sins and innovations, aversion to the truth, aversion to the people of the truth, and the like. All of it is ﴿because of what your hands have earned﴾, and the meaning is: because of what you have earned. For earning may be done by the hand, may be done by the foot, may be done by the eye, may be done by the nose, may be done by the tongue; but He expressed the whole by the hands, because most works are carried out by the hand. Now, in our sitting here, does the hand act or not? It does not act? The hand certainly acts: it takes the book, lifts it, lowers it, writes. So most works are carried out by the hand, and thus He expressed the self by the hand for this reason. ﴿Because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾, meaning He pardons much of what you have sinned, so He does not call you to account for it.

In this verse there are benefits:
* Among them: the affirmation of causes, by His saying: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned﴾. The basis for this is that the "bi" here indicates causation, so it affirms causes.

The affirmation of causes is established by the Law, by reason and by the senses, and denying it is misguidance in religion and foolishness in intellect. I say: the effect of causes is established by the Law, reason and the senses, three proofs; and denying it is misguidance in religion and foolishness in intellect. As for the establishment of causes by the Law, it is as we have read in the verse, and the evidence for this is beyond counting, both in the Qur'an and the Sunnah. As for its establishment by reason, we know that every thing that comes into being must have a cause that brings it about, known to us or unknown; this is necessary. A child cannot come out sprouting from the back of the mother's belly; it must have a cause for its existence and continuance. Likewise all events must have a cause, known or unknown. As for the senses, it is evident that causes have an effect. If you threw a glass bottle with a stone, it would break. What broke it?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Exactly, so it has a cause. If you heated cold water, it would become hot. The cause? That you heated it. This is known by the senses. Some scholars, out of their foolishness, hold that causes have no effect at all. Subhan Allah! No effect? They say: Yes, no effect. Is it not so that when you throw a stone at a bottle, the bottle breaks? They say: Yes, but the breaking occurred at the presence of the throwing, not by the throwing. How so? They say: when the thrown stone touched the bottle, it broke. Is this correct?

* Students: It is not correct.

* The Shaykh: Yes, it is not correct, as evidenced by the fact that if you took a stone three times the size of the bottle and placed it on the bottle, placing it down, the bottle would not break. Does something that accepts burning burn by fire because of a cause or without a cause? Because of a cause. Put a piece of paper in the fire and it burns. This is a reasonable matter, that is, a matter perceived by the senses. They say: No, not at all. If you affirm the effect of causes on their effects, you would be a polytheist against the Mighty God, I seek refuge in Allah! Because you have made a creator alongside Allah. I say: I have not made a creator alongside Allah, but I say: the cause has an effect not by itself, but by the strength Allah has placed in it; it is not by itself. The proof of this is the fire of Abraham, which was a great fire. They gathered a great quantity of firewood and kindled it, to the point that they hurled Abraham from a catapult, because they could not approach this fire because of its heat. What was it? Allah the Exalted said to it: ﴿O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham﴾ [al-Anbiya' 69], so it became coolness and safety for him, and it did not have its effect.

So we say: it is a cause by what Allah has placed in it of strength, and it is not effective by itself. There is another extreme who said: causes are effective by themselves. This is what we say contains a kind of shirk in his saying, and causes are not effective by themselves; the proof is the fire of Abraham. So in any case, we believe that causes have an effect by the powers Allah has placed in them, and that these powers may not have an effect if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills: ﴿because of what your hands have earned﴾.

We have said: among its benefits is the affirmation of causes, by His saying: ﴿because of what your hands have earned﴾.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person is requited for his earning with the like of his earning; for if it is because of what he has earned, it must be in proportion to what he earned. If it were more, it would be injustice, and Allah, Glorified and Exalted, does not wrong anyone.

* And among the benefits of the verse: the permissibility of expressing the whole by a part, by His saying: ﴿because of what your hands have earned﴾, although it includes what a person has earned with his foot, such as walking to houses of immorality and to wine and the like, for he is called to account for it.

If someone asks: Is it permissible to express any part by the whole?

The answer: No, but on the condition that this part has an effect on the whole.

The earning of the hand has an effect without doubt, because most works are done by it. "Free a neck" — the meaning is not that I strike the flat of the neck of the slave and say: "You, O neck, are freed," is it? That is wrong. But the neck is mentioned for the whole, because a person cannot live without a neck, and because the neck is the place of killing, whose separation from the body destroys the person. The summary: the permissibility of expressing the part for the whole, on the condition that it has an effect on what it is used to express.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah pardons much of the sins, so He does not call to account for them; by His saying: ﴿and He pardons much﴾. But is this pardon guaranteed? No, it is not guaranteed, and the evidence is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with; but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [an-Nisa' 48]. So do not let the security from the plotting of Allah lead you to say: this sin is among those Allah pardons, and then commit the sin. This is delusion and being deceived, because His saying ﴿and He pardons much﴾ is restricted by His saying ﴿and He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾.

The commentator said: (And He, the Exalted, is too generous to repeat the requital in the Hereafter). His intent, may Allah have mercy on him, is that the afflictions that befall us because of our sins suffice, and we are not punished for our sins in the Hereafter. This is the apparent meaning of the verse, because His saying ﴿because of what your hands have earned﴾ indicates that this affliction is the requital; and if it is the requital, Allah will not repeat the requital in the Hereafter, since He is too generous to repeat the requital. This is true: whatever a person is afflicted with in this world is an expiation for his sins. If the prescribed punishment (hadd) is carried out on him for a sin that has a prescribed punishment, it is an expiation; if he is disciplined for a sin that has no prescribed punishment, it is an expiation; if an affliction befalls him because of these sins, it is an expiation. So Allah will not repeat the punishment on him in the Hereafter except for one sin, which is striving in the land to cause corruption. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon the earth in corruption is only that they be killed or crucified or have their hands and feet cut off from opposite sides, or be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾ [al-Ma'idah 33]. So this is excepted, because of the grievousness of this type of sin, for corruption in the land is no easy matter. Allah has made these warring corrupters in the land subject to two punishments: punishment by the cutting of limbs, and second: ﴿and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment (33) except those who repent﴾ [al-Ma'idah 33, 34].

The commentator said: (As for those who are not sinners, what befalls them in this world is to raise their ranks in the Hereafter). This statement suggests that there are many people who are not sinners. Indeed, and upon reflection this is questionable, because there is no person who is not afflicted by sin. Even the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "Were you not to sin, Allah would take you away and bring a people who sin and then seek Allah's forgiveness, and He would forgive them." [Narrated by Muslim (2749) from Abu Hurayrah.] And the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "All of the children of Adam commit errors, and the best of those who err are those who repent often." [Narrated by at-Tirmidhi (2499) and Ibn Majah (4251) from Anas ibn Malik.] And the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said about himself: "O Allah, forgive me all my sin, the small and the great, the open and the secret, the first and the last." [Narrated by Muslim (483) from Abu Hurayrah.] And Allah said to His Prophet, addressing him: ﴿Indeed, We have opened for you a clear conquest (1) that Allah may forgive you your earlier sins and what follows﴾ [al-Fath 1, 2]. So can anyone dare to say that the Messenger did not sin, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿that Allah may forgive you your earlier sins and what follows﴾? It is impossible. That is, one cannot say he had no sin so that Allah would bestow His forgiveness upon him. Indeed, the messengers are protected from something that others are not: persistence in sin. That is impossible; Allah must pardon them, either by their seeking forgiveness and repenting to Allah, or by Allah's grace upon them. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to His Prophet: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful (1). Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾ [at-Tahrim 1, 2]. And He said to him: ﴿May Allah pardon you. Why did you give them permission until it became clear to you who were truthful and you knew the liars?﴾ [at-Tawbah 43]. This was said to the Prophet, upon him be prayers and peace, that Allah says to him: why did you hasten and give them permission? This is a great verse that orders a person's conduct, that he should not hasten in matters. If Allah rebuked His Prophet for granting them permission before the matter became clear to him, then what of others? And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor and you bestowed favor: "Keep your wife and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself what Allah was to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ [al-Ahzab 37]. Yes, the messengers, peace be upon them, are protected from major sins, protected from shirk, protected from base morals. As for the sins below that, they are not protected from them, but they are protected from persisting in them, and this is something not granted to others. We ask Allah, the Exalted, to make us and you among their followers, for He is over all things Powerful.

So the author's statement "as for those who are not sinners" is not accepted, because no one fails to sin, as you have heard in these hadiths. Accordingly, this statement of the author is not relevant. Yes, some people have sins and righteous deeds that expiate the sins without being afflicted by a calamity; this is very common. A man related to the Prophet ﷺ that he saw a woman and had with her what a man has with his wife, except that he did not commit adultery with her. He said: "Did you witness the dawn prayer with us?" I think he said: Yes. He said to him: "Good deeds remove bad deeds." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (526) and Muslim (2763) from Ibn Mas'ud.] So his dawn prayer removed the sins. Likewise the Prophet ﷺ said: "The five prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what is between them, as long as the major sins are avoided." [Narrated by Muslim (233) from Abu Hurayrah.]

Before we enter the second lesson, I want to alert you, my brothers. You are students of knowledge who came from your countries here to seek knowledge, and in your countries you seek knowledge, is that not so?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: But what is the benefit of knowledge? Is the benefit of knowledge that a person becomes a copy of a book, memorizing and gathering in his mind what he gathers, or is the benefit of knowledge action? The second. There is no good in knowledge without action, and knowledge without acting on it is a proof against a person, by the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace: "The Qur'an is a proof for you or against you." [Narrated by Muslim (223) from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari.] There is no third category. When a person acts by his knowledge, Allah the Exalted bequeaths to him knowledge of what he did not know before, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance﴾ [Muhammad 17], that is, knowledge, ﴿and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad 17], that is, they became God-fearing, mindful of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Acting on knowledge is important, and the purpose of knowledge is that a person be trained by it until he becomes a learned, godly scholar. I am displeased with some of you, that you neglect something important and easy, which is spreading the greeting of peace. We now observe one of you passing by his companion while standing and not saying "As-salamu alaykum." Why? Is it aversion to the Sunnah, or disinterest in the reward? I do not know. Or is it creating a cause for hatred and enmity? Because when a person passes you and does not greet you, there must be something in your heart, except one whose heart has hardened and who is accustomed to not greeting, and such a person is dead.

Then the Prophet ﷺ swore an oath and said: "By Allah, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another." The oath is inserted here. "Shall I not direct you to something which, if you do it, will make you love one another? Spread the greeting of peace (al-salam) among you."[[Narrated by Muslim (54/93) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] Why do we not spread it among ourselves? Yet the Muslim who gives the greeting of peace receives, what, ten good deeds. I think that if one of you were told: "Every time you greet someone, we will give you one riyal," would he greet or not? He would greet, and he would hesitate once and again, for what? So that the riyals increase. Yet these riyals he gains are in reality transient. Everything you own of this world will either leave you or you will leave it, without fail. But the good deed remains for you, and you will find yourself in greatest need of it. I advise you to act, and to seek knowledge. If you do not act, you are like books on the walls. Yet books on walls are safe, whereas you, if you do not act upon knowledge, are not safe, by Allah, you are not safe. Act. Be nurtured by knowledge in the worship of Allah, in dealing with the servants of Allah, and in dealing with yourselves as well. This is advice which I hope does not slip from your minds, for it is, God willing, beneficial. And Allah is the Granter of success.

* Student: There is a difficulty: some brothers sit in a place reading or writing, then a person needs something from another place, passes by him and returns. Must one, every time he passes and returns, fear that he is interrupting him?
* Shaykh: No. First, if you see a person busy and you fear that if you greet him you will disturb him, then do not greet him. Why? Because this is in his interest. For this reason the jurists (fuqaha', scholars of fiqh) said: greeting is disliked for a person occupied with remembrance of Allah, eating, or other such things.
* Student: In this case there is no harm.
* Shaykh: No harm. But what I mean is not this case. Perhaps the one who was not greeted would be happier than one who was greeted. Rather, they meet while walking, or one is putting on his shoes, and a person passes by him and goes beyond him without greeting him. Why does he not greet? What harm would it do him? By Allah, one nearly bursts with grief when he sees students of knowledge passing one another without greeting.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: There is no doubt, yes.
* Student: Some of them, O Shaykh, when you greet them, they look at you. That is, they look at you?
* Shaykh: A look of anger?
* Student: I do not know, O Shaykh. From the top of his head to the soles of his feet, and then it is as though a wall had passed by him.
* Shaykh: That is correct. He says: some people, when I greet them, begin to look at you. The reason is that this sunnah (practice of the Prophet ﷺ) is dead for him; he does not know it.
* Student: A group of committed students who frequent the mosque?
* Shaykh: No, this is a mistake. As for the common folk ('awamm), yes. Some of the common folk, if you greet them, they stop, and why? Because they are not accustomed to this. But the student of knowledge (talib al-'ilm), he has no excuse for this.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: If they are sitting in a row like this, greet the first of them, and that suffices.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you well, you have alerted us to giving the greeting of peace. May Allah reward you well. Many students, O Shaykh, are eager to give the greeting, and some of them may forget at times. But sometimes the greeting is returned, yet you cannot tell whether this man greeted or cleared his throat. Because it is the custom that when one says "as-salamu 'alaykum," the reply comes in the same form; when one says "as-salamu 'alaykum," you say "wa 'alaykumu s-salam wa rahmatullah," like this. But when one says "ihh," you do not know whether he greeted or cleared his throat. You do not know. Sometimes the reply is like that, so that someone says "as-salamu 'alaykum" and he has not replied?
* Shaykh: No, there must be clarity. In any case, confusion between clearing the throat and the greeting is not plausible.
* Student: He does not pronounce it, O Shaykh.
* Shaykh: Yes, he perhaps murmurs it in a whisper, and this is a mistake. Greet with a clear greeting. Just as some people with cars now, when they meet you, sound their horn. That is, if I have a horn, do I sound my horn so as to reply to him? This is also a mistake. But perhaps some people say that they sound the horn so that I will notice and greet.
* Student: If a person is afflicted with an innovation (bid'ah), how can his sins be expiated, when it increases sins?
* Shaykh: Innovation does not expiate sins; it adds to sins.
* Student: By those calamities, O Shaykh.
* Shaykh: Yes, this is a calamity, but it is a calamity that requires repentance. That is, religious calamities are a calamity; there is no doubt that when a person is afflicted with lethargy in obedience, or for example turning away from obedience, this is without doubt a calamity. But one must not be content with it; he must flee from it as he flees from material calamities.
* Student: There is a difficulty.
* Shaykh: What is it?
* Student: If a person reads the books of the scholars, and then forgetfulness overcomes him regarding many statements, does he distinguish between forgetting the Qur'an and forgetting other things?
* Shaykh: Yes, that is known.
* Student: And is this among the sins?
* Shaykh: Forgetfulness is something no human is free from. Even the Prophet ﷺ once recited and forgot a verse of the Book of Allah. No one is spared from it. But the Qur'an requires particular care, more so because of the Prophet's ﷺ command to maintain it. The Qur'an is among the most forgotten things. That is, you may memorize, for example, a text of fiqh (matn min mutun al-fiqh) which does not need much review, but the Qur'an, you must review it much, or you will forget it. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Maintain your review of the Qur'an, for by Him in whose hand is my soul, it is more prone to escape than camels from their tethers,"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5033) and Muslim (791/231) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]] and the wisdom behind the fact that the Qur'an is forgotten more than other things is:
First: the trial, so that Allah, blessed and exalted, may know who is eager to memorize the Qur'an and who is not.
Second: the abundance of reward and merit by repeating it, for in every letter there are ten good deeds.
Third: that the remembrance of Allah, exalted is He, remains in your heart. For the Qur'an is the speech of Allah. When you recite the Qur'an, it is as though you are conversing intimately with Allah, exalted is He, because you are reciting His speech, glorified and exalted is He. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, in His wisdom, made it forgotten quickly, so that you will be eager for it.
* Student: O Shaykh, there is a hadith that when two angels came to the Prophet ﷺ in a dream, he passed by those who are punished in their graves, or a man to whom the Qur'an was given but who slept through it at night and did not act upon it by day.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (1386) from the hadith of Samurah ibn Jundab.]] Does this indicate the obligation of night prayer (qiyam al-layl) upon the bearer of the Qur'an?
* Shaykh: No, it is not obligatory. But perhaps this man had a particular characteristic, or it may be said: he slept through it at night, meaning he slept through what was obligatory in it, such as the 'Isha' prayer and the Fajr prayer, for the hypocrites do not pray Fajr or 'Isha'.
* Student: They say that some sunnah acts are obligatory upon the student of knowledge?
* Shaykh: No. Yes, some sunnah acts are indeed obligatory upon the student of knowledge when his practice of them is a reviving of the sunnah. In that case it is obligatory for him to perform them, because this falls under conveying the message (al-balagh).

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And you cannot escape [Him] on earth, nor do you have, besides Allah, any protector or helper.﴾ [Ash-Shura 31] "Ma" here is a negation particle, and it functions like "laysa" (is not) according to the dialect of the Hijazis, and the Noble Qur'an was revealed in their language. On this basis, His saying ﴿antum﴾ is its subject, and ﴿bi-mu'jizeen﴾ is its predicate, but it is accompanied by the extra "ba'" (bāʾ al-zā'ida, the superfluous bā'), which is extra in terms of grammatical structure (iʿrāb), meaning that grammatically it is superfluous: were it removed, the sentence would be complete without it. However, in terms of meaning it is not superfluous, but rather serves a purpose. The purpose of the particles of emphasis (ḥurūf al-ziyāda) is to add emphasis: whenever you encounter a superfluous particle, it is for the emphasis of the generality. He says: ﴿And you cannot escape on earth﴾, i.e., you cannot escape from Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He; if He pursues you, you will not be able to escape Him on earth.

As for the saying of the commentator, may Allah have mercy on him: (﴿bi-mu'jizeen﴾ Allah, by fleeing) — this is given as an example; otherwise the meaning is more general than what he said, i.e., you cannot escape Allah by fleeing, nor by hiding, nor by lying down, and the like. A person may overpower another person if he flees from him and is faster than him; he may overpower him if he hides from him behind a wall, a cave, a tree, or the like; he may overpower him if he hides from him by lying down on the ground, and the like. Can this kind of overpowering that occurs from one person to another occur from a person against Allah? No, because nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Allah, and nothing on earth or in heaven is beyond His power.

This is a warning to these people: ﴿and you have not, besides Allah﴾, i.e., other than Him, ﴿any protector or helper﴾. ﴿And you have not﴾: here "ma" is a negation particle, and we do not say it is of the Hijazi type, because one of the conditions for its functioning like "laysa" is word order, that the noun be placed first, whereas here the predicate is placed first; accordingly it is a negation particle that does not govern.

﴿And you have not, besides Allah, any protector﴾: the "min" here is superfluous, for emphasis of the negation; ﴿any protector or helper﴾ who would ward off His punishment from you. ﴿Any protector﴾ who would take charge of you and treat you well in your guardianship, and no helper who would repel from you. So there is no protector who takes charge of you besides Allah, nor helper who repels from you the punishment of Allah. Rather, you are in His grip, Blessed and Exalted is He, wherever you may be.

In this noble verse are the following benefits:

* First: a threat to the polytheists with the punishment of Allah, and that when Allah intends it, He cannot be overpowered.

* Among them: the obligation to fear Allah and to be mindful of His watch, for when He, Glorified and Exalted, intends to punish the disobedient, nothing is hidden from Him.

* Also among its benefits: there is no one who will take charge of these deniers and support them besides Allah, and foremost among them are the idols; idols do not benefit them, and rather, if they are rational, they will disown them on the Day of Resurrection, and if they are not rational, they and those who worshipped them will be fuel for Hell, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said in Surat al-Anbiya': ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be entering it﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 98].

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And among His signs are the ships, sailing in the sea like mountains﴾ [al-Shura 32]. They stand motionless on the surface of the water. So He, glorified and exalted, explains that among His signs is the movement of these ships.

﴿If He wills, He stills the wind so that they remain﴾ [become] ﴿motionless﴾, fixed, not running, ﴿upon its surface﴾ — i.e., the surface of the sea. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful one﴾ [from His signs].

Then He said: ﴿signs﴾ (plural), because partitive means a part of a thing. If the thing is a thousand, its part may be two hundred or three hundred; if the thing is two, the part is one. Ships are countless, hence He said: ﴿Indeed in that are signs﴾, considering the many ships that run upon the sea. We may also say that, considering a single ship, what its passengers observe at sea are great signs indicating the perfection of Allah's power. Thus those who go out to sea to catch fish tell us of wonders they witness about the fish, its varieties, and the differences in their forms, sizes and shapes, which are among the greatest signs of Allah.

Both the patient and the grateful will see in these ships of the signs of Allah the Mighty and Majestic what makes them certain that Allah, glorified and exalted, is capable of all things, that He is merciful to His servants, and other things that they will see.

The disbeliever is patient in the place of patience and endures, but he does not give thanks in the place of thanks; rather he only grows in arrogance and insolence.

(﴿Or He destroys them﴾ is conjoined to "He stills", i.e., He drowns them by the violence of the wind together with their people.) ﴿And those who dispute concerning Our signs will know that they have no place of escape﴾. The one who debates is called mujadil because each of the two debaters twists his argument so that it may prevail over the argument of the other. This is the origin of mujadalah, which is dispute and enmity, ﴿concerning Our signs﴾, to establish falsehood and refute truth.

So one of its benefits: the warning of ships being drowned because of sins.

As for disputing to establish truth, it is obligatory, when a person is skilled and proficient in it. If he has no knowledge, then it is obligatory that he not dispute, because if he disputes to establish truth without knowledge, the matter may be reversed against him: he will be presented with doubts he cannot repel, and then he will be silenced. The author the commentator said: (In the nominative it is a new sentence; in the accusative it is conjoined to an estimated cause, i.e., He drowns them in order to take vengeance upon them and to make them know.)
