The answer is that their benefit is emphasis, i.e., emphasizing the negation.

* In this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah the Exalted's love for those who are just and equitable. From where is this taken?

* A student: His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Shura 40].

* The Shaykh: Its implication is that the non-wrongdoer...?

* The student: He loves him.

* The Shaykh: Well said, may Allah bless you.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of the attribute of love for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This matter is a doctrinal (aqidah) question. The line of inference: since He negated His love for the wrongdoers, this indicates that He loves the just and equitable. This reasoning resembles al-Shafi'i's (may Allah have mercy on him) argument that the believers will see Allah from His saying concerning the wicked: ﴿No indeed! Surely they, that day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 15]; he said: if He were veiled from everyone, the negation would be pointless.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a warning against wrongdoing. Its basis: in wrongdoing is the absence of Allah's love for the servant, and how great is the loss of one who has lost Allah's love. O Allah, we ask You for Your love, the love of those who love You, and the love of the deed that brings us closer to Your love.

* Among the benefits of the verse: whoever avenges himself after being wronged is not to be objected to, by His saying: ﴿And whoever avenges himself after being wronged, those, there is no blame upon them﴾.

* Among its benefits: the absence of a path against one who avenges himself is conditional upon the establishment of the wrong, by His saying: ﴿And whoever avenges himself after being wronged﴾. As for acting on accusations, it is not permitted; you must be certain that you have been wronged before you avenge yourself.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The blame is only upon those who wrong people and transgress in the earth without right.﴾ The mufassir said: (They act ﴿in the earth without right﴾ through acts of disobedience) ﴿for them is a painful punishment﴾ (painful: causing pain).

﴿The blame is only upon those who﴾: This sentence contains a particle of restriction, which is (innama) ("only"). Restriction (hasr) means affirming the ruling for what is mentioned and negating it for anything else. It is as if He said: there is no blame except upon these people. ﴿The blame is only﴾, meaning the path to reproach, condemnation and accountability, ﴿upon those who wrong people﴾, whether with their wealth, their lives or their honour. The Prophet (ﷺ) declared during the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Indeed your blood, your wealth and your honour are sacred to you"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (67) and Muslim (1679/29), from the hadith of Nufay' ibn al-Harith.]]. Wronging people revolves around these three things: blood, wealth and honour. Whoever backbites someone has wronged him; whoever takes his property has wronged him; whoever betrays him in a transaction between them has wronged him. The examples of this are without limit.

The point is that those who wrong people deserve blame. As for His saying ﴿they transgress﴾, the author explained it with his words (they act). It seems he avoided combining "transgress" with His saying ﴿without right﴾, so he said (they act), so that the verb (yabghoon) would have an independent meaning and "without right" would have an independent meaning.

The correct view is to keep the verse on its apparent meaning. The meaning of yabghoon is: they oppress, from "baghā ʿalā ghayrihi" (he transgressed against another), i.e., he attacked him unjustly. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He forbids indecency, wrongdoing and transgression (al-baghy)﴾ [al-Nahl 90]. So His saying ﴿yabghoon﴾ means they transgress against others and exceed their limits in dealing with them. His saying ﴿without right﴾ is then a descriptive qualifier clarifying that every transgression is without right. Keeping the Qur'anic text on its apparent meaning is obligatory, especially since that interpretation would make it deficient.

So ﴿they transgress in the earth﴾ [al-Shura 42], i.e., they oppress in it and exceed the bounds, ﴿without right﴾ [al-Shura 42] is a statement of the reality; it is a descriptive qualifier, since every transgression is without right. His saying ﴿without right﴾ was explained as meaning acts of disobedience, and indeed all acts of disobedience are without right. But do not understand from this that it is restricted to the right of Allah; rather it is general, covering both the right of Allah and the rights of others. Transgression against Allah's right is forbidden, and likewise transgression against the rights of human beings.

﴿For them is a painful punishment﴾ [al-Shura 42]: "Those" refers to those who wrong people and transgress in the earth without right. ﴿For them is a painful punishment﴾, i.e., painful, and "iylam" means causing pain, i.e., it is afflicting.

In this noble verse, regarding ﴿The blame is only upon those who﴾:

* Among its benefits: whoever wrongs people is held accountable, its basis being that accountability is restricted to those who wrong people and transgress in the earth without right.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: transgression is a wrong with no right in it, as shown by His saying ﴿and they transgress in the earth without right﴾ [al-Shura 42].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a warning to those who wrong people and transgress in the earth without right of a painful punishment, as shown by His saying ﴿for them is a painful punishment﴾ [al-Shura 42].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the punishment of these people is severe, because it is expressed by a nominal sentence in this specific form: ﴿those, for them is a painful punishment﴾ [al-Shura 42].

(﴿And whoever is patient and forgives﴾) — he does not take revenge, and forgives (تجاوز, "overlooks") — meaning he overlooks the wrongdoer. ﴿Indeed, that is among the matters requiring determination﴾ [al-Shura 43] — i.e., among the things that are resolved upon (معزوماتها), meaning those that are legislatively required (المطلوبات شرعًا).

﴿And whoever is patient﴾: this lam is the lam of initiation (لام الابتداء), which conveys emphasis (التوكيد). "Man" (من) is a conditional noun (اسم شرط جازم), the conditional verb is ﴿صَبَرَ﴾ ("is patient"), and the response of the condition is ﴿Indeed, that is among the matters requiring determination﴾. Pay attention to this parsing: (من) is conditional, the conditional verb is (صبر) and what is conjoined to it, and the response of the condition is ﴿إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمِنْ عَزْمِ الْأُمُورِ﴾. Here there is a difficulty: if the response of the condition is a nominal sentence, the response must be preceded by the fā' (فاء); as in the verse before it: ﴿And whoever retaliates after being wronged — those have no path [of blame] against them﴾ [al-Shura 41], where the fā' is omitted here. The difficulty is: how was the fā' omitted in the response of the condition when it is a nominal sentence?

Answer: the fā' may be omitted even when the response of the condition is a nominal sentence, and they cited for this the poet's verse:

"Whoever does good deeds, God will reward them ∗∗∗ ..........................."

(من يفعل الحسنات) is conditional, the conditional verb is (يفعل), the response is (الله يشكرها), and there is no fā' in it. They said: it is permissible at times to omit the fā', and they cited the verse as evidence, and they cited the line as evidence.

Some of them said in parsing the verse: the omission of the fā' indicates that (من) is not conditional but a relative pronoun (اسم موصول), and accordingly the meaning is: "And for the one who is patient and forgives, indeed that is among the matters requiring determination." The truth is that the first and second parsings are both permissible, but taking (من) as a conditional noun, as in the verse before it, is preferable in terms of the harmony of the context with itself, and the difficulty regarding the omission of the fā' in the response is answered by saying that it may sometimes be omitted.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And whoever is patient﴾ means: patient over the wrongdoer's injustice toward him. And if you wish, say: it is general, including everyone who is patient over harm from illness, travel, or the like; but the generality may be prevented by His saying ﴿and forgives﴾, for the apparent context indicates that what is meant is patience in refraining from punishing the wrongdoer. ﴿And forgives﴾ means: covers over the injustice he suffered. ﴿Indeed, that is among the matters requiring determination﴾ (i.e., those that are resolved upon), meaning it is evidence that the person is of those possessing determination (ذوي العزم), because he bore it, covered it over: he bore it and was patient, pardoned and forgave. ﴿Indeed, that is among the matters requiring determination.﴾

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: encouragement toward patience and forgiveness, based on His saying: ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives, indeed that is among the matters requiring determination﴾ [al-Shura 43]. But you must observe the preceding verse: that the matter contains reform (إصلاح).

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that matters differ in their degrees of determination and what falls below them, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, that is among the matters requiring determination﴾. There is no doubt they differ: some of them are undertaken by one who has a true resolve and complete manliness, and some are below this.

* Student: (...) When he was wronged and invoked against his wrongdoer, is it not permissible for him to invoke against him for more than his injustice?

* Shaykh: This is what is obligatory. But one may suppose that this wrong is not one in which it is permissible to exceed, and it is a great wrong, like the invocation of Sa'd (رضي الله عنه) against one who wronged him, when he said: he oppresses the subjects, does not distribute equally, and delays the prayer past its time; so he invoked against him a great invocation: "O God, blind his sight, prolong his life, and expose him to trials."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (755) from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas.]] So someone might say: this is greater than his injustice, but in reality it is not greater, because his wronging him includes disparaging the ruler, since he appointed over the people someone like this.

* Student: May Allah be good to you. The wrongdoer's injustice differs according to people. A person may wrong another in some matter, and if he wants to take from this person an amount equal to what was taken from him, it does not harm him as it harmed him; for example, taking a small amount of money from a poor man, while this rich person is not affected by this money if you take it from him; or striking a strong-built person with a blow that is for a weak one, where the weak one is affected by a small blow and falls, while the strong one, if struck with that blow, does not fall. Must he bring someone of strong build like him to strike him?

* Shaykh: No, it is not a condition; if he strikes him the same way he struck, that suffices.

* Student: It does not affect him.

* Shaykh: First, may Allah bless you. You know that most scholars say that for a blow there is no retaliation (قصاص) unless it causes death, and we know that such a blow usually kills, so retaliation is taken. But let us set aside this issue. Your first example: a poor man from whom a rich man took ten riyals and became utterly destitute, while this one who took ten riyals has millions. If we take ten riyals from him, nothing harms him. We say: justice is that this one be given exactly what he took, only that. (...)

It is said: a wicked man assaulted another, and the other pardoned him. Does he have a reward?

We examine: if he did not know that the man was wicked and pardoned him, seeking reform, then he has a reward. But if he knew, yet says: "I pardon him and I do not care whether he goes about corrupting the land or not," then he sins.

* Student: May Allah be good to you. Sometimes the wrongdoer dies while holding authority. Is it permissible to invoke against him? Does a person invoke against him?

* Shaykh: You mean after his death? There is no harm; he may invoke against him even after his death. Moreover, if it is assumed that the wronged person did not invoke, his right will still come to him on the Day of Resurrection, and if he takes from his good deeds by invoking against him, that is settled through the invocation. We ask Allah, Exalted is He, to gather us and you in His mercy, and to grant us and you success in what He loves and is pleased with.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guardian after Him.﴾ [Ash-Shura 44] (Man) here is a conditional particle, and it is general in meaning: whoever Allah wills to lead astray, no one can be his guardian after Allah. The meaning of this is that no one can guide him, as Allah says in another verse: ﴿So who can guide him after Allah?﴾ [Al-Jathiyah 23]. ﴿For him there is no guardian after Him.﴾ The commentator (al-mufassir) says: (That is, no one who could guide him after Allah has led him astray.) ﴿And you see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying: "Is there any way of return?"﴾ (Tara) is a visual verb, (al-zalimin) is the direct object, (yaqulun) is a circumstantial clause (jumlah haliyyah), and ﴿when they see the punishment﴾: (lamma) here, what is it? Is it a conditional particle (jazimah)? It means "when." ﴿You see the wrongdoers﴾: what is meant by "the wrongdoers" here is the disbelievers, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾ [Al-Baqarah 254].

﴿When they see the punishment﴾: that is, when they see the punishment with their own eyes, ﴿they say: "Is there any way of return?"﴾ (Hal) is an interrogative used to express wishing (lil-tamanni); that is, they wish that there were a way for them to return.

His saying ﴿to a return﴾ means: to a place of return. What is meant is a return to the world so that they may do righteous deeds. But this wish is doomed to failure, because that is impossible. Indeed, Allah the Mighty and Majestic has said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly go back to what they were forbidden﴾ [Al-An'am 28]. They wish for this and claim that if they were returned they would act righteously, but the matter is not so. ﴿Is there any way of return?﴾ He said: that is, any path. The answer is: there is no way. As you have heard, ﴿if they were returned, they would certainly go back to what they were forbidden﴾ [Al-An'am 28]. Likewise, when a wave like shades covers them in the seas and they call upon Allah, sincerely devoting religion to Him, when He rescues them they return to association (shirk).

He said: ﴿And you see them being exposed to it﴾ [Ash-Shura 45] morning and evening. The word (tara) here and the one before it: is what is meant by them the Messenger (ﷺ) alone, or is it "you see," addressing the one who is addressed?

The second, because if we say the second, it is more general than if we say the first. ﴿And you see them﴾, O seer, ﴿being exposed to it﴾ morning and evening.

(﴿And you see them being exposed to it﴾: that is, to the Fire, ﴿humbled﴾, fearful and submissive, ﴿from abasement﴾.) (Min) here indicates cause; that is, because of their abasement. These are the ones who were arrogant and haughty in the world, who did not regard people as anything and did not accept the truth. They are exposed to the Fire in this condition. ﴿Humbled from abasement﴾ means their hearts have been filled with humiliation. (﴿They look﴾ at it ﴿with a furtive glance﴾, a weak glance, stealing looks.) That is, they look at the Fire, may Allah protect us, ﴿with a glance﴾, that is, with sight, ﴿furtive﴾, that is, weak; they steal glances, like a person who is afraid of something: you find him looking at it with a weak glance, then he quickly turns his gaze away, and that is because of the intensity of their abasement. May Allah protect us and you from their condition. (Min) may be the inceptive (ibtida'iyyah) or in the sense of (ba') (with). (Min) in His saying ﴿with a furtive glance﴾ is inceptive or in the sense of (ba'), meaning: they look with a furtive glance. If the matter is between it being inceptive in its own sense or in the sense of (ba'), then it is better to take it in its own sense, meaning their looking begins from a furtive glance ﴿with a furtive glance﴾.

﴿And those who believed say﴾: they said, praising Allah the Mighty and Majestic, speaking of His blessings. He said: ﴿Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾. (Inna) requires a subject and a predicate. Its subject is ﴿the losers﴾; its predicate is ﴿those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾. That is, they have lost them: they lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection (by their being abiding in the Fire and their not reaching the maidens of paradise prepared for them). The true losers are not those who lost wealth, nor those who lost family in this world. The true losers are ﴿those who have lost themselves and their families﴾. As for the loss of their families, it is evident, because they will not be gathered with their families in the Fire, unlike the people of Paradise, concerning whom Allah says: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith, We will join their descendants with them﴾ [At-Tur 21]. That is, even if the descendants are of lower rank, Allah will raise them to their fathers. These, may Allah protect us, are separated from their families in the Fire; even if they were gathered together, what would that be? So their loss of their families is clear. But how did they lose themselves? They lost themselves because they gained nothing from the life of this world; their life is a loss, because they gained nothing from it, so they did not believe in Allah and His messengers.

As for the saying of the author, may Allah have mercy on him: (by their being abiding in the Fire and their not reaching the maidens prepared for them in Paradise, had they believed), there is an evident problem with this. What is meant by "their families" is their families in the world, and what is not meant is "the maidens prepared for them in the Hereafter had they believed," because this is already known from before. It is said to the deceased when he is buried in his grave: "This is your seat in Paradise, had you believed"; and it is said to the believer: "This is your seat in the Fire, had you not believed" [Reported by al-Bukhari (6569) and Ibn Hibban (3113), and the wording is his, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah]. So what is meant by "the families" here is their families in the world, who did not profit.

As for the saying of the author, may Allah have mercy on him: (and the relative pronoun is the predicate of inna). Where is the relative pronoun? ﴿Those who have lost themselves﴾: this is the relative pronoun. He drew attention to this so that one who thinks ﴿those who have lost﴾ is a qualifier of "the losers" would not suppose so.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment﴾. The commentator says: (the disbelievers ﴿in lasting punishment﴾, enduring; and this is part of the speech of Allah, blessed and exalted). That is, it is not part of the speech of those who believed. Recite the verse: ﴿And those who believed said: "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment."﴾ If we looked at the context, we would say this is the continuation of the believers' speech. But the author drew attention to the fact that this is the speech of Allah and not the speech of those who believed. The context allows both: it may be, as the commentator said, the speech of Allah, and it may be the speech of those who believed. Those who believed know that the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment from the time they are in the world, because they have read the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ).

As for His saying ﴿Unquestionably, the wrongdoers﴾: the sentence is emphasized by two emphasizers. The first: ﴿Unquestionably (ala)﴾, because (ala) here is for alerting, and alerting requires emphasis. The second emphasizer: ﴿Indeed (inna) the wrongdoers﴾, because (inna) is a particle of emphasis. ﴿In lasting punishment﴾: that is, enduring, may Allah protect us.

In these verses there are benefits:

* Among them: whomever Allah leads astray, no one can guide him, however high the rank of the one who tries to guide him; because of His saying: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guardian after Him.﴾ This great and frightening ruling is confirmed by what happened to the Prophet (ﷺ) with his uncle Abu Talib. Abu Talib was the brother of the Messenger's father, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family. He used to support the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, protect him, and defend him. When his death approached, the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, was with him, along with two men from Quraysh. He kept presenting Islam to him, saying: "O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah, a word by which I may argue on your behalf before Allah." The two men said to him: "Do you turn away from the religion of Abd al-Muttalib?" (which was the religion of disbelief and association). The Prophet (ﷺ) repeated it to him, and they repeated it, and the last thing he said was: "He is upon the religion of Abd al-Muttalib" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1360) and Muslim (24/39), from the hadith of al-Musayyab ibn Hazn]. We ask Allah for well-being and safety. Despite his love for the Messenger (ﷺ) and his testimony to his prophethood, he did not submit and did not accept. So the last of his life was his saying: "upon the religion of Abd al-Muttalib." He died upon association. Allah the Exalted permitted His Messenger (ﷺ) to intercede for him to lighten the punishment for him, so he interceded for him, and he was in a shallow part of the Fire, and upon him were two sandals of fire, from which his brain boils [Reported by Muslim (212/362), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas]. May Allah protect us. His brain is the highest part of his body, and the sandals are at the lowest part; if the highest is boiling, what is below it is more and more intense. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And had it not been for me, he would have been in the lowest level of the Fire" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3883) and Muslim (209/357), from the hadith of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib]. Had it not been that I interceded, or had it not been for my message, which Abu Talib defended? The apparent meaning is both together, because Allah thanked him, rather because Allah the Exalted permitted His Messenger (ﷺ) to intercede for him, in return for what he offered to Islam in support.

From this it is derived that whoever supports Islam, even if he is a disbeliever, has merit, because Islam is a religion of justice, giving every rightful person his right. For example, if disbelievers help Muslims with sincere help, and we know they have no greed in that, and the Muslims benefit from this support, then we must acknowledge their merit in this matter. Why? Because they have done a kindness to us, and because the Islamic religion is a religion of justice that does not wrong anyone of his right. As for the saying of some people: "We will not acknowledge their merit because they are disbelievers," their disbelief is between them and Allah, and their favor upon us is a right which we must acknowledge.

Let me give an example in the case of Kosovo. In the Kosovo case, what happened is something many of you have heard. Who supported them? The disbelievers supported them. The Atlantic Alliance placed all the equipment it had with which it could fight, and defended them. We did not hear of any Muslim sending a plane or a shell. Perhaps there is an excuse for them, while you blame them; but our denying this merit is an error. We say: these people have merit, and their disbelief is between them and Allah, and we do not love them for their disbelief at all. Rather we thank them for their favor, even though we hate them with the utmost hatred because they are enemies of Allah and His Messenger. This is if we know the intention is sincere. But if we know with certainty that it is deception and trickery, then here we blame them for what they did, and we do not praise them, nor acknowledge merit to them; because the ruling revolves around its cause, existence and non-existence.

I return to the benefits. He says:

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever Allah guides has indeed been taken as a guardian by Him; because when He negated guardianship from the wrongdoers, it is established for the believers. This was made explicit in His saying: ﴿Allah is the Guardian of those who believe; He brings them out from darknesses into light. And those who disbelieve, their guardians are the taghut; they bring them out from the light into darknesses. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾ [Al-Baqarah 257].

* And among the benefits of this verse: a person should constantly insist before Allah that He guide him from misguidance; because if the matter of misleading is returned to Allah, then to whom do we turn? To whom? To Allah the Mighty and Majestic. As long as misguidance and guidance are in the hand of Allah, let us return to Him.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the grief and humiliation of the wrongdoers when they see the punishment; because of His saying: ﴿And you see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying: "Is there any way of return?"﴾. Their grief is in their saying: ﴿Is there any way of return?﴾, because this is a wish.

* And among the benefits of the following noble verse: these wrongdoers are exposed to the Fire in the most complete humiliation and the most disgraceful condition: ﴿humbled﴾, that is, debased and fearful of humiliation.

* And among the benefits of this verse: that those arrogant toward the truth and stubborn will be requited with a punishment that matches their disobedience. What is the basis of this?

* Student: Allah, glorified and exalted, when they were arrogant toward the truth, made them humbled before the Fire.

* The Shaykh: The basis of this: they are exposed to the Fire humbled and abased. It is known that punishment by abasement matches disobedience through arrogance.

* And among the benefits of this verse: the wrongdoers are overtaken by humiliation, outwardly and inwardly. The inward is in His saying: ﴿humbled from abasement﴾, and the outward in His saying: ﴿they look with a furtive glance﴾.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the speaking of those who believed about the blessings of Allah the Mighty and Majestic; because of His saying: ﴿And those who believed said: "Indeed, the losers"﴾; it is as if they are praising Allah for having gained both their worldly life and their Hereafter.

* And among the benefits of the verse: that the disobedient has lost himself, and the loss is according to the measure of his disobedience; because he gained nothing from his existence in this world.

From this it follows that a person should take account of himself and look at what he has done. If he sees that he has filled his time with the intended good and the means to it, let him praise Allah; and if he sees that he has wasted it, let him seek to make amends. This is derived from His saying: ﴿Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves﴾.

Let us give an example of this: a man stood to pray and recite the Qur'an for an hour, and another spent that hour playing. Who is the winner? The first is the winner, because he filled that time with worship; the second is a loser, lost. Some scholars even said: it is forbidden for him not to occupy his time with obedience, because he is like one who has wealth and did not spend it in the way of Allah. But the correct view is that if he does not fill it with disobedience, then it is neither for him nor against him; yet he is considered a loser in comparison with the one who occupied himself with obedience to Allah. And you, reflect on this when you stand to pray: say to yourself, "My life is this time that I have spent in obedience to Allah." Train yourself in this, so that you are eager to fill your time with obedience to Allah.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the punishment of the disbelievers is lasting; because of His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment﴾.

* And among its benefits: the emphasis of this punishment, lest someone say: the punishment may come to an end.

He said: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guardian after Him.﴾ (Man) is a conditional particle, and the verb is jussive (majzum) by it. Jussive by what?

* Student: By (man).

* The Shaykh: Yes, the verb of the condition (fi'l al-shart).

* Student: The verb of the condition; its sign of jussive is sukun, and it is vowelled (...) to avoid two consecutive sukuns.

* The Shaykh: Its sign of jussive is sukun, and it is vowelled with kasra to avoid two consecutive sukuns.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: (...) Good. Why is the response (jawab) joined with the fa'? Because it is what?

* Student: Joined with (ma).

* The Shaykh: Well done, joined with (ma). Did Allah inform us?

* Student: Allah the Mighty and Majestic informed us that the disbelievers ﴿are pushed﴾ [At-Tur 13], meaning they are thrust into it.

* The Shaykh: ﴿They are pushed forcefully into the fire of Hell﴾ [At-Tur 13].

* Student: They are thrust into it, pushed. How do we reconcile: ﴿And you see them being exposed to it﴾? What is this exposure?

* The Shaykh: They are exposed to it before they enter it.

* Student: That is, on the Sirat, or how?

* The Shaykh: Allah knows best. They are exposed to it before they enter it, and the disbelievers do not try to climb the Sirat, because they are turned toward Hell in the plains of the Resurrection.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guardian after Him.﴾ [Ash-Shura 44] (Man) here is a conditional particle, and it is general in meaning: whoever Allah wills to lead astray, no one can be his guardian after Allah. The meaning of this is that no one can guide him, as Allah says in another verse: ﴿So who can guide him after Allah?﴾ [Al-Jathiyah 23]. ﴿For him there is no guardian after Him.﴾ The commentator (al-mufassir) says: (That is, no one who could guide him after Allah has led him astray.) ﴿And you see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying: "Is there any way of return?"﴾ (Tara) is a visual verb, (al-zalimin) is the direct object, (yaqulun) is a circumstantial clause (jumlah haliyyah), and ﴿when they see the punishment﴾: (lamma) here, what is it? Is it a conditional particle (jazimah)? It means "when." ﴿You see the wrongdoers﴾: what is meant by "the wrongdoers" here is the disbelievers, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾ [Al-Baqarah 254].

﴿When they see the punishment﴾: that is, when they see the punishment with their own eyes, ﴿they say: "Is there any way of return?"﴾ (Hal) is an interrogative used to express wishing (lil-tamanni); that is, they wish that there were a way for them to return.

His saying ﴿to a return﴾ means: to a place of return. What is meant is a return to the world so that they may do righteous deeds. But this wish is doomed to failure, because that is impossible. Indeed, Allah the Mighty and Majestic has said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly go back to what they were forbidden﴾ [Al-An'am 28]. They wish for this and claim that if they were returned they would act righteously, but the matter is not so. ﴿Is there any way of return?﴾ He said: that is, any path. The answer is: there is no way. As you have heard, ﴿if they were returned, they would certainly go back to what they were forbidden﴾ [Al-An'am 28]. Likewise, when a wave like shades covers them in the seas and they call upon Allah, sincerely devoting religion to Him, when He rescues them they return to association (shirk).

He said: ﴿And you see them being exposed to it﴾ [Ash-Shura 45] morning and evening. The word (tara) here and the one before it: is what is meant by them the Messenger (ﷺ) alone, or is it "you see," addressing the one who is addressed?

The second, because if we say the second, it is more general than if we say the first. ﴿And you see them﴾, O seer, ﴿being exposed to it﴾ morning and evening.

(﴿And you see them being exposed to it﴾: that is, to the Fire, ﴿humbled﴾, fearful and submissive, ﴿from abasement﴾.) (Min) here indicates cause; that is, because of their abasement. These are the ones who were arrogant and haughty in the world, who did not regard people as anything and did not accept the truth. They are exposed to the Fire in this condition. ﴿Humbled from abasement﴾ means their hearts have been filled with humiliation. (﴿They look﴾ at it ﴿with a furtive glance﴾, a weak glance, stealing looks.) That is, they look at the Fire, may Allah protect us, ﴿with a glance﴾, that is, with sight, ﴿furtive﴾, that is, weak; they steal glances, like a person who is afraid of something: you find him looking at it with a weak glance, then he quickly turns his gaze away, and that is because of the intensity of their abasement. May Allah protect us and you from their condition. (Min) may be the inceptive (ibtida'iyyah) or in the sense of (ba') (with). (Min) in His saying ﴿with a furtive glance﴾ is inceptive or in the sense of (ba'), meaning: they look with a furtive glance. If the matter is between it being inceptive in its own sense or in the sense of (ba'), then it is better to take it in its own sense, meaning their looking begins from a furtive glance ﴿with a furtive glance﴾.

﴿And those who believed say﴾: they said, praising Allah the Mighty and Majestic, speaking of His blessings. He said: ﴿Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾. (Inna) requires a subject and a predicate. Its subject is ﴿the losers﴾; its predicate is ﴿those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾. That is, they have lost them: they lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection (by their being abiding in the Fire and their not reaching the maidens of paradise prepared for them). The true losers are not those who lost wealth, nor those who lost family in this world. The true losers are ﴿those who have lost themselves and their families﴾. As for the loss of their families, it is evident, because they will not be gathered with their families in the Fire, unlike the people of Paradise, concerning whom Allah says: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith, We will join their descendants with them﴾ [At-Tur 21]. That is, even if the descendants are of lower rank, Allah will raise them to their fathers. These, may Allah protect us, are separated from their families in the Fire; even if they were gathered together, what would that be? So their loss of their families is clear. But how did they lose themselves? They lost themselves because they gained nothing from the life of this world; their life is a loss, because they gained nothing from it, so they did not believe in Allah and His messengers.

As for the saying of the author, may Allah have mercy on him: (by their being abiding in the Fire and their not reaching the maidens prepared for them in Paradise, had they believed), there is an evident problem with this. What is meant by "their families" is their families in the world, and what is not meant is "the maidens prepared for them in the Hereafter had they believed," because this is already known from before. It is said to the deceased when he is buried in his grave: "This is your seat in Paradise, had you believed"; and it is said to the believer: "This is your seat in the Fire, had you not believed" [Reported by al-Bukhari (6569) and Ibn Hibban (3113), and the wording is his, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah]. So what is meant by "the families" here is their families in the world, who did not profit.

As for the saying of the author, may Allah have mercy on him: (and the relative pronoun is the predicate of inna). Where is the relative pronoun? ﴿Those who have lost themselves﴾: this is the relative pronoun. He drew attention to this so that one who thinks ﴿those who have lost﴾ is a qualifier of "the losers" would not suppose so.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment﴾. The commentator says: (the disbelievers ﴿in lasting punishment﴾, enduring; and this is part of the speech of Allah, blessed and exalted). That is, it is not part of the speech of those who believed. Recite the verse: ﴿And those who believed said: "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment."﴾ If we looked at the context, we would say this is the continuation of the believers' speech. But the author drew attention to the fact that this is the speech of Allah and not the speech of those who believed. The context allows both: it may be, as the commentator said, the speech of Allah, and it may be the speech of those who believed. Those who believed know that the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment from the time they are in the world, because they have read the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ).

As for His saying ﴿Unquestionably, the wrongdoers﴾: the sentence is emphasized by two emphasizers. The first: ﴿Unquestionably (ala)﴾, because (ala) here is for alerting, and alerting requires emphasis. The second emphasizer: ﴿Indeed (inna) the wrongdoers﴾, because (inna) is a particle of emphasis. ﴿In lasting punishment﴾: that is, enduring, may Allah protect us.

In these verses there are benefits:

* Among them: whomever Allah leads astray, no one can guide him, however high the rank of the one who tries to guide him; because of His saying: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guardian after Him.﴾ This great and frightening ruling is confirmed by what happened to the Prophet (ﷺ) with his uncle Abu Talib. Abu Talib was the brother of the Messenger's father, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family. He used to support the Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, protect him, and defend him. When his death approached, the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, was with him, along with two men from Quraysh. He kept presenting Islam to him, saying: "O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah, a word by which I may argue on your behalf before Allah." The two men said to him: "Do you turn away from the religion of Abd al-Muttalib?" (which was the religion of disbelief and association). The Prophet (ﷺ) repeated it to him, and they repeated it, and the last thing he said was: "He is upon the religion of Abd al-Muttalib" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1360) and Muslim (24/39), from the hadith of al-Musayyab ibn Hazn]. We ask Allah for well-being and safety. Despite his love for the Messenger (ﷺ) and his testimony to his prophethood, he did not submit and did not accept. So the last of his life was his saying: "upon the religion of Abd al-Muttalib." He died upon association. Allah the Exalted permitted His Messenger (ﷺ) to intercede for him to lighten the punishment for him, so he interceded for him, and he was in a shallow part of the Fire, and upon him were two sandals of fire, from which his brain boils [Reported by Muslim (212/362), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas]. May Allah protect us. His brain is the highest part of his body, and the sandals are at the lowest part; if the highest is boiling, what is below it is more and more intense. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And had it not been for me, he would have been in the lowest level of the Fire" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3883) and Muslim (209/357), from the hadith of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib]. Had it not been that I interceded, or had it not been for my message, which Abu Talib defended? The apparent meaning is both together, because Allah thanked him, rather because Allah the Exalted permitted His Messenger (ﷺ) to intercede for him, in return for what he offered to Islam in support.

From this it is derived that whoever supports Islam, even if he is a disbeliever, has merit, because Islam is a religion of justice, giving every rightful person his right. For example, if disbelievers help Muslims with sincere help, and we know they have no greed in that, and the Muslims benefit from this support, then we must acknowledge their merit in this matter. Why? Because they have done a kindness to us, and because the Islamic religion is a religion of justice that does not wrong anyone of his right. As for the saying of some people: "We will not acknowledge their merit because they are disbelievers," their disbelief is between them and Allah, and their favor upon us is a right which we must acknowledge.

Let me give an example in the case of Kosovo. In the Kosovo case, what happened is something many of you have heard. Who supported them? The disbelievers supported them. The Atlantic Alliance placed all the equipment it had with which it could fight, and defended them. We did not hear of any Muslim sending a plane or a shell. Perhaps there is an excuse for them, while you blame them; but our denying this merit is an error. We say: these people have merit, and their disbelief is between them and Allah, and we do not love them for their disbelief at all. Rather we thank them for their favor, even though we hate them with the utmost hatred because they are enemies of Allah and His Messenger. This is if we know the intention is sincere. But if we know with certainty that it is deception and trickery, then here we blame them for what they did, and we do not praise them, nor acknowledge merit to them; because the ruling revolves around its cause, existence and non-existence.

I return to the benefits. He says:

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever Allah guides has indeed been taken as a guardian by Him; because when He negated guardianship from the wrongdoers, it is established for the believers. This was made explicit in His saying: ﴿Allah is the Guardian of those who believe; He brings them out from darknesses into light. And those who disbelieve, their guardians are the taghut; they bring them out from the light into darknesses. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾ [Al-Baqarah 257].

* And among the benefits of this verse: a person should constantly insist before Allah that He guide him from misguidance; because if the matter of misleading is returned to Allah, then to whom do we turn? To whom? To Allah the Mighty and Majestic. As long as misguidance and guidance are in the hand of Allah, let us return to Him.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the grief and humiliation of the wrongdoers when they see the punishment; because of His saying: ﴿And you see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying: "Is there any way of return?"﴾. Their grief is in their saying: ﴿Is there any way of return?﴾, because this is a wish.

* And among the benefits of the following noble verse: these wrongdoers are exposed to the Fire in the most complete humiliation and the most disgraceful condition: ﴿humbled﴾, that is, debased and fearful of humiliation.

* And among the benefits of this verse: that those arrogant toward the truth and stubborn will be requited with a punishment that matches their disobedience. What is the basis of this?

* Student: Allah, glorified and exalted, when they were arrogant toward the truth, made them humbled before the Fire.

* The Shaykh: The basis of this: they are exposed to the Fire humbled and abased. It is known that punishment by abasement matches disobedience through arrogance.

* And among the benefits of this verse: the wrongdoers are overtaken by humiliation, outwardly and inwardly. The inward is in His saying: ﴿humbled from abasement﴾, and the outward in His saying: ﴿they look with a furtive glance﴾.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the speaking of those who believed about the blessings of Allah the Mighty and Majestic; because of His saying: ﴿And those who believed said: "Indeed, the losers"﴾; it is as if they are praising Allah for having gained both their worldly life and their Hereafter.

* And among the benefits of the verse: that the disobedient has lost himself, and the loss is according to the measure of his disobedience; because he gained nothing from his existence in this world.

From this it follows that a person should take account of himself and look at what he has done. If he sees that he has filled his time with the intended good and the means to it, let him praise Allah; and if he sees that he has wasted it, let him seek to make amends. This is derived from His saying: ﴿Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves﴾.

Let us give an example of this: a man stood to pray and recite the Qur'an for an hour, and another spent that hour playing. Who is the winner? The first is the winner, because he filled that time with worship; the second is a loser, lost. Some scholars even said: it is forbidden for him not to occupy his time with obedience, because he is like one who has wealth and did not spend it in the way of Allah. But the correct view is that if he does not fill it with disobedience, then it is neither for him nor against him; yet he is considered a loser in comparison with the one who occupied himself with obedience to Allah. And you, reflect on this when you stand to pray: say to yourself, "My life is this time that I have spent in obedience to Allah." Train yourself in this, so that you are eager to fill your time with obedience to Allah.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: the punishment of the disbelievers is lasting; because of His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment﴾.

* And among its benefits: the emphasis of this punishment, lest someone say: the punishment may come to an end.

He said: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guardian after Him.﴾ (Man) is a conditional particle, and the verb is jussive (majzum) by it. Jussive by what?

* Student: By (man).

* The Shaykh: Yes, the verb of the condition (fi'l al-shart).

* Student: The verb of the condition; its sign of jussive is sukun, and it is vowelled (...) to avoid two consecutive sukuns.

* The Shaykh: Its sign of jussive is sukun, and it is vowelled with kasra to avoid two consecutive sukuns.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: (...) Good. Why is the response (jawab) joined with the fa'? Because it is what?

* Student: Joined with (ma).

* The Shaykh: Well done, joined with (ma). Did Allah inform us?

* Student: Allah the Mighty and Majestic informed us that the disbelievers ﴿are pushed﴾ [At-Tur 13], meaning they are thrust into it.

* The Shaykh: ﴿They are pushed forcefully into the fire of Hell﴾ [At-Tur 13].

* Student: They are thrust into it, pushed. How do we reconcile: ﴿And you see them being exposed to it﴾? What is this exposure?

* The Shaykh: They are exposed to it before they enter it.

* Student: That is, on the Sirat, or how?

* The Shaykh: Allah knows best. They are exposed to it before they enter it, and the disbelievers do not try to climb the Sirat, because they are turned toward Hell in the plains of the Resurrection.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 42, verse 46:

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they will have no protectors to help them against Allah﴾ [Ash-Shura 46] (i.e., no one other than Him will repel His punishment from them). ﴿And they will have no﴾ meaning: for the wrongdoers, ﴿protectors﴾, the (min) [in "min awliya'"] is grammatically extra (ziyadah), and it is for emphasis. ﴿Protectors who would help them﴾ means: they have no one who would take charge of them and help them against Allah, i.e., against His punishment. The (dun) [in "min dunillah"] here means (ghayr) [other than], as the author, may Allah have mercy on him, explained it. This is because no one can ever repel the punishment of Allah from one whom Allah wishes to punish, nor can anyone give them victory over it. In this world, if a wrongdoer wishes to wrong someone, it is possible to repel him, but no one can repel the punishment of Allah.

He said: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no way﴾. ﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray﴾ is a conditional sentence, and as mentioned before, its answer is joined with the fa' (fa') because (ma) is attached to it. ﴿For him there is no way﴾ means: no way (path) to the truth in this world or to Paradise in the Hereafter. Rather, he will be blind, and we seek refuge in Allah. He has no path to the truth. For this reason, you find that those whom Allah has decreed to be led astray are presented with the truth as clear as the sun at midday, yet they do not understand it; a barrier has been placed between them and it. Listen to the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says: "Tales of the ancients"﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 13]. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered over their hearts﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 14]. Sins have made him see the truth as falsehood and falsehood as truth. The verses of Allah, such as the Qur'an or the Torah before it was abrogated, are recited to him, yet he says: "These are tales of the ancients." A barrier has been placed between him and understanding them. Therefore, whenever you find your heart at peace with the Qur'an, loving it and reflecting upon it, know that it has been purified from sins, and whenever you find the opposite, purify your heart.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: no one can help the wrongdoers apart from Allah, because they deserve punishment, and there is no preventer of what Allah gives and no giver of what He withholds.

* Also among the benefits of this noble verse: leading astray is in the hand of Allah, and whoever Allah leads astray can never return to the truth, based on His saying: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no way﴾ [Ash-Shura 46].

* Also among its benefits: a person must always turn to Allah and ask Allah for guidance. Here is the Prophet (ﷺ) asking his Lord to guide him. At the beginning of his night prayer he would supplicate with the well-known opening supplication: "O Allah, Lord of Jibril, Mikail and Israfil, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differ. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth concerning which they differed, for You guide whom You will to a straight path."[[Narrated by Muslim (770/200) from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]] Look, he says: "Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth concerning which they differed." So how about us?

The main point is that it is taken from the verse that a person should turn, in seeking guidance, to Allah the Exalted alone, and ask Him to protect him from misguidance.

* Student: (...) We mention some verses when there is a descriptive qualifier (sifah kashifah); we say it indicates causation (...)?

* The Shaykh: This descriptive qualifier means that it is like a causal explanation for what preceded it, and also it has no implicit restrictive meaning (mafhum), and this is the important point.

* Student: Acknowledging the merit of the disbelievers in some aspects. The orientalists did some things from (...) and although (...).

* The Shaykh: No. The orientalists, you see what they are doing (...). The orientalist travels the earth to look, think and assess, and his intention is evil. As for the workers, they are fine; they seek wealth by any means.

* Student: (...) the verse is not.

* The Shaykh: How?

* The Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No. ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest levels of the Fire﴾ [An-Nisa 145] does not indicate that others will not be in it. If you say, for example: "So-and-so is in the house of so-and-so," does that preclude anyone else being in that house? No, it does not preclude it.

* Student: May Allah reward you well. The saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "If only I had..." [in "lawla ana"]: and the prohibition mentioned regarding (law)?

* The Shaykh: The prohibition mentioned regarding (law), where is it?

* The Student: Yes indeed, when a person says "law," (law) is from the work of Shaytan.

* The Shaykh: This is (lawla) (...).

* The Student: Is it permissible for a person to say: "Lawla ana"?

* The Shaykh: (...) say: what is the reconciliation between this hadith and the prohibition of (law)? Withdraw the question, and God willing the answer will come.

* The Student: We have withdrawn it.

* The Shaykh: You withdrew it? I say: attributing a thing to its cause is permissible if it is a valid cause. For example, if a man fell into the sea and another came and rescued him, it is permissible to say: "Had it not been for so-and-so, I would have drowned," because he attributed it to a known cause. But if he says: "Had it not been for so-and-so, who is buried in his grave..." Is this a known cause? A person drowned in water and said: "By Allah, had it not been for the saint so-and-so, my master, I would have drowned." Is this correct or not? It is not correct; it is shirk. In sum, take this principle: attributing a thing to its known cause is permissible, but it may not be joined with Allah by the particle waw. If it is joined with Allah by waw, it becomes forbidden. For example, saying: "Had it not been for Allah and so-and-so, I would have drowned," this is not permissible. We will mention the forms to you. If he says: "Had it not been for Allah, who sent so-and-so to me, I would have drowned," what do you say?

* The Student: This is correct.

* The Shaykh: This is correct, and it is the highest type, because he mentioned both the causer and the cause. If he says: "Had it not been for so-and-so, I would have drowned," this is permissible, because he attributed it to a valid known cause. If he says: "Had it not been for Allah and so-and-so, I would have drowned," this is not permissible, because he equated Allah with another by a particle that implies equality. If he says: "Had it not been for Allah, then so-and-so, I would have drowned," is it permissible or not? It is permissible. How many forms are there? Four. If he says: "Had it not been for Allah, so so-and-so (fa), I would have drowned," then "fa" is like "waw." What do you all say? Is "fa" like "waw"? "Fa" indicates sequence, but in reality it occupies a position between two positions. It is not like "thumma," because "thumma" indicates sequence with delay, and it is not like "waw," because "waw" indicates equality. So it occupies a position between the two positions. Do we say it is like "thumma" because it indicates sequence, or that it is like "waw" because its sequence implies immediacy? The first is correct. That is, "Lawla Allah fa-fulan," because you placed so-and-so after Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Whether it is delayed or immediate is another matter. May Allah bless you.

* Student: Shaykh, this presents us with a difficulty on this issue: what is transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to say that the saying of one who says, "Had it not been for the captain, the ship would have sunk," he considered this to be minor shirk. What is its meaning, Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: Its meaning has two aspects. First: the narration was transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim and requires verification. Second: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, perhaps at a time when people were close to shirk, wished to be strict on this matter so that people would refrain from it. The saying of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, "Lawla ana" [Had it not been for me] is clear: he attributed the thing to its cause without joining it with the will of Allah (...).

Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Respond to your Lord﴾ [al-Shura 42:47]. Istajaba means ajaba (to respond). For this reason the mufassir said: (Respond to Him with tawhid and worship). Tawhid is the opposite of shirk, and worship is the opposite of arrogance. It is obligatory upon every Muslim to respond to Allah, blessed and exalted, with faith in Him, affirming His oneness, and obedience to Him. (﴿Before there comes a Day﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿from which there is no turning back by Allah﴾, meaning that once it comes, it cannot be turned back.) ﴿From which there is no turning back by Allah﴾ means: no one can turn it back or prevent it. It was also said: ﴿from which there is no turning back by Allah﴾ means that Allah, glorified and exalted, does not turn it back once it comes. Both meanings are correct. When Allah, blessed and exalted, brings it, He has decreed it, so it cannot be turned back, and likewise no one can turn it back apart from Allah. No one can prevent it from Allah, mighty and majestic. For this reason, if anyone were to try to turn back the Day of Resurrection, he would not be able to.

(﴿There is no turning back from Allah for it. You will have no refuge on that Day, nor will you have any denial﴾: refuge which you can flee to, ﴿nor will you have any denial﴾: denial of your sins.) ﴿You will have no refuge﴾ is a nominal sentence in which the predicate is placed before the subject, and the additional (min) is inserted before the subject for emphasis. The meaning is: you will have no refuge at all apart from Allah, mighty and majestic. Al-malja' means the place of return or the shelter to which a person flees from what has befallen him.

As for His saying ﴿on that Day﴾, meaning: on that day, when it comes, ﴿nor will you have any denial﴾. He said: (denial of your sins). It seems that he explained nakīr as a verbal noun, meaning denial (inkār). If what he explained is correct, then ﴿nor will you have any denial﴾ raises a difficulty with the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [al-An'am 6:23]. This is a denial. So according to the author's explanation, "you will have no denial of your sins," it needs to be reconciled with this verse. The answer is to say: the reconciliation between them is that they will deny at first, saying, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists" [al-An'am 6:23], thinking that if they do so they will be saved as the people of tawhid were saved. Then their tongues, hands and feet will bear witness against them concerning what they used to earn, and at that point they will confess and acknowledge. So the denial comes first and the acknowledgment second. The verse, "nor will you have any denial" [al-Shura 42:47], then means, with regard to the outcome: you will not be able to deny.

It was also said that nakīr means munkir, like samī' meaning musmi', and the meaning is: no one will deny what has befallen you or repel it from you. This meaning is more correct and better suited to the context of the verse: you will have no refuge and no denier, meaning there is no refuge you can flee to, and no one who will defend you and deny what has befallen you.

﴿You will have no refuge on that Day, nor will you have any denial﴾ [al-Shura 42:47].

In this verse there are benefits:

* Among them: the obligation to respond to Allah, exalted, immediately; by His saying: ﴿Respond to your Lord before there comes﴾ this Day with which Allah threatens. Is there a fixed time in a person's life, such that he can delay repentance and seeking to make amends?

The answer: No, because a person does not know when death will overtake him, and when death overtakes him, every deed ends, as was established from the Prophet ﷺ: "When a person dies, his deeds come to an end" [narrated by Muslim (1631/14) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. So there is no difference between the coming of the Greater Hour and a person's death in terms of the cessation of deeds.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the mercy of Allah, blessed and exalted, toward His servants, in that He warns them of His punishment before it befalls them. There is no doubt that this is from His mercy and compassion toward them; otherwise He would leave them to do what they wish until punishment descends upon them.

* Among the benefits of this verse: there is no refuge on the Day of Resurrection from Allah, mighty and majestic. In this world a person may take refuge with one who holds authority and seek protection from him, but in the Hereafter, no.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: no one will deny what befalls the people of punishment of the punishment; by His saying:

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, no one will deny the punishment that befalls them.

* Student: ﴿You will have no refuge﴾.

* The Shaykh: Yes.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 42, verse 48 (part 1 of 2):

Then the Exalted said, consoling the Prophet (ﷺ): (﴿But if they turn away﴾ [al-Shura 48] from responding), and they do not respond, then there is no blame on you (﴿We have not sent you as a watcher over them﴾, guarding their deeds by making sure they do what is demanded of them). The answer, the answer to the condition, is ﴿We have not sent you as a watcher over them﴾. The meaning: if they turn away, there is no blame on you, because We did not send you as a watcher over their deeds or as one who controls them. You were sent only to deliver the message, and that has been accomplished. ﴿We have not sent you as a watcher over them. In﴾ (mā). How is ﴿in﴾ (mā)? He wanted to explain ﴿in﴾ as meaning (mā). The particle (in) comes as a negative, as here; it comes as a redundant particle; it comes as a conditional; and it comes as a lightened form of the heavy (inna).

Here it comes as a negative. The usual case is that it is a negative when it is followed by an affirmative, as in: ﴿You are only a warner﴾ [Fatir 23], ﴿I am only a warner and a bringer of good news﴾ [al-A'raf 188], and similar examples. In these it is a negative meaning (mā).

It comes as a conditional, as in: ﴿Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾ [al-Baqarah 284].

And it comes as redundant, as in the words of the poet:

Banu Ghudana, you are not gold, ∗∗∗ nor refined silver, but you are pottery.

This (in) is redundant, because if it were removed the sentence would still stand. If one said, "Banu Ghudana, you are not gold," the sentence would be sound, so it is redundant.

And it comes as a lightened form of the heavy (inna), meaning that it is the same as (inna) but lightened. In this case its noun is an omitted pronoun of the matter, and the sentence after it is its predicate. These are four meanings of (in).

﴿In﴾ (mā), that is, with the meaning of (mā): ﴿upon you is only the delivering﴾, meaning: upon you is only the delivery. Has he delivered it or not? He delivered the clear message, and he exerted great effort in that and suffered great harm for it, yet he was patient and sought reward, because the Prophet (ﷺ) knew that whatever befell him for the sake of Allah was good and an elevation. He strove for Allah with the striving due to Him and delivered the message to its utmost, and he was harmed for it, but he was patient. He used to say:

"Are you anything but a finger that has bled, ∗∗∗ and what you have suffered in the way of Allah?"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2802) and Muslim (1796/112), from the hadith of Jundub ibn Sufyan.]]

The mufassir said: (This was before the command to fight). So according to the author's statement, the verse is abrogated. The author and others like him, whenever they come to a verse like this, say: this is abrogated. This is a mistake, because abrogation (naskh) is not a light matter. Claiming abrogation means that the abrogated ruling is void and removed, and it is difficult to lift the ruling of a verse or a hadith merely because of a notion one has imagined. Therefore it is not permissible for a person to take this shameful course, that when he cannot reconcile verses he goes off saying: they are abrogated. Abrogation requires knowledge that the abrogating text came later, and it also requires that reconciling them is impossible. If reconciliation is possible, there is no abrogation. Is His saying ﴿upon you is only the delivering﴾ abrogated? Never! Until the last breath of the life of the Prophet (ﷺ), upon him was the delivering, so it was not abrogated. Delivering the message does not contradict having striving alongside it. But it is part of the wisdom of Allah, the Exalted, that He did not prescribe fighting until the Islamic community became strong. Fighting was not prescribed in Makkah; it was prescribed in Madinah, when the Islamic community had become an independent state able to fight. This is part of the wisdom, and it is described as being part of gradualness in legislation (tadarruj fi al-tashri') and of the wisdom in legislation.

So we say: the statement of the author, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, "that this was before the command to fight," is a grave error. We say: delivering is obligatory upon him even after the command to fight, and the two do not conflict. Delivering does not conflict with his being commanded to strive.

﴿Upon you is only the delivering. And when We let man taste mercy from Us﴾ (a blessing such as wealth and health) ﴿he rejoices in it. And if an evil befalls them﴾ the pronoun refers to man in terms of the species ﴿for what their hands have sent forth﴾ (a calamity), that is, what they have sent forth. He mentioned hands because most actions are performed by them ﴿then indeed man is ungrateful﴾ for blessings.

﴿And when We let [them] taste﴾. It is known that Allah, the Exalted, is one, so why does He say ﴿We﴾? We say: it is for exalting, to show greatness, authority, and the strength of dominion. ﴿When We let man taste mercy from Us﴾ [al-Shura 48], meaning: We cause it to reach him, until it is as if it were food that he tastes and has no doubt about. His saying ﴿from Us﴾ is because every blessing is from Us, and so it is from Allah, as the Exalted said: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah﴾ [al-Nahl 53].

﴿Mercy from Us﴾: he says (a blessing, such as wealth and health). The example here does not mean limitation; it is only an example. Wealth is a blessing, health is a blessing, children are a blessing, security is a blessing. The blessings of Allah cannot be counted, as the Exalted said: ﴿If you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, mankind is a wrongdoer and ungrateful﴾ [Ibrahim 34]. So what the author mentioned is by way of illustration, and illustration does not give limitation.

His saying ﴿he rejoices in it﴾ is meant as the joy of arrogance and insolence, not joy at a blessing while believing that it is from Allah. That is commanded: that a person rejoice in the blessings of Allah. In the hadith: "When Allah bestows a blessing upon His servant, He loves to see the effect of His blessing upon him."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2819), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr.]] Among the effects of a blessing is joy. When Allah grants a person wealth, he rejoices; when Allah heals him after illness, he rejoices; when he marries, he rejoices; when a child is born to him, he rejoices. But joy is of two kinds: the joy of insolence and arrogance, which is blameworthy, and joy in the blessing of Allah while adhering to His law, which is praiseworthy and permissible.

A person should not be like a donkey that does not rejoice in a blessing and does not grieve over a calamity. Rather, a person must be someone who is affected by events, rejoicing where rejoicing is due and grieving where grief is due.

﴿He rejoices in it. And if an evil befalls them﴾. The author says: (the pronoun refers to man in terms of the species), removing with that a difficulty. The difficulty is: the verse says ﴿And when We let man taste﴾, and "man" is singular or plural?

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Singular. How then does it say ﴿befalls them﴾, returning the pronoun to him in the plural?
* Student: The intended meaning of "man" is the species.
* Shaykh: Yes. The author answered it by saying that what is meant by "man" is the species, so it includes every human being, and it is correct to say ﴿And if an evil befalls them﴾, the opposite of mercy. For this reason the author explained it as a trial (bala').
﴿For what their hands have sent forth﴾, that is, for what they have sent forth of what? Of sins. He mentioned the hands because most actions are performed by them. If you think about it, which does more work, the hands or the feet?

* Students: The hands.
* Shaykh: Consider this, everyone. Now, how many steps is your walk from your house to the mosque? How many movements?
* Students: (...).
* Shaykh: And the feet do not move? If the feet did not move, would you walk? It is said that the movement of the feet is of one kind, which is walking. But the movements of the hands are so many in their types, let alone their instances. Actions are truly performed by the hand, because it is more engaged in actions than any other organ of the body. Even if someone said: the tongue is more than the hand; who can count the words of the tongue? We answer this as we answered about walking: they are of one kind. But the hand strikes, hits, writes, erases; its kinds cannot be counted. So for this reason he expressed the self by the hands.

From this is His saying: ﴿Have they not seen that We created for them from what Our hands have made, cattle, and they are their owners?﴾ [Ya-Sin 71]. Pay attention to this: ﴿from what Our hands have made﴾. What is meant? Answer me. What is meant is "from what We have made." But the Arabic language is broad and expresses the self by the hands. From this we know that there is no equality between the creation of Adam by the Hand of Allah and the working of the hands of Allah, glory be to Him, in camels and the like.

He said: ﴿Then indeed man is ungrateful﴾. Notice that he returned to the singular after the plural. ﴿When We let man taste﴾ he began with the singular, and ﴿Then indeed man﴾ he ended with the singular, so that "man" includes the human being whether gathered or individual. This is one state. But who is meant by "man" here? The apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is the disbeliever, because he is the one to whom the joy of insolence and arrogance applies, and ingratitude when he is struck by harm.

In this verse there are benefits:

* Among them: consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ) when they turned away from answering him, as indicated by His saying ﴿We have not sent you as a watcher over them﴾.
* And among the benefits of the verse: it is a consolation for those who call to Allah after the Messenger (ﷺ). The caller's duty is delivering; it is not his duty to guide people, and he cannot do that. If the Prophet (ﷺ) told us that he saw a prophet with no one with him [[Narrated by Ahmad (15), from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.]], how can we become angry when we call to Allah and no one responds to us? If prophets, who are prophets, were not responded to, how about us?

For this reason we see some callers, when they find no one to respond, become weary and abandon the call. This is a mistake. It is never permissible for you to despair of the mercy of Allah. Call, then call, then call, even if you are harmed instead of being answered, and do not despair.

So in this verse there is consolation for whom? For those calling to Allah, the Exalted. And there is also consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ). You are only obligated to deliver, and how noble it is to fulfill what is upon you of delivering. As for whether people will be guided, that is not in your hands. This is one point.

Second: some people want people to be guided overnight. This is a mistake. It is not possible, and it goes against the sunnah of Allah, the Exalted. The Prophet (ﷺ) remained in Makkah for thirteen years calling to Allah, to monotheism only, and at the end to prayer, and yet most of them did not respond; most of their notables did not respond. Until they forced him to migrate and leave his homeland. So how about you, living among a people whom military, intellectual, and moral colonialism has corrupted, wanting them to be guided overnight? Who are you to want something contrary to the sunnah of Allah, the Exalted? Be patient and proceed gradually. In my view there is no harm in dealing with people gradually, so long as the aim is reform. Be patient with some sins and let people become accustomed to giving them up gradually. For example, if a man warned people against smoking tobacco, from which many people are afflicted, and the smoker said: "I cannot," he might say: "There is no objection; drink ten a day for a week, then eight for a week, until it dwindles to nothing." Is this permissible or not? It is permissible, because I have not now approved of him smoking; I have approved of some of the harm in order to reach the complete removal of the harm. This is part of the treatment and of calling with wisdom. Just as this applies to spiritual and religious diseases, it also applies to physical diseases. The doctor treats the patient little by little and is patient with the illness little by little. He does not give the full medicine in one moment, as the Bedouin did when they gave him Novalgin and said: "Take this every six hours, one tablet." He found the matter slow and said: "I want to make it every six hours, one tablet!" He swallowed them all, so he was finished off. He hastened the matter and perished. Be patient, treat the thing in the best way. The important thing is that you are determined to remove this.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) is not a watcher over the community, neither in his lifetime nor after his death. On this basis, he is not to be sought for help after his death, and guidance is not to be requested from him; guidance is from Allah, the Exalted.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of delivering. Allah did not specify the means of delivering, so we say: every means of delivering is obligatory, and means have the rulings of the ends. In the past, delivering was limited: a person delivered to the people of his town and those who came to it. Now he can deliver to the whole world. So then we ask: if a person is able to create a page on the internet, is it permissible for him to do so?

* Students: It is permissible.
* Shaykh: Permissible? The internet contains songs, and there are calamities in it (...).
* Student: No, it is no concern of his.
* Shaykh: No, it is no concern of his?
* Student: He spreads goodness through it.
* Shaykh: Alright, what if there is a song before it and a song after it?
* Student: The actions of another do not harm him.
* Shaykh: The actions of another do not harm him. Amazing. If the one before him opens with songs and closes with songs?
* Student: He does not have that...
* Shaykh: He does not have that? So he does not deliver?
* Student: No, he delivers.
* Shaykh: He delivers even if there is a song before him and a song after him? What do you say about that? It is correct, because the song before and after is not his action. It is the action of the one who operates this station. But it is not permissible for us to abandon calling to the truth because in this broadcast, for example, or this station, there is some evil. That is incorrect and a deficient theory. Contend with the people of falsehood until the truth becomes clear, and it does not harm you if they introduce some objectionable things into it.

Some people, for example, say to us or to others: do not go on the internet, do not enter it. How can you enter it when there are songs in it and calamities? Is it not better that we enter this arena, perhaps Allah will guide one person through us, or that we leave the field to the people of evil?

* Students: The first.
* Shaykh: The first, without doubt. The first is better.

The same applies to what is said about elections. If the country is built on elections, some people say: do not vote. Everyone, should I not nominate one of the people of goodness? He says: No, because elections involve calamity, there are bribes, there are personal desires. If there are bribes and desires, I will not enter into bribes and desires, but I will enter into nominating a man whom I know to have goodness. They say: if you nominate one, a hundred wicked people will come. Alright, if the hundred wicked people have none upright among them, or if the hundred wicked people include one upright person? The second is better. And if they say: this is useless and does not benefit, one in a hundred is of no use, we say: it must have some benefit. If one sincerely intends it for Allah, it must have an effect, because the word is not effective because so-and-so spoke it, but it is effective because it is the word of Allah.

Listen to the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest﴾, and after it? And the word of Allah ﴿is the highest﴾ [al-Tawbah 40]. Is it ﴿and the word of Allah﴾? It is in the nominative, because if he had said "and the word of Allah" in the accusative it would have entered as the object: "and He made the word of Allah." The word of Allah is the highest, by His making and without His making. So it is now clear that His saying ﴿and the word of Allah is the highest﴾ has a very great position, meaning that the word of Allah is the highest no matter what comes.

Nor is it hidden from you what is repeated in the story of Musa with the magicians and Pharaoh. When they gathered, and Musa was confident of the victory of Allah, the Exalted, when they said: "Set for us an appointment," did he set for them an appointment in the middle of the night in a dark room? No. When? In broad daylight, on the day of the festival, the day of adornment: ﴿He said, "Your appointment is the day of adornment, and let the people be assembled in the morning"﴾ [Ta-Ha 59]. A wonderful thing: the magicians came, and Pharaoh gathered his cunning: ﴿So put together your plot, then come in a row, and he has succeeded today who prevails﴾ [Ta-Ha 64]. Then Musa said one word. He said: ﴿Woe to you!﴾ Finish it.

* Student: ﴿Do not invent against Allah a lie, lest He destroy you with a punishment﴾ [Ta-Ha 61].

**Shaykh:** "Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you with a punishment. Indeed, he who invents has failed" [Ta-Ha 61]. What happened as a result of this statement? "So they disputed their affair among themselves" [Ta-Ha 62]. Immediately. The *fa'* (ف) indicates sequence, immediacy, and causation: "So they disputed their affair among themselves." When people dispute, do not ask about the failure. Speak as you wish, and there is no blame: "They disputed their affair among themselves, and they failed" [Ta-Ha 62]. In the end, these sorcerers who came to scheme against Musa (Moses) joined Musa. They were threatened with death and crucifixion, but they refused.
